
# PHASE 001:

## Phase 001 — Create the ids-000-aa crate (master crate / single control point): Research Findings & Implementation Blueprint

**Research complete (30 targeted searches executed). No code written, no files created, no repository changes made. This document is the blueprint for implementation.**

---

### 1. Executive Summary

Phase 001 creates `ids-000-aa`, the master crate and single control point for the entire IDS workspace. It hosts every canonical type (`NodeId`, `RegionId`, `HUnitId`, `DatasetId`, `PartitionId`, `RecordId`, `OpRef`, `OrderingPos`, `Endpoint`, `CarrierType`, `OpState`, `CommitState`, `PlacementDecision`, `RedundancyMode`, `ConsistencyProfile`, `FailureDomain`, plus dozens of additional types referenced by contracts and invariants), all sealed trait contracts (starting with `trait Carrier` — send/receive opaque datagrams via `CarrierType + Vec<u8>`, no IP/TCP/UDP), protocol invariants, version bits, and the unified error contract. Every downstream `ids-*` crate imports these as `ids_000_aa::X` and depends on `ids-000-aa` only. Adding one edge case = edit exactly one file here, then implement in one dependent crate at a time. Carrier-agnostic absolute rule: no `std::net`, `tokio::net`, libp2p, IP, TCP, UDP, QUIC, HTTP, DNS, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular, VPN, or conventional mesh. All traffic rides `ids-carrier::Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>`). Allowed crypto only: ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305 (crypto itself lives in `ids-crypto`; this crate declares only the type-level crypto surface — `Signature`, `KeyId`, `AuthToken`, `Credential`, `Checksum`).

Research basis: 30 parallel searches returned the Shapiro et al. 2011 CRDT paper (INRIA RR-7687), the delta-CRDT paper (Almeida/Shoker/Baquero, arXiv:1603.01529), the Rust sealed-trait pattern (rust-lang API guidelines C-SEALED), thiserror library design guidance, NIST FIPS 180-4 (SHA-256), RFC 8032 (Ed25519), RFC 7539 (ChaCha20-Poly1305), libsodium XChaCha20-Poly1305 construction, quorum intersection theory (r + w > n), CRDT convergence proofs (CvRDT vs CmRDT, causal stability for tombstone GC), idempotency-key exactly-once semantics, vector clock vs hybrid logical clock ordering, durability acknowledgement levels, replication-vs-erasure-coding tradeoffs, consistency profiles (strong/causal/bounded staleness/eventual/read-your-writes), failure-domain correlated-failure modeling, hybrid redundancy (replica + erasure), workspace/monorepo patterns for Cargo, and serde newtype identifier patterns.

A skeleton `ids-000-aa` crate already exists at `C:/idfs/ids-000-aa/` with `src/types.rs` (all canonical types), `src/lib.rs` (module declarations + root re-exports), `src/contracts/mod.rs` + 30 contract modules (carrier, transport, store, session, routing, discovery, membership, placement, replication, recovery, consistency, ordering, security, client, fault, broadcast, quorum, snapshot, byzantine, lease, crdt, erasure, saga, coordinator, durability, topology, integration, protocol, wire, framing, sequencing, acks), `src/invariants/mod.rs` + ~40 invariant modules, `src/errors.rs`, `src/versioning.rs`, and `Cargo.toml` (thiserror, serde, blake3). Phase 001 research validates this skeleton and specifies the plan to complete/align it; no source modifications are made in this phase.

---

### 2. Architecture Overview

`ids-000-aa` is layer 0 of the IDS dependency stack. Every other `ids-*` crate depends on it and nothing else cross-crate at the type level. It is a pure data + contract crate: no `std::net`, `tokio::net`, or carrier implementation; all I/O is abstracted behind `trait Carrier` and `Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>`).

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   DOWNSTREAM ids-* CRATES                   │
│  ids-carrier · ids-crypto · ids-identity · ids-time · …     │
│  (each depends on ids-000-aa only)                          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│              Phase 001: ids-000-aa (THIS CRATE)             │
│  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐        │
│  │  types   │ │ contracts│ │ invariants│ │ versioning│       │
│  │ (all IDs │ │ 20+ sealed│ │ protocol  │ │ Protocol │       │
│  │  newtypes│ │ traits   │ │ invariants│ │ Version, │       │
│  │  + Enums)│ │ Carrier  │ │ ~40 rules │ │ EdgeCaseBits│      │
│  └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘        │
│  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐        │
│  │   errors │ │   codec  │ │   state  │ │   prelude │       │
│  │ unified  │ │ frame/   │ │ state    │ │ re-exports │       │
│  │ Error    │ │ datagram │ │ machines │ │           │        │
│  └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘        │
│  ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐ ┌──────────┐        │
│  │  internals│ │ recovery │ │ placement│ │ routing   │       │
│  │ type reg │ │ etc.     │ │ etc.     │ │ etc.      │        │
│  └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│             CARRIER BOUNDARY (no std::net / tokio::net)      │
│  ids-carrier::Endpoint = CarrierType + Vec<u8>               │
│  trait Carrier: send_datagram(Endpoint, &[u8]) / receive     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Design rules (non-negotiable):**
- One canonical definition per type. `NodeId`, `RegionId`, etc. are defined once in `src/types.rs` and re-exported at crate root; downstream crates never redefine them.
- Sealed traits via private supertrait (`pub trait Carrier: private::Sealed`). Downstream crates can call methods and use as bounds but cannot implement. Adding a method = edit one contract file, then implement in one dependent crate at a time.
- Newtype wrapper for every identifier (`pub struct NodeId(pub [u8; 32])`) with `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize`, `ZERO` constant, `new`, `as_bytes`, `is_zero`, `to_hex`, `from_hex`, `Display`.
- `Endpoint` is the sole address type: `CarrierType` enum (Loopback, Serial, Optical, Radio, Custom(u16)) + opaque `Vec<u8>` capped at 1024 bytes. No IP, port, SocketAddr.
- Operation lifecycle: `received → ordered → executing → committed → synchronized → verified → failed` (`OpState`); commit lifecycle: `accepted → prepared → committed → aborted` (`CommitState`).
- Versioning: `ProtocolVersion` (semver) + `EdgeCaseBits` (u128 bitfield, one bit per protocol invariant) for compile-time wire-contract gating.

### 3. Detailed Research Dimensions

#### 3.1 Canonical Types — Identifier Newtypes
Each ID is a fixed-size byte array newtype (32-byte for node/region/hunit/dataset/partition/record/ordering-domain/checksum; 16-byte for rotating-node-id/session/snapshot/lease/message/transaction/fragment/key-id/auth-token; 9-byte `OpRef`; `u64` `OrderingPos`/`Version`/`Epoch`/`ChannelId`/`FencingToken`/`StepId`). All implement `Serialize`/`Deserialize` (serde), `Hash`, `Eq`, `Copy`, with `ZERO` const, `new`, `as_bytes`, `is_zero`, `to_hex`, `from_hex`, `Display`. Source: serde newtype patterns; Rust standard library conventions; existing `ids-000-aa/src/types.rs`.

#### 3.2 Sealed Trait Contracts
`trait Carrier: private::Sealed` with `send_datagram(&self, endpoint: &Endpoint, data: &[u8]) -> Result<(), CarrierError>` and `receive_datagram`. Additional sealed traits: `Transport` (frame/deframe/sequence/acknowledge/delivery semantics), `Store`, `Session`, `Routing`, `Discovery`, `Membership`, `Placement`, `Replication`, `Recovery`, `Consistency`, `Ordering`, `Security`, `Client`, `FaultTolerance`, `Broadcast`, `Quorum`, `Snapshot`, `Byzantine`, `Lease`, `CRDT`, `Erasure`, `Saga`, `Coordinator`, `Durability`, `Topology`, `Integration`, `Protocol`, `Wire`, `Framing`, `Sequencing`, `Acks`. Sealing follows the Rust API Guidelines sealed-trait pattern (private supertrait in `mod private`), confirmed by research. Downstream crates use as trait bounds but cannot implement.

#### 3.3 Protocol Invariants (~40 rules)
`BinaryCompletion`, `DeadNodeIdentity`, `IdleRotation`, `NoGlobalMaster`, `OutEqIn`, `CoordinatedDeletion`, `FencingStonith`, `QuorumIntersection`, `ErasureThreshold`, `CorrelatedFailure`, `HUnitCompensation`, `RegionalAutonomy`, `HybridRedundancy`, `OperationLifecycle`, `DurabilityAck`, `OrderedReadVisibility`, `NodeRoster`, `RegionAffinity`, `IdentityRotation`, `IdsStandardTime`, `DailyIntegrity`, `DbRetirement`, `ReadFallback`, `TopologyDiversity`, `WriteFanout`, `CustodyGraph`, `ChecksumBoundary`, `ReplicaFreshness`, `CommitPrefix`, `VersionVector`, `MembershipEpoch`, `PlacementPolicy`, `ReplicationLag`, `RecoveryScope`, `DataLifecycle`, `SnapshotConsistency`, `ComputeToData`, `HotColdTier`, `MobilityHandoff`, `FederationTrust`. Each is a compile-time/runtime constraint checked by `InvariantChecker` in `src/internals/`.

#### 3.4 Versioning
`ProtocolVersion` (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH semver) + `EdgeCaseBits` (u128 bitfield, 40 bits = one per invariant) + `VersionRange`, `SemanticVersion`, `ProtocolFeature`, `ProtocolRegistry`, `CompatibilityMatrix`, `VersionGraph` (DAG of versions with upgrade/downgrade edges), `MigrationPath`, `VersionHistory`, `VersionNegotiation`, `EdgeCaseCompiler`. Wire-contract gating: increment `PROTOCOL_VERSION` when any field changes in bincode/serde-encoded messages; incompatible binaries must reject each other before registering peers or exchanging operations. Sources: HBase compatibility matrix, Numax wire versioning, Agent Host Protocol negotiation, qcp compatibility levels.

#### 3.5 Error Contract
Single `Error` enum (thiserror) with structured context variants per domain (`InvalidNodeIdLength`, `EndpointAddressTooLarge`, `InvalidOpRefLength`, `CarrierUnavailable`, etc.), each variant carrying recovery hints, `is_retryable()`, `is_fatal()`, `category()`, `plain_message()`. Downstream crates wrap `ids_000_aa::Error` variants; cannot extend the enum (sealed by thiserror enum design). Source: thiserror docs, Rust error-type design guidance.

#### 3.6 Carrier-Agnostic Addressing
`Endpoint` = `CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>` (max 1024 bytes). `CarrierType` enum: `Loopback`, `Serial`, `Optical`, `Radio`, `Custom(u16)`. This is the ONLY address type in the workspace. No `std::net`, `tokio::net`, IP, TCP, UDP, QUIC, HTTP, DNS, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular, VPN, or mesh anywhere. All traffic via `ids-carrier::Endpoint`. Source: HX-241 carrier-agnostic socket abstraction research; IDS prompts.txt entry 1.

#### 3.7 Crypto Surface (type-level only)
Allowed crypto: ed25519 (signatures), xchacha20poly1305 (AEAD, random 192-bit nonces), sha256 (hashing), blake3 (content addressing, fast hashing), chacha20poly1305 (AEAD, 96-bit nonces). `ids-000-aa` declares type-level surface only: `Signature([u8; 64])`, `KeyId([u8; 16])`, `AuthToken([u8; 32])`, `Credential { identity: NodeId, token: Vec<u8> }`, `Checksum([u8; 32])`. Actual crypto operations live in `ids-crypto` (Phase 003). Sources: RFC 8032 (Ed25519), RFC 7539 (ChaCha20-Poly1305), libsodium XChaCha20-Poly1305, NIST FIPS 180-4 (SHA-256), BLAKE3 spec.

#### 3.8 State Machines
`OpStateMachine`, `CommitStateMachine`, `NodeStateMachine` (Candidate→Validating→Active→Degraded→Draining→Failed→Retired), `HUnitStateMachine`, `RegionStateMachine`, `SessionStateMachine`, `MembershipStateMachine`, `PlacementStateMachine`, `ReplicationStateMachine`, `RecoveryStateMachine`, `ConsistencyStateMachine`, `OrderingStateMachine`, `BroadcastStateMachine`, `QuorumStateMachine`, `SnapshotStateMachine`, `ByzantineStateMachine`, `LeaseStateMachine`, `CRDTStateMachine`, `ErasureStateMachine`, `SagaStateMachine`, `CoordinatorStateMachine`. Each encodes legal transitions; terminal states flagged.

#### 3.9 Codec Layer
`FrameHeader`, `FrameBody`, `WireFormat`, `Datagram`, per-type codecs (`EndpointCodec`, `OpRefCodec`, `OrderingPosCodec`, `NodeIdCodec`, etc.) for serde/bincode wire encoding. Version-tagged frames for forward compatibility.

#### 3.10 Internals
`TypeRegistry`, `VersionGraph`, `ContractValidator`, `InvariantChecker`, `EdgeCaseCompiler`, `OpRefAllocator`, `OrderingPositionClock`, `DurabilityTracker`, `ReplicationStreamMgr`, `SyncCheckpointMgr`, `RecoveryPlanBuilder`, `ConsistencyProfileMgr`, `BroadcastTopology`, `QuorumCalculator`, `SnapshotCoordinator`, `ByzantineVoteMgr`, `LeaseTracker`, `CRDTMergeEngine`, `ErasureCodec`, `SagaCoordinator`, `CoordinatorEpoch`.

### 4. Threat Model & Mitigations

|| Threat | Mitigation ||
||--------|-----------|-------------|
| Type duplication across crates (divergent `NodeId` definitions) | Single canonical definition in `types.rs`; downstream crates import `ids_000_aa::X`; CI lint forbids redefinition |
| Downstream crate implementing sealed trait (breaks forward-compat) | Private supertrait `private::Sealed`; compiler enforces; rustdoc documents seal |
| Carrier-agnostic rule violation (`std::net`, `tokio::net`, IP, etc.) | `Endpoint` is sole address type; dependency audit bans networking crates; clippy/CI rule |
| Disallowed crypto algorithm | Only ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305 in allowed list; `ids-crypto` enforces at implementation layer |
| Version skew / wire incompatibility | `ProtocolVersion` + `EdgeCaseBits`; `VersionNegotiation` rejects mismatched peers before operation exchange |
| Invalid identifier (wrong length, hex decode failure) | `from_hex`/`from_str` return `Result` with `Invalid*Length` variants; `MAX_ADDRESS_SIZE` cap on `Endpoint.address` |
| Error type leakage / uncontrolled enum extension | thiserror `Error` enum is the contract; downstream matches but cannot add variants; recovery hints on every variant |
| Invariant violation at runtime | `InvariantChecker` validates all 40 rules; `can_transition_to` guards state machines; `is_valid()` on `PlacementDecision` |
| Overflow in `OrderingPos`/`Version`/`Epoch` arithmetic | `saturating_add`/`saturating_sub` everywhere; `MAX` constants defined |
| `OpRef` collision (36^9 namespace) | Allocator guarantees uniqueness; collision detection variant in error contract |

### 5. Integration with Existing Crates

|| Crate | Role in Phase 001 ||
||-------|-------|-------------------|
| `ids-000-aa` (this crate) | Master crate; all canonical types, sealed contracts, invariants, versioning, errors |
| `ids-carrier` (Phase 002) | Implements `trait Carrier`; provides concrete `Endpoint` usage; depends on `ids-000-aa` |
| `ids-crypto` (Phase 003) | Implements allowed crypto; consumes `Signature`, `KeyId`, `AuthToken`, `Credential`, `Checksum` types from `ids-000-aa` |
| `ids-identity` (Phase 004) | `StableNodeId`/`RotatingNodeId` built on `NodeId`; depends on `ids-000-aa` |
| `ids-time` (Phase 005) | `Idstime` type; `IdsTime` already defined here; depends on `ids-000-aa` |
| All remaining `ids-*` crates (Phases 006–100) | Each imports canonical types + contracts from `ids-000-aa` only |

**Integration points:**
- `ids-carrier` implements `Carrier` (send/receive opaque datagrams over `Endpoint`); `ids-000-aa` declares the sealed trait but provides no implementation.
- `ids-crypto` implements signing/verification/encryption/hashing using `Signature`, `KeyId`, `AuthToken`, `Credential`, `Checksum` from `ids-000-aa`.
- `ids-time` builds its proprietary `Idstime` on top of `IdsTime` (u64 ticks) defined here.
- No dependency on `std::net`, `tokio::net`, libp2p, or any carrier-specific crate anywhere in `ids-000-aa`.
- Cargo workspace: `ids-000-aa` is a workspace member; all downstream crates declare `ids-000-aa = { path = "../ids-000-aa" }`.

### 7. Key Algorithms & Data Structures

1. **Identifier newtype construction** — `pub struct NodeId(pub [u8; 32])` with const `ZERO`, `new`, `as_bytes`, `is_zero`, `to_hex`, `from_hex` (hex parse with length validation), `Display`. Applied uniformly to all ~200 ID types.
2. **Sealed trait dispatch** — `pub trait Carrier: private::Sealed` where `private::Sealed` is unnameable downstream; compiler guarantees only `ids-000-aa` (and designated impl crates via `impl Sealed for X` inside the crate) can implement.
3. **State-machine transition guard** — `OpState::can_transition_to(next)` encodes `received → ordered → executing → committed → synchronized → verified → failed` with `Verified`/`Failed` terminal; `CommitState::is_terminal()` / `is_success()` for commit lifecycle.
4. **Failure-domain overlap check** — `FailureDomain::shares_domain(&self, other)` compares power/facility/network-segment/operator/geographic Option<[u8;16]> fields for correlated-failure detection.
5. **Redundancy failure tolerance** — `RedundancyMode::failure_tolerance()` returns `Some(n-k)` for erasure-coded, `Some(0)` for full replica/hybrid.
6. **Consistency quorum requirement** — `ConsistencyProfile::requires_quorum()` true for `Strong`/`BoundedStaleness`; `allows_fallback()` false only for `Strong`.
7. **Durability level ordering** — `DurabilityCondition::level()` (1–6) and `meets(required)` for acknowledgement gating.
8. **Endpoint validation** — `Endpoint::new()` rejects `address.len() > MAX_ADDRESS_SIZE (1024)`.
9. **OpRef parsing** — exactly 9 ASCII alphanumeric bytes; `36^9` namespace; `from_str` validates length.
10. **Ordering position arithmetic** — `OrderingPos::next()`/`prev()` with `saturating_add`/`saturating_sub`; `ZERO`/`MAX` constants.
11. **Saturating tick arithmetic** — `IdsTime::next()`/`saturating_sub()`/`elapsed_since()` for proprietary time basis (not wall-clock).
12. **Version bitfield** — `EdgeCaseBits: u128` with one bit per invariant (40 bits used); `VersionGraph` DAG for upgrade/downgrade edges; `VersionNegotiation` rejects mismatched peers.
13. **Error categorization** — `Error::is_retryable()`, `is_fatal()`, `category()`, `plain_message()`, `suggested_retry_delay_ms()` for structured recovery.
14. **Codec encode/decode** — `FrameHeader::encode()`/`decode()` (16-byte fixed header: sequence u64, flags u8, payload_length u16, checksum u32, reserved); `FramedData::encode()`/`decode()` with payload-length validation.
15. **Join-semilattice merge (CRDT surface)** — `CRDTState`/`CRDTOp`/`CRDTDelta` opaque wrappers; merge = least upper bound; referenced by `crate::crdt` contract (actual CRDT classes live in later phases).

### 11. Engineering Decisions Summary

| Decision | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|
| Single `ids-000-aa` master crate (not folders inside existing crates) | Matches user directive "try to use separate crates instead of more folders in existing ones"; enforces single control point |
| Newtype wrappers for every identifier | Prevents accidental mixing of `NodeId` and `RegionId`; zero-cost (`#[repr(transparent)]` compatible via newtype) |
| Sealed traits via private supertrait | Rust API Guidelines C-SEALED; allows adding methods non-breakingly; downstream can use as bounds but not implement |
| `Endpoint` = `CarrierType + Vec<u8>` only | Carrier-agnostic absolute rule; no IP/TCP/UDP/QUIC/HTTP/DNS or any networking stack |
| Allowed crypto: ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305 | Per IDS policy; `ids-000-aa` declares type surface only, `ids-crypto` implements |
| `thiserror` for unified `Error` enum | Structured context + recovery hints; downstream wraps but cannot extend |
| `saturating_add`/`saturating_sub` for all tick/position arithmetic | No overflow panics in distributed ordering/commit |
| `MAX_ADDRESS_SIZE = 1024` on `Endpoint.address` | Bounded memory; prevents address-based DoS |
| `OpRef` = exactly 9 bytes (36^9 namespace) | Per prompts.txt; fixed-size for wire efficiency |
| Workspace Cargo layout with path dependencies | `ids-000-aa` at `C:/idfs/ids-000-aa/`; downstream crates depend by path |

# PHASE 002:

## Phase 002 — Create the ids-carrier crate: Native carrier interface, no existing networking stack: Research Findings & Implementation Blueprint

**Research complete (30 targeted searches executed). No code written, no files created, no repository changes made. This document is the blueprint for implementation.**

---

### 1. Executive Summary

Phase 002 creates `ids-carrier`, the single carrier-agnostic transport abstraction crate for the IDS workspace. It is the only crate that owns the traffic surface: `ids-carrier::Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + opaque `Vec<u8>`), `ids-carrier::Datagram` (opaque `Vec<u8>` payload + sequence), `send_datagram(endpoint, payload)`, and `receive_datagram()`. Every one of the 99 dependent `ids-*` crates addresses peers exclusively through `ids-carrier::Endpoint`; no other crate may import `std::net`, `tokio::net`, libp2p, or any IP/TCP/UDP/QUIC/HTTP/DNS/Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/cellular/VPN/mesh stack. `ids-carrier` is datagram-native and unreliable by default: it moves opaque byte sequences from one `Endpoint` to another, never inspects payload contents, performs no cryptography (crypto boundary belongs to `ids-crypto`, limited to ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305; `ids-carrier` envelope checksums may use only BLAKE3 or SHA-256), and assumes nothing about delivery (loss, reordering, and duplication are expected and handled by layers above, chiefly `ids-protocol`).

The crate hosts the `CarrierPlugin` trait + plugin registry: every carrier (in-process, local, loopback, test, user-supplied) is a plugin behind the trait; the core imports zero sockets. Each plugin advertises a `CarrierCapabilities` set (max datagram size/MTU, ordered, reliable, duplex, fragmentation) and peers negotiate by intersection before the first send; MTU overshoot triggers length-prefixed fragmentation/reassembly inside `ids-carrier`. Carrier health is scored with a phi accrual failure detector over plugin heartbeats; unhealthy carriers are quarantined and reconnect with exponential backoff plus jitter. Addressing is carrier-agnostic: the `Vec<u8>` address bytes are opaque to `ids-carrier` and interpreted only by the plugin; there is no IP, port, DNS name, or locator anywhere.

Research basis: 30 parallel searches returned datagram transport traits with associated address types (kcp-tokio `Transport`, reconcile-gossip `Transport`, embedded-nal, `datagram::DatagramSender`), a carrier-agnostic "carriage layer = send/receive/discover over opaque bytes" model, SDP offer/answer capability negotiation (RFC 3264 model), phi accrual failure detection (Hazelcast, Akka, Cassandra), address-without-IP research (locator/identifier separation LISP/ILNP/DIME, addressless Internet draft, Netsukuku ANDNA, OpenNet ServiceID, content-addressed/IPFS key-based routing), reliable-datagram patterns (ARQ stop-and-wait/go-back-N/selective repeat, NAK-based LAMS-DLC, NORM RFC 5740), congestion-controlled unreliable datagrams (DCCP RFC 4340), backpressure flow control (NSDI'22 BFC, credit-based flow control), WebRTC data channel reliability modes and RFC 9221 QUIC DATAGRAMs (research only — QUIC is prohibited), ZeroMQ/nanomsg/NNG transport-agnostic opaque-blob sockets, Akka.Remote location-transparent remoting, PTRS/OpenCarrier Rust pluggable-transport trait patterns (Tor pluggable transports reviewed as an anti-example: obfuscation is out of scope), path MTU discovery framing rules, message framing (length-prefix vs delimiter), gRPC exponential backoff with jitter, consistent hashing/Chord coordinator-free routing, and CIRP capability-oriented routing (research only).

A skeleton `ids-carrier` crate does not yet exist; this plan specifies crate creation from scratch: `Cargo.toml` (depends on `ids-000-aa` only, plus `thiserror`/`bytes`/`serde`/`blake3`), `src/` modules below, no source modifications to any existing crate.

---

### 2. Architecture Overview

`ids-carrier` is layer 1 of the IDS dependency stack: it sits directly on top of `ids-000-aa` (which defines `Endpoint`, `CarrierType`, `trait Carrier`, and the error/invariant contracts) and below all other `ids-*` crates. It is **not** a network protocol stack — it is a plugin host that moves opaque datagrams between `Endpoint`s.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   DOWNSTREAM ids-* CRATES (2–100)                   │
│  ids-protocol · ids-discovery · ids-routing · ids-membership · …    │
│  (each addresses peers only via ids-carrier::Endpoint)              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                Phase 002: ids-carrier (THIS CRATE)                  │
│  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────────┐   │
│  │   Endpoint   │  │   Datagram   │  │   CarrierType enum      │   │
│  │ CarrierType  │  │ payload:     │  │ Loopback Serial Optical │   │
│  │ + Vec<u8> ≤  │  │ Vec<u8> +    │  │ Radio Custom(u16)       │   │
│  │   1024 bytes │  │ seq: u64     │  │ (closed; Custom = user) │   │
│  └──────┬───────┘  └──────┬───────┘  └───────────┬────────────┘   │
│         └─────────────────┴──────────────────────┘                │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │ send_datagram(endpoint, payload) -> Result<DatagramId>      │   │
│  │ receive_datagram() -> Result<Datagram, CarrierError>        │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────────┐   │
│  │ Capability   │  │ Carrier      │  │ Carrier Health (phi)    │   │
│  │ negotiation  │  │ Health       │  │ Monitor + quarantine    │   │
│  └──────┬───────┘  └──────┬───────┘  └───────────┬────────────┘   │
│         └─────────────────┴──────────────────────┘                │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │  CarrierPlugin trait — EVERY carrier is a plugin            │   │
│  │  send / recv / capabilities / health — no sockets imported  │   │
│  └──────┬──────────┬──────────┬──────────────┬───────────────┘   │
│   in_process   local   loopback   test     user (Custom u16)     │
└──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────────┴───────────────────┘
│                      CARRIER BOUNDARY                                │
│  No std::net / tokio::net / libp2p / IP / TCP / UDP / QUIC / HTTP   │
│  / DNS / Wi-Fi / Bluetooth / cellular / VPN / mesh anywhere here    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Data flow (send):** caller builds `Endpoint { carrier, address: Vec<u8> }` + payload → `ids_carrier::send_datagram` → plugin selected by `CarrierType` → capability negotiation (intersect local/peer `CarrierCapabilities`; on first contact) → framing (length-prefixed envelope + BLAKE3/SHA-256 payload digest) → MTU check → fragment if payload > plugin MTU → plugin `send` → wire bytes. **Data flow (receive):** plugin `recv` → envelope verification → reassembly if fragmented → health update (phi sample) → deliver `Datagram` to caller. Loss/reordering/duplication are visible to callers via sequence numbers; recovery is `ids-protocol`'s responsibility.

**Design rules (non-negotiable):**
- One carrier crate only: `ids-carrier` is the single carrier crate in the workspace; zero other crates may touch sockets or carrier internals.
- `Endpoint` is the sole address type: `CarrierType` + opaque `Vec<u8>` capped at 1024 bytes. No IP, port, `SocketAddr`, DNS name.
- Datagram payloads are opaque `Vec<u8>`; `ids-carrier` never parses, inspects, or semantically interprets payload contents.
- No cryptography inside `ids-carrier`; framing checksum only, using BLAKE3 or SHA-256 (both in the allowed set).
- Unreliable datagrams by default (no ACK/retransmit/flow-control state in the core); optional reliability modules exist as research references but live behind `ids-protocol`.
- Plugins are loaded behind `CarrierPlugin`; dynamic loading is gated behind a feature flag and require explicit opt-in.
- Capability negotiation is mandatory before first send; MTU mismatch → fragment (ids-carrier) or reject, never silent truncation.
- Carrier health: phi accrual scoring; unhealthy → quarantined; reconnect via exponential backoff + jitter; never silent eternal retry.

---

### 3. Detailed Research Dimensions

#### 3.1 Opaque datagram transport interfaces

Research returned several prior-art datagram traits that shape the `CarrierPlugin` interface: kcp-tokio's `Transport` trait (`send_to(buf, target: &Self::Addr) -> usize`, `recv_from(buf) -> (usize, Self::Addr)`, `local_addr()`) with an associated `Addr` type; reconcile-gossip's `Transport` trait (`recv_from` into `buf` returning `(usize, SocketAddr)`, `send_to(buf, dst)`, `local_addr()`); embedded-nal's `UdpStack`/`ConnectedUdp` (send/receive datagrams in `no_std` embedded contexts); and the `datagram` crate's `DatagramSender::send(&[u8])`. Common pattern: a transport is defined by (a) an associated address type, (b) send/datagram-out and receive/datagram-in primitives, (c) a local address query. **Decision for `ids-carrier`:** `CarrierPlugin` exposes exactly this shape — `send_datagram(Endpoint, &[u8])`, `receive_datagram() -> Option<Datagram>`, `capabilities()`, `health()`, `name()` — with the address type fixed to `Endpoint` (carrier-agnostic) rather than `SocketAddr`. The associated-address pattern means a plugin's address representation stays inside the plugin; `ids-carrier` core sees only `Endpoint`.

#### 3.2 Carrier-agnostic endpoint and addressing

`Endpoint` = `CarrierType` (Loopback, Serial, Optical, Radio, Custom(u16), closed enum defined in `ids-000-aa`) + opaque `Vec<u8>` address bytes (≤1024 bytes per plan-001). Research on addressing without IP supports this: the "Addressless Internet" draft proposes eliminating end-to-end IP addresses entirely; LISP/ILNP/DIME locator/identifier separation splits "who" from "where"; Netsukuku ANDNA replaces DNS with hashed hostnames; OpenNet binds domains to cryptographic ServiceIDs rather than machines; IPFS-style content-addressed routing locates objects by key, not by IP. None of these require IP, TCP, or DNS inside the transport crate. **Decision:** address bytes are fully opaque to `ids-carrier` and interpreted only by the owning plugin; address resolution/naming (if any) belongs to `ids-discovery`/`ids-routing` layers above, never to `ids-carrier`. There is no DNS client, no address resolver, and no network-layer header in `ids-carrier`.

#### 3.3 Capability negotiation

Research: SDP offer/answer (RFC 3264 model) lets two peers advertise potential configurations and converge on a mutually supported actual configuration; SDP capability negotiation adds "potential configs" with attributes (crypto suites, transport types). WebRTC data channels expose reliability modes (reliable/ordered, unreliable/unordered, partial-reliable via maxRetransmits/maxPacketLifeTime) negotiated at channel creation. RFC 9221 (QUIC Unreliable Datagram Extension) advertises `max_datagram_frame_size` as a transport parameter during handshake — reviewed as research only; QUIC itself is prohibited. **Decision:** each plugin publishes `CarrierCapabilities { max_datagram_size, ordered, reliable, duplex, fragmentation_supported }`; before the first datagram to a peer, peers exchange capability advertisements and compute the intersection; `max_datagram_size` becomes the send MTU for that peer; mismatches (e.g., peer lacks fragmentation) cause the sender to fragment locally or reject oversized datagrams with `CarrierError::MtuExceeded`, never silent truncation. Negotiation results are cached per `Endpoint` and invalidated on health failure.

#### 3.4 Reliable datagram patterns (deferred to ids-protocol)

Research: ARQ reliable transmission (stop-and-wait, go-back-N, selective repeat with ACKs/NAKs, timeouts, sequence numbers); NAK-based reliable datagram service (LAMS-DLC, IEEE — checkpoint NAKs, near-optimal buffer use); NORM RFC 5740 (NACK-oriented reliable multicast). All assume an unreliable datagram substrate plus reliability layered on top. **Decision:** `ids-carrier` is deliberately unreliable (best-effort datagrams; loss/reorder/dup possible). Sequence numbers on `Datagram` let upper layers detect gaps. Reliability (ACK/NAK/retransmit/window) is owned by `ids-protocol`, not `ids-carrier`. An optional `reliability/` module (ARQ sketch, NAK sketch) is planned behind a feature flag for reference implementations only; it is not part of the core contract.

#### 3.5 Congestion control and backpressure for datagrams

Research: DCCP RFC 4340 (congestion-controlled unreliable datagrums with reliable handshake/teardown, CCID negotiation, ECN); Backpressure Flow Control (NSDI'22 — per-hop per-flow pause/resume with bounded state); credit-based flow control (receiver advertises free buffers; sender never exceeds credit); token bucket/leaky bucket rate shaping. **Decision:** `ids-carrier` exposes per-peer credit-based backpressure: `CarrierPlugin::credit_available() -> usize` and a credit-return signal; `send_datagram` returns `CarrierError::Backpressure` when peer credit is exhausted, so callers (and `ids-protocol`) throttle voluntarily. No end-to-end congestion control algorithm is mandated inside the crate; plugin authors may implement DCCP-style CCIDs inside their plugin.

#### 3.6 Framing, MTU, fragmentation, reassembly

Research: path MTU discovery (RFC 1191/3032 rules — fragments too large for output link; DF-bit semantics; reassembly only at destination); message framing alternatives — length-prefix (read N bytes then payload) vs delimiter (scan for escape byte; length-prefix preferred for opaque binary); IP fragmentation research (reassembly at destination, independent fragment travel, further fragmentation possible). **Decision:** `ids-carrier` uses a length-prefixed wire envelope (4-byte length + payload + BLAKE3/SHA-256 digest) per datagram fragment; per-plugin MTU comes from `CarrierCapabilities.max_datagram_size`; payloads exceeding MTU are fragmented by `ids-carrier` into numbered fragments and reassembled at the receiver before delivery; reassembly has a creation-time-keyed deadline (not RTT-based) so partial fragments never block indefinitely. No IP headers are ever constructed or parsed.

#### 3.7 Carrier health and failure detection

Research: phi accrual failure detector (Hazelcast, Akka, Cassandra — phi = -log10(1 − F(delay)) over heartbeat inter-arrival distribution; adaptive suspicion, threshold ~8–10; gracefully absorbs GC pauses and jitter); SWIM (alive/suspect/dead states, indirect probing). gRPC connection backoff (exponential backoff with jitter, initial 1s, multiplier 1.6, max 120s, jitter ±20%) prevents thundering herds on reconnect. **Decision:** each plugin emits heartbeat samples; `ids-carrier` runs a phi accrual scorer per peer; phi above threshold → `CarrierHealth::Unhealthy` → carrier quarantined (no sends, queued datagrams held or dropped per policy); recovery via exponential backoff with jitter (gRPC parameters). Health state is observable (`carrier_health(endpoint) -> CarrierHealth`) so `ids-failure-detector` and `ids-routing` can react. No binary dead/alive timeout; suspicion is continuous.

#### 3.8 Pluggable carrier architecture

Research: PTRS (Pluggable Transports in Rust — `PluggableTransport` trait with client/server builders, `name()`, `method_name()`, wraps `AsyncRead+AsyncWrite` streams); Tor pluggable transports (reviewed as anti-example — obfuscation/circumvention is out of scope for IDS; `ids-carrier` does not hide traffic patterns); ZeroMQ/nanomsg/NNG transport-agnostic socket API (opaque message blobs, bind/connect via `transport://address`, multiple transports — TCP, IPC, WebSocket — behind one socket type); Akka.Remote (location-transparent actor remoting, `Address`/`ActorPath` extended with remote addressing); WebRTC data channels and WebTransport datagrams (reliable/unreliable datagram modes over carrier); OpenCarrier Plugin SDK (write plugins in safe Rust). **Decision:** `ids-carrier` core is plugin-agnostic: `CarrierPlugin: Send + Sync + 'static` trait object; plugins register under a `CarrierType::Custom(u16)` id; a gated `plugin_loader` module supports dynamic loading (opt-in feature, audited `libloading`-style); static built-in plugins (in_process, local, loopback, test, blackhole) ship with the crate. No `tokio::net`, `std::net`, or socket types appear in the core; plugins may be sync or async internally behind the trait boundary.

---

### 4. Threat Model & Mitigations

|| Threat | Mitigation ||
||--------|-----------|-------------|
|| Endpoint spoofing (peer claims another's address) | Plugin authenticates endpoint ownership at bind time; `ids-crypto` (ed25519) signs endpoint binding above the carrier layer; carrier never trusts address bytes alone ||
|| Datagram tampering in transit | Envelope payload digest (BLAKE3 or SHA-256) verified before delivery; tampered datagrams dropped, never delivered ||
|| Replay of delivered datagrams | Datagram sequence numbers per endpoint; replay window tracked by `ids-protocol` layer; carrier delivers, upper layer deduplicates ||
|| MTU/fragmentation bomb (oversized payload exhausts buffers) | `max_datagram_size` from capability intersection; `CarrierError::MtuExceeded` on overshoot; fragment count cap per datagram; reassembly deadline (creation-time-keyed) bounds fragment buffer lifetime ||
|| Plugin compromise or misbehavior | Plugins run behind `CarrierPlugin` trait; quarantine unhealthy carriers (phi); revoke `Custom(u16)` plugin registration; no plugin can access another plugin's state ||
|| Health false positives mark healthy carrier unhealthy | Phi accrual adapts to observed jitter; quarantine requires sustained phi above threshold; recovery path always exists via backoff reconnect ||
|| Amplification via plugin (small in → massive out) | Per-peer credit-based backpressure; send credit cap; `send_datagram` returns `CarrierError::Backpressure` when exhausted ||
|| Address collision (two endpoints with identical bytes) | Address uniqueness is plugin-scoped (`CarrierType` + bytes); duplicate registration rejected by plugin registry at bind time ||
|| Loss/reordering/duplication (inherent to datagrams) | Explicit in contract; `Datagram.seq` lets callers detect; reliability is `ids-protocol`'s responsibility ||
|| Denial of service via datagram flood | Per-endpoint ingress queue caps; drop-tail with audit log; `receive_datagram` returns `CarrierError::QueueFull`; caller throttles ||
|| No address resolution (no DNS) by design | Addresses provisioned out of band or by `ids-discovery` above; `ids-carrier` never resolves names ||
|| Dynamic plugin loading abuse | `plugin_loader` behind feature flag; plugin signatures verified where configured; static plugins are the default and only audited path ||

---

### 5. Integration with Existing Crates

|| Crate | Role in Phase 002 ||
||-------|-------|-------------------|
|| `ids-000-aa` | Defines `Endpoint`, `CarrierType`, `trait Carrier` contract, unified error contract, invariants (incl. `out_eq_in` byte accounting at the carrier boundary); `ids-carrier` depends on it and re-exports `Endpoint`/`CarrierType` as `ids-carrier::` traffic surface ||
|| `ids-carrier` (this crate) | `Endpoint` re-export, `Datagram`, `send_datagram`/`receive_datagram`, `CarrierPlugin` trait + registry, capability negotiation, carrier health, carrier-agnostic addressing, length-prefixed framing + BLAKE3/SHA-256 checksums ||
|| `ids-crypto` | NOT a dependency of `ids-carrier`; cryptographic boundary — if authenticated/encrypted datagrams are ever layered on top, only ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305 may be used ||
|| `ids-protocol` | Consumer: framing, sequencing, acks, retransmission sit above `ids-carrier` using `Datagram.seq` and opaque payloads ||
|| `ids-discovery` / `ids-routing` | Consumers: address peers via `Endpoint`; no address resolution inside `ids-carrier` ||
|| All crates 3–100 | Depend on `ids-000-aa` and use `ids-carrier::Endpoint` as the only traffic surface; none import sockets ||
|| User carrier plugins | Implement `CarrierPlugin`; register under `CarrierType::Custom(u16)`; audited static plugins ship in-tree (in_process, local, loopback, test, blackhole) ||

**Integration points:** `ids-000-aa::contracts::carrier::Carrier` is implemented by `ids_carrier::CarrierEngine`; `send_datagram`/`receive_datagram` on the engine satisfy the contract. `ids-carrier` never calls into any other `ids-*` crate (one-way dependency: `ids-carrier` → `ids-000-aa` only).

### 7. Key Algorithms & Data Structures

#### 7.1 Endpoint and Datagram
```
Endpoint = { carrier: CarrierType, address: Vec<u8> }   // address ≤ 1024 bytes, opaque
CarrierType = Loopback | Serial | Optical | Radio | Custom(u16)
Datagram = { endpoint: Endpoint, payload: Vec<u8>, seq: u64 }
DatagramId = { origin: Endpoint, seq: u64 }
```

#### 7.2 CarrierPlugin trait (all carriers are plugins)
```
trait CarrierPlugin: Send + Sync + 'static {
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
    fn capabilities(&self) -> CarrierCapabilities;
    fn health(&self) -> CarrierHealth;
    fn send_datagram(&self, endpoint: &Endpoint, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<DatagramId, CarrierError>;
    fn receive_datagram(&self) -> Result<Option<Datagram>, CarrierError>;
}
```

#### 7.3 Capability negotiation (intersection)
```
local ∩ peer = CarrierCapabilities {
    max_datagram_size = min(local.max, peer.max),
    ordered = local.ordered && peer.ordered,
    reliable = local.reliable && peer.reliable,
    duplex = local.duplex && peer.duplex,
    fragmentation_supported = local.frag && peer.frag,
}
// send path: if payload.len() > negotiated.max_datagram_size → fragment (ids-carrier)
//             if !fragmentation_supported && overshoot → CarrierError::MtuExceeded
```

#### 7.4 Carrier health (phi accrual)
```
// phi = -log10(1 - F(delay)) where F is the CDF of heartbeat inter-arrival times
if phi > threshold (≈8–10): health = Unhealthy → quarantine
reconnect: backoff = min(initial * multiplier^attempt, max) + jitter(±20%)
```

#### 7.5 Length-prefixed framing + fragmentation
```
envelope = [u32 length] [payload bytes] [u32 digest(BLAKE3 or SHA-256 of payload)]
fragment i of n = { datagram_id, frag_index, frag_count, payload_slice }
reassemble: buffer by datagram_id; deliver only when all fragments present or deadline passed
deadline: creation_time + lifetime (creation-time-keyed, never RTT-based)
```

#### 7.6 Credit-based backpressure
```
credit_available(peer) -> usize; send_datagram decrements credit; plugin returns credits on
drain; credit == 0 → CarrierError::Backpressure (caller throttles, never blocks silently)
```

#### 7.7 What ids-carrier deliberately does NOT do
No ACK/retransmit (ids-protocol); no congestion-control algorithm in core (plugin may implement); no cryptography (ids-crypto); no address resolution (ids-discovery); no sockets (CarrierPlugin boundary).

|| `ids-000-aa` | `Endpoint`, `CarrierType`, `trait Carrier`, error contract, invariants (sole hard dependency) ||
|| `thiserror` | `CarrierError` enum ||
|| `bytes` | buffer handling for payloads ||
|| `serde` + `serde_bytes` | serialization of envelopes and test vectors ||
|| `blake3` | envelope payload digest (allowed crypto set) ||

|| `criterion` | benchmarks (dev-only) ||

**Prohibited dependencies (audited by test):** `std::net`, `tokio::net`, `tokio` runtime (core crate is sync/async-agnostic), `libp2p`, any IP/TCP/UDP/QUIC/HTTP/DNS crate, Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/cellular/VPN/mesh crates. `sha256` usage limited to envelope digest if chosen over BLAKE3; `xchacha20poly1305`, `chacha20poly1305`, `ed25519` are **not** used by `ids-carrier` (crypto boundary: `ids-crypto`).

### 9. Measurable Acceptance Criteria

|| # | Criterion | Measurement ||
||---|-----------|-------------|
|| AC-002.1 | Byte-exact datagram round trip | send_datagram → receive_datagram over in_process carrier returns identical `Vec<u8>`, seq matched, 10k iterations ||
|| AC-002.2 | Endpoint is the only address type | All send/recv APIs take/return `ids-carrier::Endpoint`; grep audit confirms no `SocketAddr`, `IpAddr`, port, or DNS type in `ids-carrier` ||
|| AC-002.3 | Zero prohibited dependencies | `cargo tree` + grep audit: no std::net/tokio::net/libp2p/IP/TCP/UDP/QUIC/HTTP/DNS/Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/cellular/VPN/mesh crate or module anywhere in `ids-carrier` ||
|| AC-002.4 | Capability negotiation converges | Two peers exchange `CarrierCapabilities`; negotiated `max_datagram_size` = min; mismatched reliability → neither peer claims reliable ||
|| AC-002.5 | MTU enforcement | Payload > negotiated MTU is fragmented or rejected with `CarrierError::MtuExceeded`; never silently truncated; reassembly is byte-exact ||
|| AC-002.6 | Carrier health + quarantine | Phi above threshold marks peer `Unhealthy`; sends return `CarrierError::CarrierUnhealthy`; backoff+jitter reconnect recovers ||
|| AC-002.7 | Opaque payloads | `ids-carrier` never inspects payload bytes beyond digest/length; test with entropy-random payloads passes unchanged ||
|| AC-002.8 | No cryptography in carrier | Only BLAKE3/SHA-256 envelope digest; no ed25519/xchacha20poly1305/chacha20poly1305 imports in `ids-carrier` ||
|| AC-002.9 | Deterministic test carrier | `test` plugin: fixed seed → identical send/recv sequence across runs ||
|| AC-002.10 | Property tests | 100,000+ proptest iterations: endpoint round-trip, datagram seq monotonicity, fragment reassembly, capability intersection idempotence ||
|| AC-002.11 | Fuzz targets pass | malformed envelopes, oversized fragments, capability chaos → all fail-safe (error returned, no panic) ||
|| AC-002.12 | Backpressure | `credit == 0` → `send_datagram` returns `CarrierError::Backpressure` without blocking ||
|| AC-002.13 | Plugin isolation | One plugin's failure/panic boundary does not corrupt another plugin's state (test via blackhole + in_process coexistence) ||

### 10. Remaining Uncertainties

1. **Closed vs open `CarrierType`:** plan-001 sketches a closed enum (`Loopback, Serial, Optical, Radio, Custom(u16)`). Confirm whether user plugins must always use `Custom(u16)` or whether the enum should be `#[non_exhaustive]`/plugin-registered.
2. **Sync vs async plugin trait:** `ids-carrier` core is sync; plugins may be async internally. Decide whether `CarrierPlugin::send_datagram` returns `Result` or `impl Future` — no `tokio` dependency, so any async is plugin-private behind the trait.
3. **Dynamic plugin loading:** `libloading`-style loading is opt-in and security-sensitive; decide whether it ships at all or whether plugins are linked statically only.
4. **Datagram size ceiling:** 1024-byte address cap comes from plan-001; the payload max (negotiated MTU default) has no agreed default value yet — workload-dependent.
5. **Fragmentation reassembly deadline:** creation-time-keyed lifetime is chosen, but the default deadline value and cleanup policy are unquantified.
6. **Address provisioning:** how endpoints learn peer addresses (static config vs `ids-discovery` gossip) is deferred to `ids-discovery`; `ids-carrier` provides only the hook.
7. **Credit exhaustion policy:** whether `send_datagram` blocks, errors, or drops when peer credit is exhausted needs a product decision (plan: return `CarrierError::Backpressure`).
8. **no_std support:** whether `ids-carrier` compiles `no_std` (embedded carriers) is undecided; `features.rs` reserves the flag.

---

### 11. Engineering Decisions Summary

|| Decision | Rationale ||
||----------|-----------|-------------|
|| Separate `ids-carrier` crate (not subfolder) | User rule: separate crates instead of more folders; keeps carrier boundary crisp ||
|| `Endpoint` = `CarrierType` + opaque `Vec<u8>` (≤1024 B) | Matches plan-001 `ids-000-aa` design; sole IDS address type; no IP/DNS ||
|| `ids-carrier::Endpoint` is the traffic surface | Re-exports `ids-000-aa::Endpoint`; all 99 crates route through it ||
|| Unreliable datagrams by default | Loss/reorder/dup expected; reliability belongs to `ids-protocol`; keeps carrier thin ||
|| `CarrierPlugin` trait + registry | Every carrier is a plugin; core imports zero sockets; user carriers via `Custom(u16)` ||
|| Capability intersection before first send | SDP offer/answer pattern; MTU and reliability negotiated explicitly ||
|| Length-prefixed envelope + BLAKE3/SHA-256 digest | Length-prefix suits opaque binary; digest is the only integrity mechanism, using allowed primitives ||
|| Phi accrual carrier health + quarantine | Adaptive suspicion absorbs jitter/GC pauses (Hazelcast/Akka); quarantine avoids silent eternal retry ||
|| Exponential backoff with jitter for reconnect | gRPC pattern; prevents thundering herd after carrier outage ||
|| Per-peer credit-based backpressure | Sender never overwhelms receiver; `CarrierError::Backpressure` is explicit, never silent blocking ||
|| No crypto in `ids-carrier` | Crypto boundary is `ids-crypto`; allowed primitives (ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305) apply only above ||
|| No `std::net`/`tokio::net`/libp2p/IP/TCP/UDP/QUIC/HTTP/DNS | Carrier-agnostic absolute rule; audited by `prohibited_deps_tests` ||

# PHASE 003:

## Phase 003 — Create the ids-crypto crate: Research Findings & Implementation Blueprint

**Research complete (30 targeted searches executed). No code written, no files created, no repository changes made. This document is the blueprint for implementation.**

---

### 1. Executive Summary

Phase 003 creates a **new separate crate `ids-crypto`** (not folders inside an existing crate), organized into subfolders by subsystem. It is the IDS cryptographic primitive layer implementing **only** the allowed primitives: ed25519 (signing/verification), xchacha20poly1305 and chacha20poly1305 (symmetric authenticated encryption), sha256 and blake3 (hashing). It provides key generation, signing, verification, symmetric encryption/decryption, hashing, key derivation, nonce management, key rotation, key revocation, and constant-time comparisons — all exposed behind a narrow, domain-specific API surface so callers never touch raw algorithm primitives directly.

**Critical structural rule:** `ids-crypto` is the **only** IDS crate (of 100) that does **NOT** depend on `ids-000-aa`. This avoids a circular dependency: `ids-000-aa` would otherwise need crypto types for its canonical `Endpoint`/`CarrierType`, and `ids-crypto` would need `ids-000-aa` types. `ids-crypto` is a leaf crate with zero dependencies on any other IDS crate. All downstream crates (ids-identity, ids-security, ids-session, etc.) depend on `ids-crypto` directly.

**No networking dependencies:** no `std::net`, `tokio::net`, libp2p, IP, TCP, UDP, QUIC, HTTP, DNS, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular, VPN, or mesh anywhere in the crate. `ids-crypto` has no concept of a network address, socket, or carrier; all traffic that eventually crosses a wire rides `ids-carrier::Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>`) in the carrier crate, and `ids-crypto` merely produces/consumes the byte payloads sealed inside those datagrams.

### 2. Architecture Overview

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    DOWNSTREAM IDS CRATES                            │
│  ids-identity · ids-security · ids-session · ids-membership · …     │
│  (each depends directly on ids-crypto; none depend on each other    │
│   for crypto)                                                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                  │
                                  ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            Phase 003: ids-crypto (NEW LEAF CRATE)                   │
│  ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌────────────┐ │
│  │  ed25519     │ │  xchacha20   │ │  sha256      │ │  blake3    │ │
│  │  sign/verify │ │  poly1305    │ │  hash        │ │  hash/KDF  │ │
│  │  key gen     │ │  AEAD seal/  │ │  digest      │ │  keyed/    │ │
│  │  constant-time│ │  open        │ │  constant-time│ │  derive    │ │
│  └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └────────────┘ │
│  ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌────────────┐ │
│  │ chacha20poly │ │ key derivation│ │ nonce mgmt   │ │ key rotation││
│  │ 1305 AEAD    │ │  (HKDF + BLAKE3│ │  generation/ │ │  revocation││
│  │  seal/open   │ │  derive_key)  │ │  tracking/   │ │  grow-only ││
│  └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └────────────┘ │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │  constant_time.rs — ct_eq, ct_select, zeroize on drop          │ │
│  │  errors.rs — CryptoError (thiserror, no fallback to panic)     │ │
│  │  prelude.rs — re-exports                                        │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                  │
                                  ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            ids-carrier (opaque Endpoint: CarrierType + Vec<u8>)      │
│  send_datagram / receive_datagram — carries sealed ids-crypto       │
│  payloads; ids-crypto does NOT import ids-carrier (one-way dep)      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Design principle — domain wrapper, not raw exposure:** `ids-crypto` does not re-export `ed25519-dalek::SigningKey` or `aead::Aead` traits directly into the IDS codebase. Every primitive is wrapped in an IDS-specific newtype (`Ed25519SigningKey`, `XChaCha20Poly1305SealKey`, `Blake3Digest`, `Sha256Digest`, `Nonce`, `KeyHandle`) so that (a) allowed-algorithm policy is enforced at the type boundary, (b) key material is zeroized on drop, (c) nonce uniqueness rules are encoded in types rather than comments, and (d) the crate can swap implementations without touching the other 99 crates.

**Zeroize discipline:** Every key-holding type implements `zeroize::Zeroize` and `Drop` that zeroes memory on scope exit. No secret material survives beyond the lifetime of its wrapper type.

**No RNG inside the crate:** `ids-crypto` does not import `getrandom`, `rand`, or any OS entropy source. Key generation and nonce generation accept caller-provided entropy via a `CryptoRng`-like trait parameter (or take a `&mut impl RngCore + CryptoRng`). This keeps the crate pure, testable, and carrier-/runtime-agnostic. The caller (e.g. ids-identity or ids-security) supplies entropy.

---

### 3. Detailed Research Dimensions

#### 3.1 ed25519 — signatures and key generation

**Research basis:** RFC 8032 specifies Ed25519 as a pure EdDSA over Curve25519 with SHA-512. Signatures are deterministic: `r = SHA-512(prefix || message)`, `s = (r + k·a) mod L`. Key generation: 32-byte random seed → SHA-512 → clamp (clear bits 0,1,2 of byte 0; clear bit 7 of byte 31; set bit 6 of byte 31) → scalar `s` → public key `A = [s]B`. Verification checks `S·B = R + k·A` where `k = SHA-512(R || A || M)`. Verification must reject non-canonical `S >= L`, small-order points, and malformed encodings (strict checking per ZIP-215 / RFC 8032 §5.1.7).

**ids-crypto decision:** Wrap ed25519 in `Ed25519SigningKey` / `Ed25519VerifyingKey` newtypes. Key generation takes caller entropy (32 bytes). Signing is deterministic per RFC 8032 (no per-message randomness beyond the key seed). Verification uses strict checks: public key on-curve, `S < L`, `R` decodes, cofactorless equation holds. Context strings (Ed25519ctx) supported for domain separation between IDS subsystems (e.g. "ids-identity/v1/mapping", "ids-security/v1/revocation"). Ed25519ph (prehashed) explicitly rejected — prehash variants are deprecated in RFC 8032 §8.5 and add collision risk.

#### 3.2 xchacha20poly1305 — extended-nonce AEAD

**Research basis:** XChaCha20-Poly1305 (draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha, RFC 8439 family) extends ChaCha20-Poly1305's nonce from 96 bits to 192 bits (24 bytes) by deriving a subkey via HChaCha20 from the first 16 bytes of the nonce, then delegating to standard ChaCha20-Poly1305 with the remaining 8 bytes as the 64-bit nonce. Because the nonce is 192 bits, random per-message nonces are safe: birthday-bound collision probability reaches 50% only after ~2^96 messages (~7.3×10^28), effectively infinite for any practical key lifetime. Standard ChaCha20-Poly1305's 96-bit nonce is too short for safe random generation (collision probable after ~2^48 messages ≈ 9 days at 10^9 msgs/sec).

**ids-crypto decision:** `ids-crypto` exposes `XChaCha20Poly1305Seal` / `XChaCha20Poly1305Open` as the **primary** symmetric AEAD, with random 24-byte nonces generated by the caller. `ChaCha20Poly1305` (96-bit nonce) is offered only as a secondary, stateful path requiring caller-managed monotonic counters (documented risk: counter persistence across restarts). Tag size 16 bytes (Poly1305). Key size 32 bytes. AAD supported. Decryption verifies tag before releasing plaintext (fail closed). Nonce reuse with the same key is fatal (reveals plaintext XOR + Poly1305 key recovery) — documented as a hard precondition, enforced by type design where possible.

#### 3.3 chacha20poly1305 — standard-nonce AEAD

**Research basis:** RFC 8439 / RFC 7539 define ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD: 256-bit key, 96-bit nonce, 32-bit block counter (counter 0 reserved for Poly1305 one-time key derivation), 256 GB max plaintext per key, 16-byte tag. Nonce uniqueness is mandatory; reuse breaks both confidentiality (keystream reuse → plaintext XOR) and authenticity (one-time Poly1305 key reuse → universal forgery).

**ids-crypto decision:** Secondary AEAD path behind `ChaCha20Poly1305Seal` / `ChaCha20Poly1305Open`. Requires caller to supply a 12-byte nonce guaranteed unique per key (counter recommended; random only with documented birthday limits). Max message size 256 GB enforced. Not default because random-nonce safety is the IDS design goal.

#### 3.4 sha256 — cryptographic hash

**Research basis:** FIPS 180-4 Secure Hash Standard. SHA-256 produces a 256-bit digest via serial Merkle-Damgård over 512-bit blocks. 128-bit collision resistance, 256-bit preimage resistance. Serial chain limits throughput to single-core performance; no length-extension immunity (SHA-256 is vulnerable to length-extension attacks).

**ids-crypto decision:** `Sha256Digest` newtype wrapping `sha2::Sha256` (RustCrypto Digest trait). Used where FIPS-aligned hashing is required (e.g. compatibility with external systems, content addressing that must be SHA-256). Not used for per-message authentication where BLAKE3 keyed mode suffices.

#### 3.5 blake3 — hash, keyed MAC, KDF, XOF

**Research basis:** BLAKE3 is a single algorithm based on BLAKE2 + Bao tree mode. Three domain-separated modes: `hash` (unkeyed), `keyed_hash` (32-byte key → PRF/MAC), `derive_key` (context string + key material → KDF). All modes support extendable output (XOF) of arbitrary length. Default 256-bit output. 128-bit collision resistance, 256-bit preimage resistance. Immune to length-extension by design (tree structure, domain separation). Highly parallelizable (SIMD, multi-threaded), typically 3–12× faster than SHA-256 on large inputs; slightly slower only on very small (<4 KiB) batched inputs.

**ids-crypto decision:** `Blake3Digest` is the **default** hash for IDS-internal use: content fingerprints, mapping-table integrity, nonce derivation, key derivation context. `blake3::derive_key(context, key_material)` used for IDS key derivation (replaces HKDF where BLAKE3's context-committed KDF is sufficient). `blake3::keyed_hash` used for MAC where HMAC-SHA256 would otherwise appear. HKDF-SHA256 retained as the explicit KDF option when a standard KDF is required (see 3.6).

#### 3.6 Key derivation — HKDF-SHA256 and BLAKE3 derive_key

**Research basis:** RFC 5869 HKDF: Extract (HMAC(salt, IKM) → PRK) + Expand (PRK + info + counter → OKM of arbitrary length). Conservative, hash-agnostic, widely deployed (TLS 1.3, Signal, MLS, CMS). BLAKE3 `derive_key(context, key_material)` provides context-committed KDF in one call with extensible output; context string should be hardcoded, globally unique, application-specific ("[application] [timestamp] [purpose]").

**ids-crypto decision:** Two KDF entry points:
- `hkdf_sha256_derive(ikm, salt, info, length)` — when standards compliance (RFC 5869) or interoperability is needed.
- `blake3_derive_key(context, key_material, length)` — default IDS-internal KDF; context strings namespaced per subsystem ("ids-crypto/v1/session-key", "ids-crypto/v1/identity-seed", etc.).
Both output key material into zeroizing `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>` or fixed-size array types.

#### 3.7 Nonce generation and management

**Research basis:** ChaCha20-Poly1305 (96-bit nonce): random nonce collision probable after ~2^48 messages under one key — unsafe for random generation; requires monotonic counter with crash-recovery persistence. XChaCha20-Poly1305 (192-bit nonce): random per-message nonce safe (2^96 birthday bound). Nonce must never repeat with the same key; nonce is not secret and may be sent alongside ciphertext.

**ids-crypto decision:** `Nonce` newtype, size-parameterized (`Nonce96` for ChaCha20Poly1305, `Nonce192` for XChaCha20Poly1305). Generation: caller supplies entropy; `ids-crypto` fills bytes and returns the typed nonce. For XChaCha20, random generation is the documented default. For ChaCha20, a `NonceCounter` type wraps a monotonic u64 with overflow detection; persistence across restarts is the caller's responsibility (ids-security or ids-session owns counter storage). Nonce tracking (used-nonce set) is out of scope for `ids-crypto` — it is a primitive layer; replay/nonce-tracking lives in ids-security/ids-session.

#### 3.8 Key rotation and key revocation

**Research basis:** OWASP Key Management Cheat Sheet / NIST SP 800-57: symmetric data encryption keys capped at ~2 years for low-volume, days to weeks for high-volume/link encryption. Usage-based limits (e.g. AES-GCM 2^32 IVs) apply by volume, not just calendar. Key rotation must account for both time and volume. Grow-only revocation sets (G-Set, CRDT-style): revocation is append-only, idempotent, no "un-revoke"; gossip-propagated; compromised identity gets a fresh key rather than un-revoking (Agent Manifest x0x pattern; GNUEG revocation flooding + set reconciliation).

**ids-crypto decision:** `KeyHandle` carries a version/epoch u64. `KeyRotation` module: rotate-on-time and rotate-on-volume policies, configurable thresholds (default symmetric key rotation after configurable message count or time window; ed25519 signing keys longer-lived). `RevocationStore`: grow-only set of revoked key identifiers (blake3 fingerprint of public key), each entry signed by the issuer (ed25519). `is_revoked(key_id)` → fail-closed check. Revocation distribution (gossip over ids-carrier::Endpoint) lives in ids-identity/ids-security; `ids-crypto` provides the signed revocation record type, serialization, and verification primitive only.

#### 3.9 Constant-time comparisons

**Research basis:** `memcmp()` / `==` exit early on first byte difference → timing side-channel enables byte-by-byte secret recovery (MAC forgery, token guessing). Constant-time comparison: XOR all bytes, OR into accumulator, single branch on final result. Rust `subtle::ConstantTimeEq` / `zeroize` are the established patterns; CVE-2023-49092 (Marvin) and RustSec advisories show real-world impact of non-constant-time crypto code.

**ids-crypto decision:** `constant_time` module: `ct_eq(a, b) -> bool` (constant-time equality for same-length slices; length mismatch returns false without leaking which length), `ct_select(cond, a, b)` (constant-time conditional move), `ct_digest_eq(a, b)` for digest comparison. All signature verification, MAC tag verification, and key fingerprint comparison route through these. No `==` on secret material anywhere in the crate.

---

### 4. Threat Model & Mitigations

| Threat | Mitigation |
|--------|-----------|
| Nonce reuse with same key (ChaCha20-Poly1305 96-bit) | XChaCha20-Poly1305 default with 192-bit random nonces; ChaCha20-Poly1305 requires caller-managed counter; overflow detection on NonceCounter |
| Poly1305 key recovery from nonce reuse | Documented as fatal; type design makes nonce reuse hard to accidentally do; key handle ties nonce space to key epoch |
| Signature forgery via weak/malleable signatures | Strict ed25519 verification: S < L, point decoding, cofactorless equation; ZIP-215 checks; context strings for domain separation |
| Timing attacks on comparison/verification | constant_time module everywhere; subtle-style CT eq/select; zeroize on drop |
| Secret material lingering in memory | Zeroize on all key/nonce/seed types; Drop impl zeroes; no logging of secrets |
| Key compromise with no revocation path | RevocationStore grow-only set + signed revocation records; rotation policies; fresh key on compromise (no un-revoke) |
| Collision/hash weakness | BLAKE3 default (128-bit collision, no length-extension); SHA-256 available where FIPS alignment required |
| Wrong algorithm used (policy violation) | Newtype wrappers + feature-gated primitive exposure; only 5 allowed algorithms compile in; any other crypto crate is a compile-time dependency error |
| Replay of sealed ciphertext | Out of scope for ids-crypto (primitive layer); replay protection lives in ids-security/ids-session using ids-crypto outputs |
| Key derivation without context separation | BLAKE3 derive_key requires context string; HKDF uses info parameter; both enforce domain separation by API design |
| Entropy supplied by weak caller RNG | ids-crypto takes caller entropy; documented requirement that caller uses CSPRNG; no internal RNG to fail |

---

### 5. Integration with Existing Crates

Phase 003 depends on and integrates with:

| Crate | Role in Phase 003 |
|-------|-------------------|
| `ids-crypto` | This crate — leaf, no IDS dependencies |
| `ids-carrier` | `ids-crypto` does NOT depend on ids-carrier; downstream crates place sealed ids-crypto payloads into `Endpoint(CarrierType, Vec<u8>)` datagrams |
| `ids-000-aa` | **No dependency** — ids-crypto is the only IDS crate without this dependency (avoids circular dependency) |
| `ids-identity` | Uses ed25519 for identity keys, blake3 for StableNodeId/RNI derivation, xchacha20poly1305 for at-rest encryption |
| `ids-security` | Uses all primitives for auth, encryption, key management, revocation |
| `ids-session` | Uses xchacha20poly1305/chacha20poly1305 for session encryption, ed25519 for session binding |
| `ids-membership` | Uses ed25519 for credential validation |
| All downstream | Depend directly on ids-crypto; never transitively through another IDS crate for crypto |

**Integration points:**
- `ids-crypto` produces byte payloads (signatures, ciphertexts, digests, derived keys); downstream crates embed these in `ids-carrier::Endpoint` datagrams or persist them.
- `ids-crypto` accepts entropy from callers; no `getrandom`/`rand` dependency inside the crate.
- Downstream crates never call raw `ed25519-dalek`, `aead`, `sha2`, or `blake3` directly — they go through `ids-crypto` wrappers, enforcing the allowed-algorithm policy at one boundary.
- No `std::net`, `tokio::net`, libp2p, TCP/IP, UDP, QUIC, HTTP, DNS, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular, VPN, or mesh anywhere (I-CARR-001 carrier-agnostic rule).

### 7. Key Algorithms & Data Structures

#### 7.1 ed25519 key generation (RFC 8032)
```
seed = 32 random bytes (caller-provided entropy)
h = SHA-512(seed)
s = clamp(h[0..32])     // clear bits 0,1,2 of byte 0; clear bit 7 of byte 31; set bit 6 of byte 31
A = [s]B                // scalar base mult on edwards25519
pubkey = encode(A)      // 32-byte little-endian y-coordinate + sign bit of x
keypair = (seed, pubkey) // both zeroized on drop
```

#### 7.2 ed25519 sign / verify (RFC 8032, strict)
```
sign(seed, prefix, M, context):
  h = SHA-512(seed) → (s, prefix_bytes)
  r = SHA-512(prefix_bytes || context || M) mod L
  R = [r]B
  k = SHA-512(R || A || M) mod L
  s = (r + k·s) mod L
  sig = encode(R) || encode(s)   // 64 bytes

verify(pubkey, M, sig, context):
  reject if sig not 64 bytes; reject if pubkey not on-curve (ZIP-215)
  split sig into R (32) || s (32); reject if s >= L (non-canonical)
  k = SHA-512(R || A || M) mod L
  accept iff s·B = R + k·A   (cofactorless equation)
```

#### 7.3 XChaCha20-Poly1305 seal / open (draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha / RFC 8439)
```
seal(key, plaintext, aad, nonce192):
  subkey = HChaCha20(key, nonce192[0..16])
  subnonce = 0x00000000 || nonce192[16..24]   // 96-bit nonce for inner ChaCha20
  (ciphertext, tag) = ChaCha20Poly1305(seal, subkey, plaintext, aad, subnonce)
  return nonce192 || ciphertext || tag

open(key, nonce192 || ciphertext || tag, aad):
  subkey = HChaCha20(key, nonce192[0..16])
  subnonce = 0x00000000 || nonce192[16..24]
  plaintext = ChaCha20Poly1305(open, subkey, ciphertext, aad, subnonce, tag)
  reject if tag verification fails (constant-time compare, fail closed)
```

#### 7.4 ChaCha20-Poly1305 seal / open (RFC 8439 / RFC 7539)
```
seal(key, plaintext, aad, nonce96):
  poly_key = ChaCha20(key, counter=0, nonce96)   // first block → Poly1305 one-time key
  ciphertext = ChaCha20(key, counter=1.., nonce96) XOR plaintext
  tag = Poly1305(poly_key, aad || ciphertext || lengths)
  return ciphertext || tag   // nonce96 carried separately by caller

open: recompute tag; constant-time compare; reject on mismatch before releasing plaintext
```

#### 7.5 BLAKE3 derive_key (KDF)
```
derive_key(context, key_material, length):
  stage1 = BLAKE3_hash(IV, DERIVE_KEY_CONTEXT flag, context) → 32-byte context_key
  stage2 = BLAKE3_hash(context_key, DERIVE_KEY_MATERIAL flag, key_material) → length bytes
  return stage2[0..length]
```

#### 7.6 HKDF-SHA256 (RFC 5869)
```
extract(salt, ikm) = HMAC-SHA256(salt, ikm) → PRK
expand(PRK, info, L) = T(1)||T(2)||... where T(i) = HMAC-SHA256(PRK, T(i-1)||info||i)
                      truncate to L bytes
```

#### 7.7 Constant-time equality
```
ct_eq(a, b):
  if len(a) != len(b): return false   // length check not timing-secret (public lengths)
  acc = 0
  for i in 0..len: acc |= a[i] ^ b[i]
  return acc == 0
```

#### 7.8 Revocation record (grow-only)
```
RevocationRecord {
  key_id: [u8; 32],        // blake3(revoked public key)
  reason: RevocationReason,
  issued_at: u64,          // ids-time tick
  issuer_sig: Ed25519Signature,
}
RevocationStore: grow-only set of records; add is idempotent; is_revoked(key_id) → fail-closed
```

### 10. Remaining Uncertainties

1. **Concrete ed25519 crate:** `ed25519` (types only) + `ed25519-dalek` (implementation) vs `signature` traits abstraction vs a single pure-Rust crate. Decision pending implementation; dalek is the most mature with constant-time signing and verify_strict.
2. **Wire encoding:** CBOR (deterministic, self-describing) vs bincode vs protobuf for sealed envelopes in carrier datagrams. CBOR favored; crate TBD.
3. **HKDF vs BLAKE3 derive_key as default KDF:** BLAKE3 derive_key is simpler and context-committed; HKDF-SHA256 offers RFC 5869 compliance. Both provided; default TBD.
4. **Nonce counter persistence:** ChaCha20-Poly1305's 96-bit nonce requires a monotonic counter; persisting it across restarts (to avoid reuse after reboot) is a downstream (ids-security/ids-session) concern, not solved in ids-crypto.
5. **Revocation distribution:** ids-crypto provides the signed revocation record type; gossip/distribution over ids-carrier::Endpoint lives in ids-identity/ids-security — integration boundary TBD.
6. **Formal verification scope:** TLA+/PlusCal spec of nonce safety and revocation monotonicity (in ids-doc) — effort level TBD.
7. **Feature flags:** whether to make individual primitives feature-gated (e.g. no_sha256 for minimal builds) — API surface decision pending.

---

### 11. Engineering Decisions Summary

| Decision | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|
| ids-crypto is a leaf crate (no ids-000-aa dep) | avoids circular dependency; only IDS crate without this dependency (CRATES.md rule) |
| Domain newtypes over raw primitives | enforces allowed-algorithm policy at one boundary; zeroize on drop; implementation-swap friendly |
| XChaCha20-Poly1305 as primary AEAD | 192-bit nonce makes random per-message nonces safe; no counter state needed |
| ChaCha20-Poly1305 secondary, counter-only | 96-bit nonce unsafe for random generation; caller manages monotonic counter |
| Deterministic ed25519 (RFC 8032) | no per-message randomness; simpler, matches RFC 8032 default |
| Strict ed25519 verification (S<L, on-curve, ZIP-215) | prevents signature malleability and weak-key forgery |
| BLAKE3 default hash | faster than SHA-256, no length-extension, built-in keyed/KDF/XOF modes |
| SHA-256 available for FIPS alignment | where external compliance requires it |
| No internal RNG; caller supplies entropy | pure, testable, runtime-agnostic |
| Constant-time everywhere (ct_eq, ct_select) | side-channel resistance for all secret comparisons |
| Zeroize on all key/nonce/seed types | no secret material survives scope exit |
| Revocation = grow-only signed set | append-only, idempotent, fail-closed; fresh key on compromise (no un-revoke) |
| Context strings for ed25519ctx + KDF contexts | domain separation between IDS subsystems |
| New separate crate ids-crypto | matches CRATES.md "separate crates, not more folders" rule; ~250–400 files |

# PHASE 004:

## Phase 004 — Create the ids-identity crate: Research Findings & Implementation Blueprint

**Research complete (30 targeted searches executed). No code written, no files created, no repository changes made. This document is the blueprint for implementation.**

---

### 1. Executive Summary

Phase 004 creates a **new separate crate `ids-identity`** (not folders inside an existing crate), organized into subfolders by subsystem. It implements IDS-B identity separation: a **stable internal identity** (`StableNodeId`, never exposed on the wire) paired with a **periodically rotating network-facing identifier** (`RotatingNodeId`, RNI). All traffic rides `ids-carrier::Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>`); the crate is strictly carrier-agnostic. Allowed crypto only: ed25519 (signing/verification of RNI mappings), xchacha20poly1305 and chacha20poly1305 (encrypting identity records at rest), sha256 and blake3 (fingerprints, mapping-table integrity, StableNodeId derivation).

**Core design:** `StableNodeId` is a node's permanent logical identity (key-derived or random, assigned at enrollment, never reused after a node leaves). `RotatingNodeId` is a short-lived, unlinkable network handle derived from the stable identity, rotated on a schedule with validity windows and a transition state machine (scheduled → active → superseded → expired → revoked). The RNI mapping table stores `(RNI → StableNodeId, validity window, state, ed25519 signature)` entries; resolution is authenticated (caller presents an ed25519-signed mapping proof). Rotation is enforced **idle-only**: an RNI rotates only while the node has no in-flight requests; active requests keep their stable ID. Emergency revocation immediately invalidates an RNI (and, on compromise, forces a fresh `StableNodeId` — a dead node never returns with its old identity).

**No networking dependencies:** no `std::net`, `tokio::net`, libp2p, IP, TCP, UDP, QUIC, HTTP, DNS, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular, VPN, or mesh. All identity announcement/resolution traffic is opaque `ids-carrier::Endpoint` bytes.

---
