### 7. Key Algorithms & Data Structures

1. **SWIM probe loop:** every protocol period T, scheduler selects target (random or round-robin), emits `Ping` over `ids-carrier::Endpoint`; on `Ping-Ack` within window, member stays `alive`; on silence, dispatch `k` indirect probers; indirect-prober agreement upgrades `suspected` toward confirmed.
2. **Gossip dissemination:** suspicion/alive/dead transitions piggyback on outgoing ping/ack datagrams; epidemic spread reaches O(log N) periods cluster-wide; anti-entropy re-probing repairs divergence.
3. **Phi accrual:** sliding window (last N inter-arrival samples in `Idstime` ticks); running mean/variance; normal CDF F; φ = -log10(1 − F(timeSinceLastHeartbeat)); conviction when φ ≥ Φ; margin absorbs occasional lost heartbeats (GC pauses).
4. **Chandra-Toueg evaluation:** configurable completeness class (strong/weak) and accuracy class (strong/weak/eventual); runtime evaluation against observed suspicion/proven sets.
5. **Suspected vs proven:** `Suspected` = φ ≥ Φ or SWIM indirect silence (hint only, no recovery); `Proven` = indirect-prober quorum agreement or STONITH evidence; only `Proven` advances ids-membership to `failed` and triggers ids-recovery.
6. **Oscillation control:** pending duration D, consecutive-check count C, hysteresis deadband (Φ_suspect > Φ_refute), per-domain damping, exponential backoff on repeat flappers.
7. **Authenticated envelopes:** ed25519 signature over (sender NodeId, payload, nonce, Idstime timestamp); blake3/sha256 digest of member-state for gossip anti-entropy; optional chacha20poly1305/xchacha20poly1305 envelope encryption.
8. **Data structures:** `MemberList` (NodeId → Member), `SuspicionTable` (NodeId → φ history), `ProvenFailureRegistry`, `OscillationLog`, `ReplayNonceCache`.

### 8. Dependencies

- `ids-000-aa` — types, sealed trait contracts, invariants, error contracts (required; master crate).
- `ids-carrier` — `Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>`), `send_datagram`/`receive_datagram` (required; sole traffic path).
- `ids-crypto` — ed25519, blake3, sha256, chacha20poly1305, xchacha20poly1305 (required; only allowed crypto set).
- `ids-time` — `Idstime` proprietary tick basis (required; no wall-clock).
- `ids-topology` — `FailureDomain` for correlated-suspicion grouping (optional feature-gated integration).

No `std::net`, `tokio::net`, libp2p, or any carrier crate beyond `ids-carrier`. Dev/test dependencies (proptest, criterion) limited to test-only targets with no networking. Cargo.toml will carry an explicit audit rule: prohibited-dependency check fails the build if any forbidden crate appears.

### 9. Measurable Acceptance Criteria

- **Carrier-agnostic:** zero references to `std::net`, `tokio::net`, libp2p, IP/TCP/UDP/QUIC/HTTP/DNS/Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/cellular/VPN/mesh; all traffic via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>`). Verified by dependency audit + source grep.
- **Crypto bound:** only ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305 appear in `ids-crypto`-bound code paths; any other crypto dependency fails CI.
- **Time basis:** all phi inter-arrival measurements and protocol period T keyed to `ids-time::Idstime`; no `std::time::SystemTime`/wall-clock in failure-reasoning paths.
- **SWIM:** probe period T configurable; expected detection within O(k) periods; gossip dissemination reaches quorum in O(log N) periods; suspicion precedes death (alive → suspected → confirmed).
- **Phi:** φ = -log10(1 − F(t)) implemented; sliding window size N configurable; threshold Φ configurable (paper sweet spot 8 ≤ Φ); heartbeat margin absorbs ≥1 missed heartbeat without conviction.
- **Completeness/accuracy:** strong/weak completeness and strong/weak/eventual accuracy exposed as selectable contracts; runtime evaluation reports property satisfaction per failure domain.
- **Suspected vs proven:** suspicion alone never triggers ids-recovery; proven failure requires indirect-prober quorum or STONITH evidence; refutation on `Ping-Ack` returns node to `alive` (respecting `dead_node_identity`).
- **Oscillation:** no more than C flips per window D before backoff; hysteresis deadband between suspect/refute thresholds enforced.
- **False rates:** false-positive and false-negative counters exposed via ids-observability; per-domain budgets configurable and enforced by test vectors.
- **Security:** all suspicion/confirmation datagrams ed25519-signed; replay nonces enforced; unsigned datagrams dropped.
- **Tests:** property-based (proptest), adversarial (chaos silence/delay/reordering), conformance (Chandra-Toueg classes, SWIM, phi), determinism, fuzz targets for swim + phi.

### 10. Remaining Uncertainties

- Final `Idstime` drift tolerance vs phi window sizing: how much clock drift the proprietary time basis absorbs before φ estimates distort (depends on ids-time phase-005 details not yet fixed).
- Whether ids-failure-detector internal SWIM/phi modules are later factored into `ids-swim` (#75) / `ids-phi-accrual` (#76) or remain internal; dependency ordering (crate 7 precedes crates 75/76) argues for internal implementation now, delegation later.
- Proven-failure evidence standard: indirect-prober quorum size k vs failure-domain STONITH via ids-stonith (#82) — to be coordinated with ids-membership (#8).
- GC-pause classifier thresholds (pause margin vs phi spike) need production telemetry from ids-observability before final values.
- Interaction with ids-identity (#4) RotatingNodeId: suspicion keyed to `StableNodeId` while RNI rotates; refutation across rotation windows needs care (idle-only rotation enforcement).

### 11. Engineering Decisions Summary

- **Compose SWIM + phi internally** in crate 7 rather than depend on later-numbered `ids-swim`/#75 and `ids-phi-accrual`/#76, preserving crate creation order; delegate later if factored out.
- **Carrier-agnostic datagram-only:** all detection traffic is opaque `Endpoint` payloads; the crate never opens sockets or interprets carrier topology.
- **ed25519-authenticated suspicion** with nonce + Idstime timestamps; optional chacha20poly1305/xchacha20poly1305 encryption; blake3/sha256 digests — nothing outside the allowed crypto set.
- **Idstime clock** for all timing; no wall-clock or HLC in detection paths.
- **Suspected ≠ proven:** suspicion prepares (avoid new writes), only proven failure triggers membership `failed` and recovery.
- **Oscillation control by default:** pending duration, hysteresis deadband, per-domain damping, flapper backoff — on by default, tunable.
- **Completeness/accuracy as contracts:** strong/weak variants exposed and selectable per dataset, acknowledging no perfect detector exists in an asynchronous, carrier-unreliable system.

# PHASE 008:

## Phase 008 — Create the ids-membership crate: Research Findings & Implementation Blueprint

**Research complete (30 targeted searches executed). No code written, no files modified. This document is the blueprint for implementation. Research only — no source modifications.**

---

### 1. Executive Summary

Phase 008 creates the **ids-membership** crate — authenticated, versioned joins/leaves coordinated with placement and ownership for the IDS distributed system. The crate manages the full node/H-unit/region membership lifecycle: states (candidate/validating/active/degraded/draining/failed/retired), H-unit membership, regional cluster membership, membership versioning, admission control, credential validation, capacity advertisement, health reporting, and removal procedures. All traffic rides `ids-carrier::Endpoint` (CarrierType + Vec<u8>) — carrier-agnostic by construction. Allowed crypto only: ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305.

**Core design decision:** A versioned membership view (monotonic epoch/version per change) held as a join-semilattice state that converges via SWIM-style gossip with phi-accrual suspicion, anti-entropy digest reconciliation (BLAKE3), and admission gated by ed25519-signed credentials validated against ids-identity (StableNodeId + RotatingNodeId). Nodes progress candidate → validating → active via admission control; removal transitions active → degraded → draining → (failed or retired). Membership versions coordinate with ids-placement and ids-topology so ownership changes follow admission, never precede it.

**Separate crate rule:** ids-membership is its own crate (not a folder inside ids-000-aa), depending on ids-000-aa, ids-carrier, ids-crypto, ids-identity, ids-time, ids-topology, ids-failure-detector. Consistent with CRATES.md dependency rule (all crates depend on ids-000-aa; ids-crypto does not).

**Carrier-agnostic:** Zero std::net, tokio::net, libp2p, IP, TCP, UDP, QUIC, HTTP, DNS, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular, VPN, or mesh. The trait `trait Membership` in ids-000-aa (join/leave/lifecycle) is implemented here; all datagrams flow through `ids-carrier::send_datagram`/`receive_datagram`.

---

### 2. Architecture Overview

The membership layer is the cluster's source of truth for "who is in, what state, and at what version." It sits above the carrier transport and below placement/routing/ownership.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    OWNERSHIP / PLACEMENT LAYER                  │
│            (ids-placement, ids-routing, ids-distribution)       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      ids-membership (THIS CRATE)                │
│  ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌────────────────────────┐ │
│  │ Admission    │ │ Versioned    │ │ Lifecycle state        │ │
│  │ Controller   │ │ Membership   │ │ machine (per node/HU)  │ │
│  └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └────────────────────────┘ │
│  ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌────────────────────────┐ │
│  │ Credential   │ │ Capacity     │ │ Health reporter        │ │
│  │ Validator    │ │ Advertisement│ │ (heartbeat/phi-accrual)│ │
│  └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └────────────────────────┘ │
│  ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌────────────────────────┐ │
│  │ Gossip       │ │ Anti-Entropy │ │ Removal / Drain        │ │
│  │ Dissemination│ │ Digest (BLAKE3│ │ Procedure (drain/retire│ │
│  │ (SWIM-style) │ │  Merkle-like)│ │  / decommission)       │ │
│  └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └────────────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│             ids-carrier · ids-000-aa · ids-crypto · ids-identity│
│             ids-time · ids-topology · ids-failure-detector       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Data flow — authenticated join:** prospective node sends `JoinRequest` (signed with its admission credential, carrying StableNodeId + RNI + capacity advertisement) via `ids-carrier::Endpoint`. Admission controller validates signature (ed25519) against ids-identity trust root, checks capacity quotas (ids-resource boundary), and if admitted increments the membership version and emits `MemberAdded(v)` gossiped via SWIM-style rumor mongering. The node transitions candidate → validating → active after a validating window (ids-time-based) and successful health checks.

**Data flow — graceful leave/drain:** node sends `LeaveIntent` (signed); state moves active → draining; placement evacuates replicas (coordinated with ids-placement/ids-replication); once drained and ownership transferred, state → retired; `MemberRemoved(v)` gossiped with incremented version. Failed nodes: phi-accrual suspicion → confirmed failure → state → failed → removal after a tombstone window.

**Membership versioning:** every join/leave/fail/retire bumps a monotonic `MembershipVersion` (u64, tied to ids-time commit ticks). Views are versioned snapshots; placement and routing consume the latest committed version so ownership never races membership.

---

### 3. Detailed Research Dimensions

#### 3.1 Node States and Lifecycle State Machine

States (from CRATES.md §8 / prompts.txt entry 8): candidate, validating, active, degraded, draining, failed, retired.

- **candidate:** node has sent JoinRequest, awaiting admission decision. No traffic served, no replicas assigned.
- **validating:** admitted provisionally; running health + credential re-check window (ids-time bounded). Limited read-only traffic possible; no writes.
- **active:** full member; serves reads/writes, holds replicas, eligible for placement/routing.
- **degraded:** member but below health threshold (phi-accrual suspicion, resource pressure); placement avoids new assignments; existing replicas retained.
- **draining:** graceful departure in progress; no new writes; replicas being evacuated to other members; coordination with ids-replication/ids-placement.
- **failed:** confirmed failure (phi threshold crossed + indirect probe consensus, or STONITH via ids-fencing-epoch/ids-stonith); replicas marked for recovery via ids-recovery.
- **retired:** permanently removed; `MemberRemoved` gossipped; tombstone retained for anti-entropy convergence window.

Transitions are versioned: each transition increments `MembershipVersion` and is gossipped. Invalid transitions rejected (e.g., active → retired without drain, candidate → active without admission).

Reference patterns: HashiCorp Serf member states (alive/suspect/left/failed), graceful leave intents (Serf internals), Kubernetes node drain/cordon (evacuation before removal), CockroachDB node decommission (replica streaming before exit), OR-Set add-wins semantics for concurrent join/leave of the same node identity.

#### 3.2 H-Unit Membership and Regional Cluster Membership

Hierarchy: Region → H-Unit → Node. A node belongs to exactly one H-unit; an H-unit belongs to exactly one region (failure-domain alignment with ids-topology §6). Regional cluster membership = the set of H-units (and their nodes) active in a region.

- H-unit membership: add/remove H-units at region scope; versioned per region; cross-region H-unit moves require mobility coordination (ids-mobility, out of scope for this crate).
- Regional membership view: per-region `RegionMembership { region_id: RegionId, h_units: Map<HUnitId, HUnitState>, version: MembershipVersion }`.
- Failure-domain awareness: placement constraints (power, facility, network, operator, jurisdiction) consulted before admitting a node so domain independence is preserved (ids-topology integration).
- No cross-region membership merge in this crate — regions are autonomous membership domains; cross-region consistency handled by ids-consistency/ids-replication.

Reference: AWS/Azure/GCP region-zone failure-domain hierarchy, Service Fabric hierarchical fault domains, Mesos region/zone domains, Simplyblock failure-domain placement contract.

#### 3.3 Membership Versioning

Every membership change (join, leave, fail, retire, degrade, drain, capacity update) produces a new `MembershipVersion` (monotonic u64). Views are immutable snapshots keyed by version.

- Version bump source: ids-time commit ticks or a local logical counter per region; never wall-clock for ordering.
- Placement/routing consume the version at decision time; a placement made against version N must not be applied after version N+k without re-validation (stale-view guard).
- Gossip carries `(version, view_delta)`; receivers apply only if `delta.version > local.version` (idempotent, out-of-order tolerant).
- Version gaps trigger anti-entropy pull (fetch missing view deltas).

Reference: Cassandra gossip vector clocks (generation, version), Raft configuration change joint consensus (USENIX ATC'14), OpenRaft adaptive membership (quorum overlap), Serf Lamport clock for join/leave ordering.

#### 3.4 Admission Control

Admission decides whether a candidate node joins. Gated on:

1. **Credential validation:** ed25519 signature over JoinRequest verified against ids-identity trust root (StableNodeId bound to provisioned admission key). Fail-closed on missing/invalid credential (AIStore node-join auth pattern: bootstrap trust problem — node not yet in cluster map, primary must authenticate before admitting).
2. **Capacity check:** node's advertised capacity (storage/CPU/memory/network/IOPS) vs. region quotas (ids-resource boundary); reject if region over-subscribed.
3. **Failure-domain check:** node's declared domain (power/facility/network/operator/jurisdiction) preserves domain independence (ids-topology).
4. **Duplicate identity:** StableNodeId/RNI not already an active member (OR-Set semantics: concurrent join of same identity = one wins, idempotent).

Admission output: `Admit(v)` or `Reject(v, reason)`, both versioned and gossipped. Rejected candidates remain candidate or are ejected.

#### 3.5 Credential Validation

- JoinRequest signed with node's admission credential (ed25519).
- Credential checked against ids-identity: StableNodeId + RNI validity window; revoked credentials → immediate reject (emergency revocation path, ids-identity).
- Replay protection: nonce + monotonic sequence per node (ids-time bounded window), rejecting stale joins.
- No TLS/PKI — carrier-agnostic; authentication is message-level (ed25519 over payload), transport-independent.

#### 3.6 Capacity Advertisement

Each active node periodically gossips `CapacityReport { node_id, storage_free, cpu, memory, network_bw, iops, timestamp }`. Consumed by ids-placement for capacity-aware placement and by admission for quota enforcement. Reports are versioned and bounded in size (no unbounded growth).

#### 3.7 Health Reporting

- Heartbeat: each node emits signed health beacons on the carrier; peers track last-heard (ids-time based).
- Phi-accrual suspicion (from ids-failure-detector): phi = -log10(1 - F(timeSinceLastHeartbeat)) computed from inter-arrival distribution; suspicion threshold configurable.
- Health states feed node state transitions: active → degraded (suspicion) → failed (confirmed).
- Health reports piggyback on gossip (SWIM: membership updates piggybacked on ping/ack).
- Local health awareness (Lifeguard, arxiv:1707.00788): node's own load/GC pause considered to reduce false positives.

#### 3.8 Removal Procedures

- **Graceful leave:** LeaveIntent → draining → evacuate replicas (coordinate ids-replication/ids-placement) → retired → MemberRemoved(v).
- **Failure removal:** phi threshold + indirect probe confirmation → failed → tombstone window → MemberRemoved(v) after recovery attempts exhausted (ids-recovery integration).
- **Forced retire:** operator-initiated retirement (security/compliance); bypasses drain if data already replicated elsewhere; immediate MemberRemoved(v).
- **Dead node identity:** dead node never returns with old identity; fresh ID assigned (ids-000-aa invariant `dead_node_identity`).

Reference: Cassandra nodetool decommission (stream data before exit), Kubernetes drain (cordon + evict), CockroachDB decommission, Serf leave intents.

#### 3.9 Gossip-Based Dissemination (SWIM-style)

Membership updates (joins, leaves, failures, capacity, health) disseminated via randomized peer probing + gossip payloads (SWIM, DSN 2002 paper; HashiCorp memberlist/Serf).

- Each round: probe one random peer (direct ping); piggyback membership view delta; indirect probes (ping-req via k others) on suspicion.
- Rumor mongering: new updates pushed hot; anti-entropy: periodic full-state sync with random peer for convergence.
- Eventually consistent: weakly consistent views converge logarithmically with group size; constant message load per member independent of group size.
- No central coordinator (IDS-B design principle: no global master).

#### 3.10 Anti-Entropy & Digest Reconciliation

Periodic full-state exchange with a random peer; Merkle-like digest (BLAKE3) over membership view to locate divergence in O(log n) rather than full-state transfer; ship only missing deltas. Tombstones retained for convergence window then GC'd at causal stability (all peers acked past a version).

Reference: Dynamo Merkle tree anti-entropy, ConflictSync digest-driven sync, scuttlebutt anti-entropy, OR-Set tombstone GC at causal stability.

#### 3.11 Coordination with Placement and Ownership

Membership is the input; placement is the consumer.

- Placement consumes the latest committed membership version; a node not in active state receives no new replicas.
- On member removal (drain/failed/retired), placement re-homes that node's partitions/replicas (ids-recovery).
- Ownership changes (partition ownership) only committed against a membership version where all owning nodes are active.
- Joint-consensus-style safety: membership change + ownership change must not create disjoint majorities (Raft joint consensus pattern).

---

### 4. Threat Model & Mitigations

| Threat | Mitigation |
|--------|-----------|
| Unauthenticated node joins (Sybil) | ed25519-signed JoinRequest validated against ids-identity trust root; fail-closed |
| Replay of old JoinRequest/LeaveIntent | Nonce + monotonic sequence; ids-time bounded replay window |
| Credential theft / compromise | Emergency revocation via ids-identity; revoked credentials rejected prospectively |
| False failure detection (healthy node marked failed) | Phi-accrual + indirect probe confirmation + Lifeguard local-health awareness; suspicion before failure |
| Premature removal (node evicted before data evacuated) | Drain state requires replica evacuation confirmation before retired |
| Stale placement against old membership version | Placement gates on committed membership version; stale-view guard |
| Gossip partition / divergent views | Versioned views + anti-entropy digest reconciliation; converge on heal |
| Membership version rollback / replay | Monotonic u64 versions; reject deltas with version <= local |
| Capacity advertisement DoS (inflated claims) | Quotas enforced by ids-resource; claims cross-checked against observed usage |
| Removal during active writes | Drain state blocks new writes; in-flight writes completed or aborted per consistency profile |
| Byzantine membership messages | Out of scope for Phase 008 (deferred to ids-byzantine); authenticated (ed25519) but not BFT |

| `ids-000-aa` | Canonical types (NodeId, RegionId, HUnitId, Endpoint, CarrierType, OpState, FailureDomain), sealed `trait Membership` contract, invariants (dead_node_identity, no_global_master, binary_completion), error contracts |
| `ids-carrier` | `Endpoint` (CarrierType + Vec<u8>), `send_datagram`/`receive_datagram` — sole traffic path |

- Credentials verified via ids-identity; health via ids-failure-detector; placement gated by membership version.

### 7. Key Algorithms & Data Structures

#### 7.1 Node State Machine

```
candidate --(admit)--> validating --(health pass + validating window)--> active
active        --(suspicion)--> degraded --(health recover)--> active
active        --(leave intent)--> draining --(evacuation complete)--> retired
active/degraded --(failure confirmed)--> failed --(tombstone window)--> removed
failed        --(recovery success)--> active   (re-join with fresh identity per invariant)
```

Guards: no active→retired without drain; no candidate→active without admission; transitions increment `MembershipVersion`.

#### 7.2 Versioned Membership View

```
MembershipView {
    version: MembershipVersion,        // monotonic u64
    nodes: Map<NodeId, NodeEntry>,
    h_units: Map<HUnitId, HUnitState>,
    regions: Map<RegionId, RegionMembership>,
    tombstones: Set<NodeId>,           // removed nodes within convergence window
}
ViewDelta { version, kind (Join/Leave/Fail/Retire/Degrade/Drain/Capacity), node_id, payload }
apply(local_view, delta): if delta.version > local.version { merge delta; local.version = delta.version }
```

Idempotent: applying the same delta twice is a no-op. Out-of-order tolerated: deltas with version <= local.version ignored; gaps trigger anti-entropy pull.

#### 7.3 SWIM Gossip Round

```
each round:
  1. pick random peer; send Ping(view_delta) + piggyback health
  2. on Ack: peer alive; merge peer's delta into local view
  3. on timeout: indirect probe → ping-req to k random peers about target
  4. if all indirect fail: mark suspect → gossip suspect → phi-accrual confirm → failed
```

Constant message load per member; failure detection expected constant time; dissemination latency O(log n).

#### 7.4 Phi-Accrual Suspicion

```
phi = -log10(1 - F(timeSinceLastHeartbeat))
F = CDF of inter-arrival times (normal approx, mean/std from history)
suspicion if phi > threshold; confirmation via indirect probes
```

#### 7.5 Anti-Entropy Digest Reconciliation

```
digest = BLAKE3(view_state)   // Merkle-like tree over node entries
exchange digests with random peer; equal → in sync
differ → descend tree to locate divergent entries → ship missing deltas
tombstone GC only at causal stability (all peers acked past version v)
```

#### 7.6 Admission Decision

```
admit(join_request):
  1. verify ed25519 sig over JoinRequest vs ids-identity trust root
  2. check nonce + sequence (replay guard)
  3. check StableNodeId/RNI not already active (OR-Set idempotency)
  4. check capacity vs region quota (ids-resource boundary)
  5. check failure-domain independence (ids-topology)
  6. if all pass: Admit(v) → version bump → NodeEntry(candidate) → validating
  7. else: Reject(v, reason)
```

#### 7.7 Graceful Drain

```
drain(node):
  state → draining; block new writes
  for each replica on node: stream to target (ids-replication), update placement (ids-placement)
  when all replicas evacuated: state → retired; MemberRemoved(v) gossipped
```

### 10. Remaining Uncertainties

1. **Validating window duration:** ids-time-based provisional window length for candidate→validating→active — workload-dependent, needs tuning.
2. **Phi-accrual threshold and inter-arrival distribution:** defaults are placeholders; production tuning required per deployment latency profile.
3. **Tombstone convergence window:** how long removed-node tombstones are retained before GC — trade-off between metadata bloat and resurrection risk; needs membership-aware causal stability.
4. **Persistence backend:** optional sled/view-store persistence vs. pure in-memory — durability requirements for multi-day storage undefined.
5. **Cross-region membership:** regions are autonomous; cross-region H-unit moves deferred to ids-mobility; coordination boundary not yet specified.
6. **Capacity claim verification:** advertised capacity cross-checked against observed usage — verification frequency and enforcement model undefined.
7. **Formal verification scope:** TLA+/PlusCal spec for state machine and version convergence; extent (core vs. gossip + anti-entropy) undecided.
8. **Wire format:** CBOR vs bincode for membership datagrams — schema evolution needs decision.

---

### 11. Engineering Decisions Summary

| Decision | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|
| Separate crate `ids-membership` (not subfolder) | CRATES.md separate-crate rule; clean dependency boundary |
| Versioned membership view (monotonic u64) | Idempotent, out-of-order-tolerant gossip; placement/routing gate on version |
| SWIM-style gossip + phi-accrual suspicion | Constant per-member load; expected constant detection time; logarithmic dissemination (DSN 2002; HashiCorp Serf/memberlist) |
| Admission gated by ed25519 credential vs ids-identity | Solves bootstrap trust problem (AIStore node-join auth pattern); fail-closed |
| Graceful drain before retire | Prevents data loss during removal (Cassandra decommission, K8s drain, CockroachDB) |
| OR-Set idempotent join/leave of same identity | Concurrent join/leave of same node identity converges (add-wins semantics) |
| Anti-entropy digest (BLAKE3 Merkle-like) | Locate divergence in O(log n) vs full-state (Dynamo, ConflictSync) |
| No RTT-bound timers; ids-time keyed | Correct over variable delays (carrier-agnostic) |
| Tombstone GC at causal stability (all-peer ack) | Prevents zombie resurrection |
| Reject op-based broadcast as primary | Requires reliable exactly-once causal broadcast — contradicts carrier-agnostic design |
| Allowed crypto only: ed25519/xchacha20poly1305/sha256/blake3/chacha20poly1305 | IDS crypto policy |

# PHASE 009:

## Phase 009 — Create the ids-placement crate (capacity-aware and failure-correlation-aware placement): Research Findings & Implementation Blueprint

**Research complete (30 targeted searches executed). No code written, no source modifications, no repository changes made. This document is the blueprint for implementation only.**

---\

### 1. Executive Summary

Phase 009 creates the **ids-placement** crate — the engine that decides where data lives in the IDS distributed store. It is a placement engine with hard constraints and soft objectives: capacity-aware placement (storage, CPU, memory, network, IOPS), failure-domain-aware placement (power, facility, network segment, operator, jurisdiction), failure-correlation-aware placement (avoid correlated loss), recovery-cost-aware placement, dynamic rebalancing, multiple placement strategies (hash, range, geographical, workload-aware, capacity-aware, hybrid), and hard constraint enforcement (residency, authorization, durability, capacity, data type, retention).

**Core engineering decisions (research-verified):**
- Placement is a **pure function of the data key/id, the cluster topology map, and the placement policy** — deterministic across replicas, no central allocator (CRUSH pattern: Weil et al., SC'06; avoids single point of failure and full-mapping bookkeeping).
- **Hard constraints are validated first, soft objectives rank candidates** (flexi-constraint/Constraint Relaxation pattern: arXiv 2507.13895; failed hard constraint = placement impossible, not degraded).
- **Failure-domain independence is failure-mode-specific** (MerceMay analysis): replicas spread across independent failure domains are independent only for the named mode; correlated-failure modeling uses a directed dependency graph/arborescence (COCOA/arXiv 1701.01539 DP algorithms) to avoid placing replicas on branches that a single failure can wipe out.
- **Capacity tracking is multi-dimensional** (storage, CPU, memory, network, IOPS); fit test is component-wise vector comparison (MerceMay bin-packing analysis): free cores alone do not imply room.
- **New crate `ids-placement`** per user's separate-crates rule; depends only on `ids-000-aa` (types/sealed contracts), `ids-topology` (failure domains), `ids-resource` (capacity metrics), `ids-membership` (node lifecycle), `ids-placement-policy` (dataset policy), `ids-consistency-profile` (durability), `ids-redundancy-mode` (replication vs erasure), `ids-crypto` (allowed crypto only: ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305).
- All traffic via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>`); zero `std::net`, `tokio::net`, libp2p, IP, TCP, UDP, QUIC, HTTP, DNS, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular, VPN, or mesh.

---\

### 2. Architecture Overview

The placement engine sits between the topology/membership layer and the distribution/replication layer. It is **not** a network protocol — it is a local, deterministic decision engine that produces `PlacementDecision` (canonical type in `ids-000-aa`) consumed by `ids-distribution`, `ids-replication`, `ids-routing`, and `ids-read`.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   CONSUMER LAYER                            │
│  ids-distribution · ids-replication · ids-routing · ids-read│
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│              Phase 009: ids-placement (NEW CRATE)           │
│  ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────────────┐   │
│  │  Strategy   │ │  Constraint │ │  Capacity & Failure │   │
│  │  Selector   │ │  Enforcer   │ │  Domain Model         │   │
│  └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘ └─────────────────────┘   │
│  ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────────────┐   │
│  │   Rebalancer│ │   Recovery  │ │  Objective Scorer   │   │
│  │  (dynamic)  │ │   Cost      │ │  (soft objectives)  │   │
│  └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘ └─────────────────────┘   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│            ids-topology · ids-resource · ids-membership     │
│   FailureDomain hierarchy · capacity metrics · node lifecycle│
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│             ids-000-aa (canonical types, sealed contracts)   │
│   PlacementDecision · FailureDomain · RegionId · HUnitId ... │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Data flow of a placement decision:**
1. Request arrives: dataset id, redundancy mode, consistency profile, data type, retention, size, replicas/fragments needed.
2. **Constraint Enforcer** filters candidate nodes/H-units/regions against hard constraints (residency, authorization, durability, capacity headroom, data type, retention) — any unsatisfiable hard constraint → placement rejected, never degraded.
3. **Strategy Selector** picks strategy per policy: hash (consistent/rendezvous), range (key-range partitioning), geographical (proximity to consumers), workload-aware (access patterns), capacity-aware (multi-dim bin fit), hybrid (weighted blend).
4. **Failure-Domain Model** applies failure-domain independence at the required level; failure-correlation model (directed dependency graph) rejects placements where one correlated failure could disable too many replicas (COCOA DP objective).
5. **Objective Scorer** ranks survivors on soft objectives: least-loaded, locality, cost, rebalance churn minimization.
6. `PlacementDecision` emitted: deterministic node set + rationale + version stamp; consumed by distribution/replication; rebalancer re-evaluates on topology/capacity/membership changes.

---\

### 3. Detailed Research Dimensions

#### 3.1 Placement Strategies (hash, range, geographical, workload-aware, capacity-aware, hybrid)

**Hash / rendezvous hashing (HRW):** each object key is hashed against the cluster map; destination is a pure function of key + map. When one node joins/leaves, only ~1/N of objects move (AIStore rebalance docs, NVIDIA). Deterministic, no central directory. Limitation: uniform random assignment is not capacity-optimal under heterogeneous hardware — skewed weights produce unbalanced placement (MerceMay analysis). Used as the baseline strategy; capacity-aware variants layer on top.

**Range partitioning:** key ranges map to partition owners; placement moves whole ranges. Good for ordered scans and range queries; split/merge coordinated by `ids-distribution`. Less flexible for failure-domain spreading than hash.

**Geographical:** data placed near consumers/regions to minimize latency (Volley, USENIX NSDI'10: automated geo-placement correlating access logs to latency/cost/capacity models; Iridium, SIGCOMM CCR: joint data+task placement over WAN). Constraints: inter-DC bandwidth cost, per-region capacity caps, data residency laws.

**Workload-aware:** placement tracks access patterns (hot/cold), moves hot data to high-performance nodes (H2DP, TPDS'19: heterogeneity-aware placement across HDD/SSD; workload-driven placement for IMDBMS, HPI: cost models over access traces). Coarse-grain workload-aware replication improves throughput 25–80% (NC State TR-2017-2). Dynamic re-evaluation needed as patterns change at runtime.

**Capacity-aware:** multi-dimensional bin fit — CPU, memory, storage, network, IOPS vectors; component-wise fit test (MerceMay bin-packing: fit = vector comparison, not scalar sum). Greedy/first-fit/best-fit heuristics; NP-hard, so production uses heuristics with bounded moves (consistent hashing with bounded loads, SODA'18 Karger et al.; Google Research blog, Mirrokni/Thorup/Zadimoghaddam 2018: capacity C = ceil((1+eps)·n/k), overflow cascades to next bin).

**Hybrid:** weighted blend of strategies per dataset policy (e.g., 70% capacity-aware + 30% geographical). Policy-driven weights from `ids-placement-policy`.

#### 3.2 Capacity Tracking (storage, CPU, memory, network, IOPS)

Each node/H-unit/region exposes a capacity vector: total, used, reserved, headroom per dimension. Placement fits only if every dimension of the placement's demand ≤ remaining headroom (component-wise comparison). Headroom reserved for recovery/rebalance bursts (Alauda Ceph planning: keep headroom for recovery, rebalance, upgrades; expand before near-full).

Metrics sources: `ids-resource` crate (storage/CPU/memory/network monitoring, latency/queue/utilization/health). IOPS and throughput per storage device (Cloudera infra metrics: Disk IOPS, throughput; AWS FSx Lustre: DiskIopsUtilization per OST). Capacity planning forecasts growth from historical usage (IBM Storage Insights: 7-day minimum history; forecast next year).

Capacity is tracked as **usable** not raw (replication/erasure reduce effective space; Alauda: usable capacity examples for 3-replica). Headroom percentages configurable (e.g., 80% warning threshold).

#### 3.3 Failure-Domain-Aware Placement & Failure-Correlation Modeling

**Failure domain hierarchy:** root → region → datacenter → room → row → rack → chassis → host → device (Ceph CRUSH bucket types; Lightbits: each server labeled with a set of FDs, minimum 3 non-intersecting FDs; replicas never share a domain). Correlated factors: physical proximity, shared power source, shared networking, shared operator/jurisdiction (Ceph docs).

**Correlated failure model:** directed dependency graph/arborescence — nodes = failure events, edge u→v means failure of u triggers v. Goal: choose placements where correlated failures disable as few replicas as possible. Two DP algorithms: O(n + ρ·log ρ) for single file on tree; polynomial when skew is constant (COCOA, arXiv 1701.01539). Causal failure model generalization: node v cascades when ≥ℓ(v) incoming neighbors failed (arXiv 1503.02654).

**Domain independence is failure-mode-specific:** replicas on separate racks are independent against rack power loss but not against data-center-wide events (MerceMay). Effective replication factor = mode-specific. Placement must name the failure mode it protects against.

**Domain independence verification (IDS-topology integration):** power-domain separation, network-segment separation, operator separation, jurisdiction separation — verified before placement accepted.

#### 3.4 Recovery-Cost-Aware Placement

When a node dies, every object it held must be re-replicated; the replacement must not land in a domain already occupied by surviving replicas (MerceMay: rebuild traffic concentrates across rack boundary under HDFS 2+1). Rebuild traffic is the constraint that most often forces placement changes.

Recovery-cost-aware placement: pre-compute rebuild fan-in/fan-out per candidate; prefer placements where recovery can be served from local/cheap helpers (Google Colossus RS(6,3), Facebook RS(10,4), Azure RS(12,4); USENIX FAST'21 correlated SSD failure study). Recovery bandwidth cost modeled per failure domain (intra-cluster vs inter-cluster cost ratio; GRBC model for clustered regenerating codes). Balanced recovery load distribution algorithm (USENIX ATC'23 Shan: pick target nodes with used storage within (1+ε) of min, minimizing recovery load edge weights).

#### 3.5 Hard Constraint Enforcement (residency, authorization, durability, capacity, data type, retention)

Hard constraints remove candidates entirely (Cloudflare placement: regions/jurisdiction constraints; AWS Well-Architected data residency: geographic restrictions under GDPR Chapter V). Constraint satisfaction vs optimization separation: feasible-configs generation then Pareto selection (IEEE CLOUD 2018: hard+soft constraints, multiple conflicting objectives).

- **Residency / jurisdiction:** data may only be stored in permitted regions/countries (Google Spanner data residency: per-placement region selection; Northflank: residency attribute assigned at creation, propagated end-to-end).
- **Authorization:** placement only on nodes/operators authorized for the dataset (data-use policy, ownership policy).
- **Durability:** minimum replicas/fragments, erasure (n,k), required placement domains (HDFS EC policies: RS-6-3 default, RS-10-4; oneuptime durability comparison: topology + recovery window matter more than ratio).
- **Capacity:** component-wise fit test; headroom reservation.
- **Data type:** storage-type policies (HDFS storage types: SSD vs HDD fallback paths).
- **Retention:** retention period + legal hold interact with placement (WORM/immutable; retention-aware zone placement, RetainZ USENIX: group checkpoints retiring together for zone reclamation).

Failed hard constraint → placement rejected (never silently degraded). Soft objectives then rank feasible candidates.

#### 3.6 Dynamic Rebalancing

Triggered by topology change (node join/leave/maintenance/decommission), capacity skew, or workload shift. AIStore global rebalance: decentralized, each target recomputes HRW destination for local objects, moves only objects whose owner changed (~1/N of objects per single node change). Trigger conditions: load imbalance thresholds, cooldown periods, min-load thresholds (GreptimeDB region balancer: acceptable_load_ratio, min_load_threshold, cooldown). Rebalance vs resilver distinction (AIStore): rebalance = placement correction; resilver = redundancy restoration after failure.

Rebalance scope: full vs partial (bounded by cost budget; StorPool balancer scores and constraint violations). Serves reads during migration (AIStore). Migration bounded to avoid thundering herd (ids-fault integration: circuit breakers, bulkheads, backpressure).

---\

### 4. Threat Model & Mitigations

|| Threat | Mitigation ||
||--------|-----------|-------------|
| Correlated failure wipes multiple replicas | Failure-domain independence at named level; correlation graph (arborescence) checked before placement; DP-optimal replica spread |
| Placement on over-capacity node | Component-wise capacity fit test; headroom reservation; reject before placement |
| Hard constraint silently violated | Hard constraints validated first; unsatisfiable = reject, never degrade; audit log of rejections |
| Rebalance churn / thundering herd | Bounded rebalance budget, cooldown windows, ~1/N move fraction (AIStore), circuit-breaker gating via ids-fault |
| Deterministic placement diverges across replicas | Pure function of key+map+policy; same inputs → same decision on every replica; version-stamped decisions |
| Recovery overloads surviving nodes | Recovery-cost-aware target selection; bounded recovery fan-in; capacity-bounded recovery (ids-recovery) |
| Placement leaks data to unauthorized region | Residency/authorization constraints checked before any candidate scored; jurisdiction filtering (Cloudflare pattern) |
| Correlated power/network failure across "independent" domains | Domain independence verification (power, network segment, operator, jurisdiction) from ids-topology |

- `ids-replication` uses placement output to place replicas/fragments across failure domains.

- Carrier-agnostic: placement never touches `std::net`/`tokio::net`/libp2p; all traffic via `ids-carrier::Endpoint`.

### 7. Key Algorithms & Data Structures

#### 7.1 Placement decision pipeline
```
decide(req: PlacementRequest) -> PlacementDecision:
  candidates = all eligible nodes (membership: active/degraded only)
  candidates = constraint_enforcer.filter(candidates, req.hard_constraints)
  if candidates.empty(): return Rejected(unsatisfiable_constraints)
  survivors = strategy_selector.select(req, candidates)   // per-strategy candidate set
  ranked = objective_scorer.rank(survivors, req.soft_objectives)
  failure_domain.verify_independence(ranked.top_k, req.required_domains)
  correlation_graph.check(ranked.top_k, req.correlation_model)
  return PlacementDecision(ranked.best, rationale, version)
```

#### 7.2 Component-wise capacity fit test
```
fit(node, demand) = ∀ d ∈ {storage, cpu, memory, network, iops}:
                    node.remaining[d] >= demand[d]
```

#### 7.3 Failure-domain independence (arborescence DP, COCOA-style)
- Failure model = directed rooted tree/arborescence; edge u→v: failure of u triggers v.
- Objective: place ρ replicas on leaves minimizing max replicas disabled by any single failure event.
- DP: O(n + ρ·log ρ) for single file; polynomial when replica-count skew is constant.

#### 7.4 Consistent hashing with bounded loads
- Hash key and nodes to unit circle; key → first bin clockwise; if full, cascade to next non-full bin.
- Bin capacity C = ceil((1+eps)·n/k); expected moves within factor of optimum on add/remove.

#### 7.5 Rebalance trigger
```
rebalance if: max_util − min_util > imbalance_threshold
              OR node join/leave/maintenance/decommission
              OR workload skew exceeds threshold
bounded by: move_fraction ≤ budget, cooldown between runs
```

### 9. Measurable Acceptance Criteria

|| # | Criterion | Measurement ||
||---|-----------|-------------|
|| AC-009.1 | Deterministic placement | Same key+map+policy → identical `PlacementDecision` on every replica (property test, 100k iterations) |
|| AC-009.2 | Hard constraint rejection | Unsatisfiable hard constraint → placement rejected, never silently degraded (adversarial test) |
|| AC-009.3 | Failure-domain independence | Replicas placed across distinct failure domains at the required level; no two replicas share a domain that fails together (unit + adversarial) |
|| AC-009.4 | Correlated-failure avoidance | Placement minimizes replicas disabled by any single correlated failure event (DP-optimal on tree model) |
|| AC-009.5 | Capacity fit (multi-dimensional) | Placement accepted iff every capacity dimension (storage/CPU/memory/network/IOPS) fits (component-wise test) |
|| AC-009.6 | Capacity-aware bin packing | Heterogeneous nodes filled proportionally to capacity; no overload under skew (bench) |
|| AC-009.7 | Recovery-cost-aware | Recovery targets minimize rebuild fan-in/fan-out and cross-domain bandwidth (cost model bench) |
|| AC-009.8 | Dynamic rebalancing | Triggered on topology/capacity/workload change; ~1/N objects move per single-node change; bounded by budget + cooldown |
|| AC-009.9 | Strategy correctness | Each strategy (hash/range/geographical/workload/capacity/hybrid) produces valid placements per its contract (unit tests) |
|| AC-009.10 | Carrier agnosticism | Compiles and behaves identically with zero `std::net`/`tokio::net`/libp2p/TCP/UDP/QUIC/HTTP/DNS/Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/cellular/VPN/mesh dependencies |
|| AC-009.11 | Allowed crypto only | Only ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305 used; no other crypto primitives |
|| AC-009.12 | Adversarial tests pass | Correlated failure, overload, skew, constraint-conflict tests all fail-safe |

### 10. Remaining Uncertainties

1. **Strategy weighting for hybrid:** exact weight blend per dataset class (capacity vs geography vs workload) is workload-dependent; defaults are placeholders pending measurement.
2. **Correlation graph source:** static config, learned from failure history, or operator-declared — all must be supported behind one interface; no decision yet.
3. **Capacity refresh cadence:** how often capacity vectors are updated from `ids-resource`; staleness tolerance for placement decisions undefined.
4. **Rebalance cost model:** exact move-cost formula (bytes × distance × priority) and budget defaults need workload tuning.
5. **Placement decision versioning:** how `PlacementDecision` versions interact with `ids-partition-map` versioning and migration tracking is undefined.
6. **Signed placement decisions:** whether `PlacementDecision` carries an ed25519 signature (via `ids-crypto`) for audit is a product decision, not a research conclusion.
7. **Geographical proximity data source:** consumer location / region latency data source undefined; geographical strategy needs an input interface.
8. **Formal verification scope:** TLA+/PlusCal spec for placement invariants (domain independence, constraint rejection) deferred to `ids-doc`.

---\

### 11. Engineering Decisions Summary

|| Decision | Rationale ||
||----------|-----------|-------------|
|| Pure function of key+map+policy (CRUSH pattern) | Deterministic, no central allocator, no full-mapping bookkeeping (Weil et al. SC'06; AIStore HRW) |
|| Hard constraints first, soft objectives rank | Failed hard constraint = reject, never degrade (Constraint Relaxation pattern, arXiv 2507.13895) |
|| Multi-dimensional component-wise capacity fit | Free cores alone don't imply room; vector comparison per dimension (MerceMay bin-packing analysis) |
|| Failure-domain independence is failure-mode-specific | Replicas on separate racks are independent against rack power loss, not DC-wide events (MerceMay) |
|| Correlation graph via arborescence DP | Minimize replicas disabled by one correlated failure; O(n + ρ·log ρ) (COCOA, arXiv 1701.01539) |
|| Recovery-cost-aware target selection | Rebuild traffic is the constraint that most often forces placement changes (MerceMay) |
|| Rebalance ~1/N objects per node change | Decentralized, bounded churn (AIStore global rebalance) |
|| New `ids-placement` crate | User's separate-crates rule; clean dependency boundary; keeps existing crates focused |
|| Allowed crypto only | ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305; nothing else |
|| Carrier-agnostic via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` | No `std::net`/`tokio::net`/libp2p/TCP/UDP/QUIC/HTTP/DNS/Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/cellular/VPN/mesh |

# PHASE 010:

## Phase 010 — Create the ids-distribution crate (data partitioning and distribution): Research Findings & Implementation Blueprint

**Research complete (30 targeted searches executed). No code written, no source modifications, no repository changes made. This document is the blueprint for implementation only.**

---

### 1. Executive Summary

Phase 010 creates the **ids-distribution** crate — the engine that divides a dataset into independently placeable units (partitions) and tracks their distribution across nodes, H-units, and regions. It owns partition boundaries, key-to-partition mapping, split/merge behavior, partition metadata, partition ownership, and logical-to-physical mapping stability during migration. The crate sits between `ids-placement` (which decides *where* a unit goes) and `ids-replication`/`ids-routing`/`ids-read` (which consume placement output); it is the layer that turns a logical dataset into a set of placeable, movable partition objects.

**Core engineering decisions (research-verified):**

- **Partition as the unit of distribution:** a dataset is divided into partitions; each partition is independently placeable and owns a disjoint key-range or hash-bucket range. Consistent with Dynamo, Bigtable tablets, TiKV regions, CockroachDB ranges, Couchbase vBuckets, MongoDB chunks — all treat a bounded unit as the atom of placement.
- **Logical → physical indirection via a versioned partition map:** logical partition boundaries are stable identities; physical location (node/H-unit/region) is a separate, versioned mapping that changes on split/merge/move without changing the logical partition id. Matches Couchbase vBucket map (doc ID → vBucket → server) and NodeDB vShards (data hashed to vShard → catalog → owner). Enables live migration and rebalancing without client-visible key remapping.
- **Key mapping strategies:** consistent/rendezvous hashing (uniform spread, ~1/N remap on membership change), range partitioning (ordered scans, contiguous [start,end) ranges like Bigtable/TiKV/CockroachDB), and directory-based mapping (explicit boundary table for residency/uneven shards). Strategy chosen per dataset policy, not globally.
- **Split/merge with hysteresis:** size-triggered split when a partition exceeds target S; merge when adjacent partitions stay below ~0.5×S for a sustained period; hysteresis (split at >1.5×S, merge <0.5×S) prevents split/merge thrash. Split point sampled at key median; daughters get roughly equal ranges/load. Atomic publication: prepare children from a consistent snapshot, capture post-snapshot writes, atomically publish new map epoch, fence old owner, retain redirect/rollback metadata until old routers drain, delete parent only after no reader references it. Merge is the reverse with one publication point.
- **Single authoritative owner at a time:** each partition has one write owner; ownership transfer fences the old owner, transfers a consistent snapshot plus in-flight mutation replay, then atomically publishes the new owner (LEAP-style owner table transfer; shard-growth handoff pattern). Reads served during migration via redirect to both source and target during cutover.
- **Logical-to-physical mapping stability during migration:** partition logical id never changes across a move; only the catalog entry (physical location) is updated atomically. Tombstone/redirect retained briefly so in-flight requests resolve. No key remapping on the client side.
- **New crate `ids-distribution`** per user's separate-crates rule; depends only on `ids-000-aa` (types/sealed contracts), `ids-placement` (placement decisions), `ids-topology` (failure domains), `ids-membership` (node lifecycle), `ids-placement-policy`, `ids-consistency-profile`, `ids-redundancy-mode`, `ids-crypto` (allowed crypto only: ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305), `ids-partition-map` (logical→physical map crate, sibling).
- All traffic via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>`); zero `std::net`, `tokio::net`, libp2p, IP, TCP, UDP, QUIC, HTTP, DNS, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular, VPN, or mesh.

---

### 2. Architecture Overview

The distribution crate sits between the placement layer and the replication/routing/read layer. It is **not** a network protocol — it is a local, deterministic partition lifecycle engine that produces partition metadata, map epochs, and ownership records consumed by `ids-replication`, `ids-routing`, `ids-read`, and `ids-query`.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    CONSUMER LAYER                                    │
│  ids-replication · ids-routing · ids-read · ids-query · ids-write   │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│              Phase 010: ids-distribution (NEW CRATE)                 │
│  ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │   Partition  │ │  Key Mapping │ │   Partition Metadata        │  │
│  │   Boundaries │ │  Resolver    │ │   (epoch, version, owner)   │  │
│  └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────────────────┘  │
│  ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  Split/Merge │ │   Ownership  │ │ Logical→Physical Stability  │  │
│  │   Controller │ │  Transfer    │ │   During Migration          │  │
│  └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────────────────┘  │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│             ids-placement · ids-partition-map · ids-topology         │
│   PlacementDecision · logical↔physical map · failure domains         │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│             ids-000-aa (canonical types, sealed contracts)           │
│   PartitionId · DatasetId · NodeId · RegionId · HUnitId · ...        │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Data flow of partition lifecycle:**

1. Dataset created with redundancy mode + consistency profile → `ids-placement-policy` defines replica/fragment counts and required domains → `ids-distribution` creates initial partition(s) spanning the full keyspace, records partition metadata (boundaries, epoch 1, version 1, owner unset).
2. Write/read arrives keyed by `RecordId`/`DatasetId` → Key Mapping Resolver hashes/ranges the key → identifies target partition → consults versioned partition map → resolves owning node/H-unit/region → `ids-routing` directs the request.
3. Partition grows beyond split threshold → Split Controller selects median split key from consistent snapshot → creates daughter partitions [start, mid) and [mid, end) → assigns new partition ids → captures writes after snapshot via dual-application/log → brings daughters to cutover frontier → atomically publishes new map epoch → fences parent writes → retains redirect until old routers drain → deletes parent state.
4. Adjacent partitions below merge threshold → Merge Controller validates adjacency + same owner domain → combines into one partition → single publication point preserves both children through the cutover.
5. Rebalance/move triggered by `ids-placement` or `ids-selfreorg`/`ids-mobility` → Ownership Transfer: fence old owner, transfer consistent snapshot + mutation replay, atomically publish new owner in map, retain redirect/rollback until drain complete → logical partition id unchanged, only physical location updated.
6. Partition metadata (epoch, version, boundaries, owner, location, checksums) persisted via `ids-partition-map`; consumers subscribe to map version changes.

---

### 3. Detailed Research Dimensions

#### 3.1 Partition Boundaries & Key Mapping (hash, range, directory)

**Consistent/rendezvous hashing:** keys and nodes mapped onto a hash ring/space; a key resolves to the first node clockwise (consistent hashing) or the highest-weight node (rendezvous/HRW). Adding/removing one node remaps only ~1/N of keys (Karger et al., MIT; Dynamo paper). Uniform spread, no hot spots under random keys, no central directory. Limitation: range scans inefficient (keys scattered); heterogeneous capacity needs virtual nodes or weighted HRW. Couchbase uses CRC32(doc ID) → 1024 fixed vBuckets → vBucket map → server; uniform 1/1024 share per vBucket. Used as baseline for equality lookups.

**Range partitioning:** contiguous key ranges [start_key, end_key) map to partition owners; Bigtable tablets, TiKV regions, CockroachDB ranges, HBase regions all use this. Good for ordered/range scans and prefix queries; range queries hit only relevant partitions. Risk: sequential keys (timestamps, monotonically increasing IDs) concentrate writes on the last range → hot spots; mitigated by hashed shard keys or key prefix salting. Split/merge natural (adjacent ranges). Needs metadata management of boundaries (Bigtable METADATA hierarchy, CockroachDB meta1→meta2→ranges).

**Directory/virtual-bucket mapping:** fixed logical bucket count (e.g., 1024 vBuckets or 4096 logical shards as in Aerospike), hashed from key, then a versioned table maps each bucket to a physical owner. Indirection decouples logical partition identity from physical location → live migration without remapping keys (Couchbase, NodeDB vShards). Supports residency, uneven shards, tenant moves. Price: metadata dependency — routers need a strongly managed, versioned map and safe cache invalidation on move begin/end. Best for IDS: combine logical bucket/virtual-partition layer with per-bucket versioned ownership.

**Hybrid per dataset:** policy selects strategy — hash for uniform equality workloads, range for scan-heavy workloads, directory for residency/uneven/tenant-isolated datasets.

#### 3.2 Split/Merge Behavior

**Split triggers:** size-based (partition exceeds target S, e.g. tens of MB–tens of GB depending on engine — Bigtable 100–200 MB tablets, MongoDB 64 MB chunks, TiKV 96 MB regions, YugabyteDB 512 MB low phase / 10 GB high phase / 100 GB force split) and load-based (QPS/write-throughput exceeds threshold even below size target, preempting hot ranges). Hysteresis: split at >1.5×S, merge only below ~0.5×S to prevent split/merge thrash ("region explosion" from poor boundaries).

**Split algorithm:** sample key distribution within parent → choose median split key → create daughters [start, mid) and [mid, end) with roughly equal key ranges/load → assign new partition ids → record parent→children lineage in metadata.

**Merge triggers:** adjacent partitions both below ~0.5×S and low load for sustained period; small adjacent regions merged (TiKV max-merge-region-size/keys, split-merge-interval cooldown; newly split regions not merged immediately).

**Atomic publication (both split and merge):**
1. Choose boundary + durable split/merge identity.
2. Create child state from consistent parent snapshot.
3. Capture writes after snapshot via log or dual-application protocol.
4. Bring children to parent's cutover frontier.
5. Atomically publish new map/epoch and fence parent writes.
6. Retain redirect + rollback metadata until old routers drain.
7. Delete obsolete parent state only after no reader or rollback path references it.

Merge is the reverse: one publication point preserves both children through cutover.

#### 3.3 Partition Metadata

Each partition carries: partition id (stable logical identity), dataset id, key boundaries [start_key, end_key) or hash-bucket set, epoch (version bumped on split/merge/owner change), version (data-generation counter), owning node/H-unit/region, replica/fragment placement set, redundancy mode, consistency profile, size, key count, creation time, last-split/merge timestamp, checksums, lineage (parent id for split children, children ids for merged parent), redirect/rollback pointers during migration.

Metadata is versioned: every split/merge/owner change publishes a new map epoch; consumers cache and invalidate on epoch change. Partition map is the authoritative source of logical→physical mapping (see `ids-partition-map` crate).

#### 3.4 Distribution Across Nodes/H-units/Regions

Distribution = placement + replication + ownership. `ids-placement` produces `PlacementDecision` (node/H-unit/region set per partition); `ids-distribution` records the decision in the partition map as the physical location; `ids-replication` places replicas/fragments across failure domains per `ids-redundancy-mode`; `ids-routing` resolves requests to the owning replica.

Failure-domain awareness (from `ids-topology`): replicas/fragments of one partition spread across independent failure domains (power, facility, network segment, operator, jurisdiction) so one correlated failure disables at most one replica. Correlated-failure modeling (arborescence/dependency DAG DP, COCOA) checks placement before acceptance.

Capacity awareness (from `ids-resource`): component-wise fit test (storage/CPU/memory/network/IOPS vectors); headroom reserved for recovery/rebalance bursts.

#### 3.5 Partition Ownership

Each partition has exactly one write owner (leader/primary) at any time; replicas/fragments are followers/secondaries. Ownership is recorded in the partition map with an epoch; changes require atomic publication.

**Ownership transfer protocol** (LEAP-style + shard-growth handoff):
1. Requester (or controller) initiates transfer; partitioner/old owner identified from map.
2. Old owner fenced: no new writes accepted after fence point; in-flight writes drained.
3. Consistent snapshot transferred to new owner; mutations after snapshot replayed (idempotent reapplication keyed by OpRef/OrderingPos).
4. Catch-up verified; cutover boundary established under controlled handoff.
5. New map epoch published atomically: new owner authoritative, old owner drops the partition.
6. Redirect/rollback retained until old routers/clients drain; reads may consult both source and target during cutover.

No two nodes own the same partition concurrently (split-brain prevented by single-epoch map + fencing, coordinated with `ids-lease`/`ids-byzantine` for fencing epochs).

#### 3.6 Logical-to-Physical Mapping Stability During Migration

The logical partition id is immutable across moves; only the catalog entry (physical node/H-unit/region) changes. Indirection (vBucket/vShard pattern) means clients key on logical partition id, resolve via current map, and never rehash keys on topology change. During migration: writes fenced to old owner until cutover; target catches up via snapshot+replay; new epoch published; old owner retains redirect briefly; in-flight requests resolved through redirect. Cutover verified before old state deleted. This preserves logical identity, access policy, and history during region/node moves (integrates with `ids-mobility`).

#### 3.7 Partition-Level Integrity & Checksums

Each partition's metadata includes per-partition checksums (blake3/sha256 over boundaries + content digest) verified at split/merge/move; integration with `ids-integrity` for end-to-end checksums, Merkle trees per partition, replica audits, silent bit-rot detection. Partition-level integrity verification before ownership transfer acceptance.

---

### 4. Threat Model & Mitigations

|| Threat | Mitigation ||
||--------|-----------|-------------|
| Split point chosen in sparse key region → uneven daughters, repeated splits, "partition explosion" | Sample key distribution; median split key; hysteresis (split >1.5×S, merge <0.5×S); reject boundaries violating min/max size |
| Split/merge thrash under oscillating load | Hysteresis + cooldown window (`split-merge-interval`); minimum time between split/merge on same partition |
| Two owners for one partition (split-brain) | Single authoritative epoch in versioned map; fencing before transfer; atomic publication; `ids-lease`/`ids-byzantine` fencing epochs |
| Logical partition id changes on move → client remapping | Immutable logical id; indirection via versioned partition map; only physical location updated |
| Data loss during split/merge (writes after snapshot lost) | Dual-application/log capture post-snapshot writes; replay to children; catch-up to frontier before cutover |
| Over-capacity partition after split/merge | Component-wise capacity fit test per daughter/merged partition via `ids-resource`; reject if any dimension exceeds headroom |
| Correlated failure disables multiple replicas of one partition | Failure-domain independence at named level; correlation-graph DP check before placement; replicas across independent domains |
| Stale router cache routes to old owner after move | Redirect retained until drain; map epoch bump invalidates caches; clients re-resolve on redirect/moved response |
| Unauthorized region receives partition | Residency/jurisdiction constraints from `ids-placement-policy` checked before any placement; `ids-security` authorization |
| Metadata corruption (map/epoch) | Checksums (blake3/sha256) on every metadata payload; versioned map with fail-closed on mismatch; multiple historical snapshots |
| Rebalance churn / thundering herd on membership change | Bounded move fraction (~1/N per node change, AIStore HRW); cooldown windows; `ids-fault` circuit-breaker/bulkhead gating |

---

### 5. Integration with Existing Crates

|| Crate | Role in Phase 010 ||
||-------|-------------------|-------------------|
| `ids-000-aa` | Canonical types: `PartitionId`, `DatasetId`, `NodeId`, `RegionId`, `HUnitId`, `RecordId`, `OpRef`, `OrderingPos`, `PlacementDecision`, `RedundancyMode`, `ConsistencyProfile`, `FailureDomain`; sealed `trait Distribution` contract |
| `ids-placement` | Produces `PlacementDecision` (where each partition goes); consumed as input to partition placement |
| `ids-partition-map` | Authoritative logical→physical partition map; versioned epochs; owned jointly with `ids-distribution` |
| `ids-topology` | FailureDomain hierarchy; domain independence verification; correlated-failure model |
| `ids-membership` | Node states; only active/degraded nodes eligible as partition owners |
| `ids-placement-policy` | Dataset policy: replica/fragment counts, required domains, redundancy mode |
| `ids-consistency-profile` | Durability/acknowledgement semantics per profile (affects partition replica requirements) |
| `ids-redundancy-mode` | Full replication vs erasure coding per dataset (determines fragment count per partition) |
| `ids-carrier` | `Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>`) — partition map references endpoints; distribution never touches carriers directly |
| `ids-crypto` | Allowed crypto only: ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305 (signed partition metadata/audit) |
| `ids-integrity` | Per-partition checksums, Merkle trees, integrity verification at split/merge/move |
| `ids-mobility` / `ids-selfreorg` | Drive region/node moves and placement revision; consume ownership-transfer protocol |

**Integration points:**
- `ids-placement` → `ids-distribution`: placement decisions become physical locations in the partition map.
- `ids-replication` consumes partition ownership + placement to place replicas/fragments.
- `ids-routing` resolves requests to partition owner using the versioned map.
- `ids-read`/`ids-write` target partitions by key → map → owner.
- `ids-query` decomposes queries across partitions using partition boundaries + ownership metadata.
- `ids-mobility`/`ids-selfreorg` trigger ownership transfer + map epoch changes.
- Carrier-agnostic: distribution never imports `std::net`/`tokio::net`/libp2p; all traffic via `ids-carrier::Endpoint`.

**Why ~120–200 files:** one file per responsibility — partition lifecycle + state machine, 3 key-mapping strategies + selector, metadata + map epoch + checksums, split/merge controller + plans + atomic publish + hysteresis + cooldown, ownership + transfer + fence + cutover + redirect + drain, distribution + replica set + domain spread, migration + snapshot transfer + catch-up + logical stability, integrity + Merkle, fuzzing, property/integration/adversarial/determinism/chaos tests, benchmarks, formal spec, docs, test vectors. No stubs.

---

### 7. Key Algorithms & Data Structures

#### 7.1 Partition lifecycle state machine
```
creating → active → {splitting | merging | moving | retired}
active --(split trigger)--> splitting --(atomic publish)--> active (daughters) + retired (parent)
active --(merge trigger)--> merging --(atomic publish)--> active (merged) + retired (children)
active --(move trigger)--> moving --(cutover publish)--> active (new owner) + retired (old owner)
```

#### 7.2 Key mapping resolution
```
resolve(key: RecordId, dataset: DatasetId) -> PartitionId:
  strategy = mapping_selector(dataset.policy)   // hash / range / directory
  bucket = strategy.hash_or_range(key)          // hash bucket or range index
  return partition_map.lookup(dataset, bucket, current_epoch)
```
Hash: consistent/rendezvous (~1/N remap on membership change). Range: ordered [start,end) boundary lookup. Directory: versioned bucket→owner table (indirection, no client remapping).

#### 7.3 Split with hysteresis
```
split_candidate(partition):
  if partition.size > 1.5 × S: return Split
  if partition.size < 0.5 × S and low_load(sustained): return Merge candidate
  else: NoOp
split_point = median_key(partition.keys, sample)
daughters = [start, split_point), [split_point, end)
```

#### 7.4 Atomic publication (split/merge/move)
```
publish(epoch': MapEpoch):
  1. prepare children/target from consistent snapshot
  2. capture post-snapshot writes (log/dual-application)
  3. bring to cutover frontier
  4. atomically publish map epoch', fence old owner
  5. retain redirect/rollback until drain
  6. delete obsolete state after no reader references it
```

#### 7.5 Ownership transfer
```
transfer(partition, new_owner):
  fence(old_owner)                      // no new writes
  snapshot = consistent_snapshot(old_owner)
  replay(mutations_after_snapshot)      // idempotent, keyed by OpRef/OrderingPos
  verify_catchup(target = frontier)
  publish_map_epoch(new_owner)          // atomic, single publication
  retain_redirect(old_owner) until drain
  old_owner.drops(partition)
```

#### 7.6 Per-partition checksum
```
checksum(partition) = blake3(boundaries || content_digest || epoch || owner)
```
Verified at split/merge/move; integrated with `ids-integrity` Merkle trees.

### 9. Measurable Acceptance Criteria

|| # | Criterion | Measurement ||
||---|-----------|-------------|
|| AC-010.1 | Deterministic partitioning | Same dataset+key+map+policy → identical partition assignment on every replica (property test, 100k iterations) |
|| AC-010.2 | Logical id stability | Partition logical id immutable across split/merge/move; only physical location changes (migration test) |
|| AC-010.3 | Single write owner | Exactly one owner per partition at any epoch; no split-brain (ownership transfer test + adversarial) |
|| AC-010.4 | Split correctness | Daughters partition [start,mid) ∪ [mid,end) = parent range; no gaps/overlaps (unit + property) |
|| AC-010.5 | Merge correctness | Merged partition = union of adjacent children; both children preserved through one publication point (unit + adversarial) |
|| AC-010.6 | Hysteresis | No split/merge oscillation: split >1.5×S, merge <0.5×S, cooldown enforced (chaos/load-oscillation test) |
|| AC-010.7 | Atomic publication | Map epoch publication is atomic; old owner fenced before new owner authoritative (transfer test) |
|| AC-010.8 | Key mapping coverage | Every key resolves to exactly one partition; no key unmapped (mapping test, all strategies) |
|| AC-010.9 | Distribution across domains | Partition replicas/fragments spread across independent failure domains (domain-independence test) |
|| AC-010.10 | Capacity fit | Partition accepted only if every capacity dimension fits (component-wise test via ids-resource) |
|| AC-010.11 | Integrity verification | Per-partition checksum verified at split/merge/move; mismatch → reject transfer (integrity test) |
|| AC-010.12 | Cache invalidation | Map epoch bump invalidates router caches; stale reads get redirect/moved (migration test) |
|| AC-010.13 | Carrier agnosticism | Compiles/behaves identically with zero std::net/tokio::net/libp2p/TCP/UDP/QUIC/HTTP/DNS/Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/cellular/VPN/mesh deps |
|| AC-010.14 | Allowed crypto only | Only ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305 used; nothing else |
|| AC-010.15 | Adversarial tests pass | Split-brain, sparse boundaries, thrash, stale-cache, corruption tests all fail-safe |

### 10. Remaining Uncertainties

1. **Initial partition count per dataset:** fixed logical bucket count (e.g., 1024/4096) vs. dynamic single-starting-partition that auto-splits — no decision yet; both supported behind mapping strategy interface.
2. **Split/merge threshold defaults:** size S and load thresholds are workload-dependent; defaults are placeholders pending measurement (Bigtable 100–200 MB, TiKV 96 MB, MongoDB 64 MB, YugabyteDB 512 MB/10 GB reference points).
3. **Map epoch publication mechanism:** atomic publication via `ids-partition-map` vs. separate epoch service — interface defined, implementation target TBD.
4. **Ownership transfer catch-up protocol:** dual-application vs. log-replay for post-snapshot mutations; idempotent replay boundaries keyed by OpRef/OrderingPos need `ids-write`/`ids-commit-state` integration details.
5. **Partition metadata size growth:** lineage + redirect/rollback pointers accumulate; retention/GC policy for split/merge history undefined.
6. **Signed partition metadata:** whether map epochs/partition metadata carry ed25519 signatures (via `ids-crypto`) for audit is a product decision.
7. **Formal verification scope:** TLA+/PlusCal spec for partition invariants (single owner, atomic publication, logical id stability) deferred to `ids-doc`.

---

### 11. Engineering Decisions Summary

|| Decision | Rationale ||
||----------|-----------|-------------|
| Partition as unit of distribution | Atom of placement in Dynamo/Bigtable/TiKV/CockroachDB/Couchbase; independently placeable, movable |
| Logical → physical indirection (versioned map) | Live migration/rebalance without client key remapping (Couchbase vBucket, NodeDB vShards) |
| Key mapping per dataset policy (hash/range/directory) | Hash for uniform equality, range for scans, directory for residency/uneven shards |
| Split/merge with hysteresis (1.5×S / 0.5×S) | Prevents partition explosion and split/merge thrash (dynamic partition management research) |
| Atomic publication + fencing | Single authoritative epoch; no split-brain; old owner fenced before new owner authoritative |
| Single write owner per partition | Simplifies consistency; ownership transfer via fence → snapshot → replay → cutover → publish |
| Immutable logical id across moves | Access policy, history, and client addressing preserved during region/node moves (`ids-mobility`) |
| Per-partition checksums + Merkle (ids-integrity) | Integrity at split/merge/move; bit-rot detection |
| New `ids-distribution` crate | User's separate-crates rule; clean dependency boundary between placement and replication/routing |
| Allowed crypto only | ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305; nothing else |
| Carrier-agnostic via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` | No `std::net`/`tokio::net`/libp2p/TCP/UDP/QUIC/HTTP/DNS/Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/cellular/VPN/mesh |
