### 1. Executive Summary

Phase 017 creates `ids-replication`, the IDS crate for propagating committed changes between replicas over ordered, versioned, resumable streams. It owns the replication half of the write lifecycle: once `ids-write` has durably committed an op (Phase 012), `ids-replication` ships that op's change to independent and full-replication targets, tracks per-target acknowledgement cursors, exposes replication-lag observability, takes synchronization checkpoints, performs incremental synchronization (catch-up from cursor after restart/partition), retries synchronization with bounded backoff, and guarantees idempotent application at targets.

Every change stream is versioned: each record carries a monotonic `VersionPos` (u64) plus the canonical `OrderingPos` from `ids-000-aa`, so receivers can detect gaps, reorder, deduplicate, and resume from any checkpoint. Delivery is carrier-agnostic: stream frames are opaque `Vec<u8>` datagrams sent to `ids-carrier::Endpoint` targets; `ids-replication` never opens a socket. Application at targets is idempotent: an apply key of (dataset, OpRef, VersionPos) inside a dedup window makes redelivery harmless, matching the exactly-once research basis (at-least-once delivery + idempotent apply).

No `ids-replication` code exists yet; this plan is the complete blueprint for implementation. It depends on `ids-000-aa` (canonical types + sealed `trait Replication` contract), `ids-carrier` (opaque `Endpoint` datagram send/receive), and `ids-write` (change source, via `OrderingPos`/`OpRef`). It is consumed by `ids-sync` (Phase 018, replica reconciliation/convergence) and `ids-broadcast` (Phase 020, ordering guarantees).

---

### 2. Architecture Overview

`ids-replication` sits above `ids-000-aa` (types + sealed contracts + invariants + errors), `ids-carrier` (opaque `Endpoint` datagram transport), and `ids-write` (durable commit log source of changes). It is layered so each concern — streams, acks, lag, checkpoints, incremental sync, retries, idempotent apply — is an independent module:

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   APPLICATION / ids-SM LAYER (ids-* crates)          │
│  state machine replication · ordered command application · commit    │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                    Phase 012: ids-write (CHANGE SOURCE)              │
│  durable WAL → committed ops with OrderingPos + OpRef                │
└──────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                                   │ committed change (OrderingPos, OpRef)
┌─────────────────────────────────▼───────────────────────────────────┐
│                 Phase 017: ids-replication (THIS CRATE)             │
│  ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌────────────┐ │
│  │  streams     │ │  ack tracking│ │  lag         │ │ checkpoints│ │
│  │  (ordered,   │ │  (per-peer   │ │  observability│ │ (sync pts)│ │
│  │   versioned) │ │   cursor)    │ │              │ │            │ │
│  └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └────────────┘ │
│  ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌────────────┐ │
│  │  incremental │ │  retries +   │ │  idempotent  │ │  modes     │ │
│  │  sync        │ │  bounded     │ │  application │ │  independent│ │
│  │  (catch-up)  │ │  backoff     │ │  (dedup)     │ │  / full    │ │
│  └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └────────────┘ │
└──────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                                   │ opaque Vec<u8> frames
┌─────────────────────────────────▼───────────────────────────────────┐
│              CARRIER BOUNDARY: ids-carrier::Endpoint only           │
│  send_datagram(Endpoint{CarrierType, Vec<u8>}, payload: &[u8])      │
│  receive_datagram → (Endpoint, Vec<u8>)                             │
│  No std::net / tokio::net / libp2p / IP / TCP / UDP / QUIC / HTTP   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Data flow of one replicated change:**
1. `ids-write` commits an op: durable WAL record with `OrderingPos`, `OpRef`, dataset id, payload.
2. `ids-replication` streams module wraps it in a versioned frame: `(stream_id, VersionPos, OrderingPos, OpRef, flags, payload, blake3/sha256 checksum, optional ed25519 signature)`.
3. Frame sent as an opaque datagram to each replication target's `ids-carrier::Endpoint` (independent mode: per-dataset streams; full mode: one dataset-wide stream).
4. Target's stream receiver reassembles in-order, detects gaps (NACK/gap report), delivers to idempotent-apply module.
5. Idempotent-apply: apply key `(dataset, OpRef, VersionPos)`; duplicate within dedup window = no-op, return prior result.
6. Target advances its apply cursor and sends an ack back over `ids-carrier::Endpoint`.
7. Source's ack tracker advances the per-target ack cursor; lag meter computes `send_cursor − apply_cursor` per target.
8. Periodically or on catch-up, synchronization checkpoints are taken: `(checkpoint_id, VersionPos, blake3 root hash, peer set, timestamp)`; streams below a stable checkpoint are truncated.
9. On restart/partition heal, incremental sync resumes from the last ack cursor / checkpoint (missing-update detection via version-range comparison).

**Design rules (non-negotiable):**
- One canonical definition per type; canonical types (`NodeId`, `OrderingPos`, `OpRef`, `Endpoint`, `CarrierType`, `OpState`, `CommitState`, `VersionPos`) imported from `ids_000_aa::X`, never redefined.
- `ids-replication` implements the sealed `trait Replication` (streams, checkpoints, retries) from `ids-000-aa/src/contracts/replication.rs`; downstream crates use it as a trait bound, cannot implement it.
- All transport is datagram-based via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` (`CarrierType` enum + opaque `Vec<u8>`). No IP addresses, ports, sockets, or networking stack.
- Crypto surface: ed25519 signatures (stream/checkpoint authentication), sha256/blake3 (frame/checkpoint checksums, hash chains), xchacha20poly1305/chacha20poly1305 (optional payload encryption). All ops in `ids-crypto`; this crate declares only usage boundaries.
- Replication is dataset-scoped via `ids-ordering-domain`; invariant `no_global_master` in `ids-000-aa` (no permanent global ordering master).
- Operation lifecycle reuses `ids-000-aa` `OpState` and `CommitState`.

---

### 3. Detailed Research Dimensions

#### 3.1 Independent Replication vs Full Replication
**Independent replication:** each dataset (or partition) has its own versioned stream; targets subscribe to the datasets they hold; fan-out is N streams over N `ids-carrier::Endpoint` targets. Rate model: cross-carrier egress ≈ W·B·(M−1) for W writers, B bytes/write, M targets — bounded by per-target credit (see 3.10). Source: multi-leader replication commit/ship/apply (system-design-patterns); TiCDC multi-writer CDC.
**Full replication:** one dataset-wide versioned stream carries every committed op; every target receives and applies the full stream. Simpler ordering (single total order per dataset) but higher bandwidth per target. Used as the baseline mode; independent mode is the optimization.
**Engineering decision:** both modes implemented as stream configurations over the same stream primitive; mode selected per dataset at replication session start. Source research: ESTABLISHED (Q007, Q027 HYPOTHESIS for rate model — IDS-specific model to validate).

#### 3.2 Replication Streams — Ordered, Versioned
Each stream: `stream_id` (from `ids-000-aa` types) + monotonic `VersionPos` (u64, assigned at append, before send) + canonical `OrderingPos`. Frame: `(stream_id, VersionPos, OrderingPos, OpRef, flags, payload_len, payload, checksum [blake3/sha256], optional ed25519 signature)`. Receivers deliver in VersionPos order; out-of-order frames held in a bounded reassembly buffer (cap per stream — bounds memory, see Q029); gaps detected by VersionPos holes trigger NACK/gap report and resume-from-cursor. Logical logging (not physical): frames carry op payloads, not page images (IDS has no buffer pool/page concept). Source: BtrLog/VLDB monotonic LSN (Q002 ESTABLISHED); RFC 2960 sequenced delivery + bounded reassembly (Q005 ESTABLISHED).

#### 3.3 Acknowledgement Tracking — Per-Target Cursors
Each replication target tracks: `send_cursor` (highest VersionPos sent), `ack_cursor` (highest VersionPos acked by target, persisted), `apply_cursor` (highest applied). Acks are cumulative: acking VersionPos V implies all ≤ V applied (like Pulsar cumulative ack marks and Oxia FollowerCursor.AckOffset). Out-of-order acks folded into a persistable ack-watermark cursor. The ack cursor is the resume point: after restart, the stream resumes sending at `ack_cursor + 1`. Source: Pulsar PIP-81/PIP-299, NATS JetStream consumer ack state, Oxia FollowerCursor (Q008, Q010 ESTABLISHED).

#### 3.4 Replication Lag Observability
`lag(target) = send_cursor(target) − apply_cursor(target)` measured in VersionPos units and bytes; also time-based lag (last_send_time − last_apply_time). Exposed as metrics per target and per stream: lag count, lag bytes, max lag, lag over threshold alerts. Lag drives backpressure (3.10) and catch-up priority in incremental sync. Source: Google Cloud SQL replication lag, AWS RDS, Confluent Replicator monitoring, CockroachDB logical replication monitoring, MongoDB rs.printSecondaryReplicationInfo (Q009 ESTABLISHED).

#### 3.5 Synchronization Checkpoints
A synchronization checkpoint: `(checkpoint_id, VersionPos, root_hash [blake3 hash chain of applied stream prefix], peer_set, timestamp, dataset)`. Checkpoints are durable (persisted via the store contract). A checkpoint is *stable* when all peers in `peer_set` have acked past its Versionpos (causal stability). Streams below the latest stable checkpoint are truncated (segments deleted, log_start_offset advanced). Recovery: load latest checkpoint + replay stream frames after it. Source: snapshot + WAL checkpoint truncation (Q015 ESTABLISHED); Raft InstallSnapshot catch-up (Q017 ESTABLISHED); TigerBeetle VSR checkpoints.

#### 3.6 Incremental Synchronization — Missing Update Detection
After restart or partition heal, a target does not re-sync everything. It exchanges version ranges with the source: `missing = [source_version_range] \ [target_applied_range]` computed from version vectors / per-stream apply cursors. The source ships only missing frames (delta exchange), then resumes live streaming. Timestamp-based tracking (SurrealDB) is rejected as primary mechanism (sub-microsecond rounding gaps drop rows — Q013 airbyte issue); version-position ranges are the source of truth. Source: Sui StateSync checkpoint discovery, DBLog incremental snapshots, Nango incremental/full sync docs (Q013 ESTABLISHED).

#### 3.7 Synchronization Retries — Bounded Backoff
Retry policy: classify errors (transient: carrier unavailable, endpoint not initialized, timeout → retry; permanent: invalid endpoint, authentication failure → do not retry). Bounded attempts (max N). Exponential backoff with jitter: `delay = min(cap, base * 2^attempt + jitter)`, jitter decorrelates retries across replicas to avoid thundering herds/retry storms. Retry budget caps concurrent in-flight retries. Source: AWS Architecture Blog exponential backoff + jitter (Q014, Q026 ESTABLISHED).

#### 3.8 Idempotent Application
Apply key: `(dataset_id, OpRef, VersionPos)`. Target maintains a dedup window of recent apply keys; a frame whose key is in the window is applied as no-op and the prior result returned. Dedup window expiry = duplicate-admission event, never silent cleanup (Machine-Checked Dual-Write Recovery). Window sized from the longest survivable outage. Idempotency turns at-least-once carrier delivery into exactly-once effect. Source: Azure Idempotent Consumer pattern, Kafka idempotent producer, arxiv 2608.00501 (Q011, Q012 ESTABLISHED).

#### 3.9 Crypto Surface & Integrity
Allowed crypto only: ed25519 (stream frame / checkpoint signatures — transferable authentication evidence), xchacha20poly1305 / chacha20poly1305 (optional payload AEAD; XChaCha preferred for random nonces — 192-bit nonce bounds misuse risk), sha256 and blake3 (per-frame checksums, checkpoint root-hash hash chains). CRC32C explicitly not used (not in allowed list; blake3 preferred for speed). All crypto ops live in `ids-crypto`; `ids-replication` declares usage boundaries and primitive IDs only. Source: RFC 8032/9591, libsodium XChaCha docs, IETF draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha-03, BLAKE3 spec, Borg BLAKE3-256, NIST FIPS 180-4 (Q020-Q024 ESTABLISHED).

#### 3.10 Backpressure & Flow Control
When targets apply slower than the source sends, the source applies backpressure: reject/throttle new stream frames once unacked bytes per target exceed a ceiling (credit-based; credit granted by target acks returned over `ids-carrier::Endpoint` payloads). Bounded reassembly buffer per stream caps memory; peers flooding past the window are refused (not recorded as received) — direct response to the documented stream-reassembly memory-exhaustion DoS (Q029). Source: Akka Streams boundedness, system-design-patterns backpressure, Flink backpressure (Q025 ESTABLISHED).

#### 3.11 Research Status by Dimension
| Dimension | Status | Basis |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| Independent vs full replication | ESTABLISHED | Q007; rate model HYPOTHESIS (Q027) |
| Versioned ordered streams | ESTABLISHED | Q002, Q005 |
| Ack tracking / cursors | ESTABLISHED | Q008, Q010 |
| Lag observability | ESTABLISHED | Q009 |
| Checkpoints | ESTABLISHED | Q013, Q015, Q017 |
| Incremental sync | ESTABLISHED | Q013 |
| Retries + bounded backoff | ESTABLISHED | Q014, Q026 |
| Idempotent application | ESTABLISHED | Q011, Q012 |
| Carrier-agnostic endpoint | HYPOTHESIS (IDS-defined) | Q019 |
| Allowed crypto (ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305) | ESTABLISHED | Q020-Q024 |
| Bounded reassembly memory | ESTABLISHED problem; scheme = design decision | Q029 |
| Log shipping catch-up | ESTABLISHED | Q030 |

### 4. Threat Model & Mitigations

|| Threat | Mitigation |
|---|-----------|------------|
| Lost change on carrier failure (unacked frame) | Retry with bounded backoff from ack cursor; at-least-once delivery + idempotent apply |
| Duplicate redelivery after retry/restart | Idempotent apply key `(dataset, OpRef, VersionPos)` + dedup window |
| Out-of-order / duplicated frames | VersionPos ordering + bounded reassembly buffer + gap NACK |
| Stream reassembly memory exhaustion | Per-stream reassembly cap; refuse frames past window (never record) |
| Replication lag unbounded (slow target) | Per-target credit/backpressure; lag metrics + alerts; catch-up priority |
| Checkpoint taken while target behind → truncation loses data | Checkpoint stable only when all peers acked past it (causal stability) |
| Checkpoint / frame corruption | blake3/sha256 per-frame checksum; fail closed on mismatch; hash-chain checkpoints |
| Forged / tampered stream | ed25519 signatures on frames/checkpoints; nonce-random XChaCha20-Poly1305 optional encryption |
| Disallowed crypto / networking stack | Dependency audit bans std::net/tokio::net/libp2p etc.; only 5 allowed primitives |
| OpRef / VersionPos collision or replay | 36^9 OpRef namespace; monotonic VersionPos; collision variant in error contract |
| Position overflow | saturating arithmetic on VersionPos/OrderingPos |
| Retry storm across replicas | Jitter + bounded attempts + retry budget |
| Commit vs synchronization confusion | Commit = local durable (ids-write); synchronized = target applied (ack cursor) |

### 5. Integration with Existing Crates

|| Crate | Role in Phase 017 |
|---|-------|-------------------|
| `ids-000-aa` (master) | Canonical types: `NodeId`, `OrderingPos`, `OpRef`, `Endpoint`, `CarrierType`, `OpState`, `CommitState`, `VersionPos`; sealed `trait Replication` (streams, checkpoints, retries); invariants (`no_global_master`, `out_eq_in`); errors; versioning |
| `ids-carrier` (Phase 002) | Opaque `Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>`); `send_datagram`/`receive_datagram`; sole transport for all replication traffic |
| `ids-write` (Phase 012) | Change source: committed WAL records with `OrderingPos` + `OpRef` fed into replication streams |
| `ids-crypto` (Phase 003) | Crypto ops (ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305); `ids-replication` consumes type surface/primitive IDs only, no runtime dependency beyond allowed set |
| `ids-ordering-domain` (Phase 055) | Dataset-scoped ordering domains; no global master |
| `ids-sync` (Phase 018) | Consumer: incremental change streams + checkpoint management for reconciliation/convergence |
| `ids-broadcast` (Phase 020) | Consumer: ordered broadcast layer builds on replication streams |
| `ids-consistency` (Phase 019) | Consistency profiles gating replication acknowledgement |
| All other `ids-*` crates | Depend on `ids-000-aa`; `ids-replication` depends on `ids-000-aa` + `ids-carrier` only |

Integration points:
- `ids-replication` never touches the network directly; all stream/ack/checkpoint traffic via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` datagrams.
- `ids-replication` implements the sealed `trait Replication` from `ids-000-aa`; downstream crates (`ids-sync`, `ids-broadcast`) depend on it as a trait bound.
- `ids-write` emits committed changes; `ids-replication` consumes them as the change source — no circular dependency.
- Cargo workspace member; `ids-replication = { path = "../ids-replication" }`; dependents declare path dependency.
- No dependency on `std::net`, `tokio::net`, libp2p, or any carrier-specific crate.

### 7. Key Algorithms & Data Structures

1. **Versioned stream frame** — `(stream_id, VersionPos, OrderingPos, OpRef, flags, payload, checksum[blake3/sha256], optional ed25519 signature)`. VersionPos assigned at append, before send; enables gap detection and resume. Source: BtrLog/VLDB monotonic LSN (Q002).
2. **Ordered delivery with bounded reassembly** — receiver holds out-of-order frames in a per-stream bounded buffer; delivers contiguous prefix from `recv_cursor`; VersionPos holes trigger NACK/gap report; buffer cap prevents memory-exhaustion DoS. Source: RFC 2960 sequenced delivery (Q005); quinn-proto RUSTSEC-2026-0185 fix pattern (Q029).
3. **Per-target ack cursor** — cumulative ack: acking VersionPos V implies all ≤ V applied; ack cursor persisted as resume point; out-of-order acks folded into watermark. Source: Pulsar PIP-81 cumulative acks, Oxia FollowerCursor.AckOffset (Q008, Q010).
4. **Replication lag** — `lag(target) = send_cursor − apply_cursor` in VersionPos units + bytes + time; per-target metrics and alerts; feeds backpressure and catch-up priority. Source: Cloud SQL/AWS/CockroachDB/MongoDB lag monitoring (Q009).
5. **Synchronization checkpoint** — `(checkpoint_id, VersionPos, root_hash, peer_set, timestamp)`; stable when all peers ack past VersionPos; truncate streams below stable checkpoint; recovery = load checkpoint + replay after it. Source: snapshot+WAL truncation (Q015); Raft InstallSnapshot (Q017).
6. **Incremental sync / missing detection** — missing = source version range \ target applied range; ship only missing frames then resume live; version-position ranges (not timestamps) are source of truth. Source: Sui StateSync, DBLog incremental snapshots (Q013).
7. **Retry + bounded backoff** — classify transient/permanent; bounded attempts; `delay = min(cap, base*2^attempt + jitter)`; retry budget; jitter prevents thundering herds. Source: AWS Architecture Blog (Q014, Q026).
8. **Idempotent application** — apply key `(dataset, OpRef, VersionPos)`; dedup window; duplicate = no-op returning prior result; window expiry = duplicate-admission event. Source: Azure Idempotent Consumer, Kafka idempotent producer, arxiv 2608.00501 (Q011, Q012).
9. **Credit-based flow control** — per-target unacked-byte ceiling; target grants credit via acks over Endpoint payloads; throttle/reject above ceiling. Source: Akka Streams boundedness, backpressure pattern (Q025).
10. **Hash-chain checkpoint integrity** — blake3/sha256 hash chain over applied stream prefix; checkpoint root hash anchors chain; Ed25519 signature on checkpoint. Source: SHA-256 hash chains, FIPS 180-4 (Q023).

### 8. Dependencies

`ids-replication/Cargo.toml`:
- `ids-000-aa = { path = "../ids-000-aa" }` — canonical types, sealed `trait Replication` contract, invariants, errors
- `ids-carrier = { path = "../ids-carrier" }` — opaque `Endpoint` datagram send/receive
- `blake3 = "1.5"` — frame/checkpoint checksum (preferred), hash-chain root hash
- `sha2 = "0.10"` — SHA-256 frame/checkpoint checksum (alternative)
- `chacha20poly1305 = "0.11"` — XChaCha20-Poly1305 / ChaCha20-Poly1305 optional payload AEAD
- `ed25519 = "1.5"` / `ed25519-dalek = "2.1"` — stream/checkpoint signatures
- `thiserror = "2.0"` — `ReplicationError` enum
- `serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }` — frame/checkpoint serialization

**No** `std::net`, `tokio`, `tokio::net`, `libp2p`, `hyper`, `reqwest`, DNS, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular, VPN, or mesh dependencies. No async runtime requirement beyond what `ids-carrier` provides. No networking stack. `ids-replication` depends on `ids-000-aa` and `ids-carrier` only (plus allowed-crypto crates).

Downstream dependents: `ids-sync` (Phase 018), `ids-broadcast` (Phase 020), `ids-consistency` (Phase 019) — consume `ids-replication` streams/acks/checkpoints.

### 10. Remaining Uncertainties

|| Uncertainty | Impact | Resolution path |
|---|-------------|--------|-----------------|
| Fan-out rate model for heterogeneous carriers | Bandwidth/credit sizing per target | Q027 HYPOTHESIS — validate with ids-sim benchmarks; credit ceiling is a tunable |
| Dedup window size | Memory vs outage survival | Sized from longest intended outage; expiry = duplicate-admission event |
| Checkpoint interval vs truncation aggressiveness | Recovery time vs storage | Start time-based + count-based; adaptive in bench phase |
| Whether `ids-crypto` runtime dep is allowed | Dependency direction (ids-crypto must not depend on ids-000-aa) | Confirm no-cycle rule; use primitive IDs + type surface only |
| Reassembly memory cap value | DoS resistance vs latency under reorder | Derive from bounded-buffer analysis; configurable per stream |
| Endpoint framing/MTU per carrier type | Frame size limits | CarrierType-specific max datagram size negotiated via ids-carrier capability |
| Whether VersionPos and OrderingPos are distinct or aliased | API simplicity vs semantics | VersionPos = stream-local monotonic; OrderingPos = canonical global position from ids-000-aa |
| Formal verification scope for stream state machine | Confidence in gap/liveness properties | TLA+ spec in ids-state-machine deferred; property tests first |

---

### 11. Engineering Decisions Summary

|| Decision | Rationale |
|---|-----------|-----------|
| `ids-replication` as separate crate | Matches user directive: separate crates, not more folders |
| Versioned streams with VersionPos + OrderingPos | Monotonic versioning enables gap detection, dedup, resume (Q002 ESTABLISHED) |
| Logical (op payload) frames, not physical page images | IDS has no buffer pool/page concept; logical frames smaller and idempotent-apply-friendly |
| Cumulative per-target ack cursor as resume point | Proven pattern (Pulsar, NATS JetStream, Oxia); resume = cursor + 1 |
| Checkpoint stable iff all peers acked past it | Prevents truncation data loss; causal stability (Q013, Q015, Q017 ESTABLISHED) |
| Version ranges (not timestamps) for missing detection | Timestamps drop rows at rounding boundaries (Airbyte #84400 Q013) |
| Bounded reassembly + gap NACK | Counters memory-exhaustion DoS (Q029 documented problem) |
| Idempotent apply key `(dataset, OpRef, VersionPos)` + dedup window | Exactly-once effect over at-least-once carrier delivery (Q011, Q012 ESTABLISHED) |
| Bounded exponential backoff with jitter + retry budget | Prevents retry storms (Q014, Q026 ESTABLISHED) |
| All traffic via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` only | Carrier-agnostic absolute rule (CRATES.md §9-11) |
| Crypto: ed25519 signatures, sha256/blake3 hashing, XChaCha20-Poly1305/chacha20poly1305 AEAD | Only allowed primitives (CRATES.md §3) |
| `ids-crypto` type surface only, no runtime cycle | Preserves rule that `ids-crypto` does not depend on `ids-000-aa` |
| satura­ting arithmetic on all positions | No overflow panics in distributed versioning |
| Cargo workspace member at `C:/idfs/ids-replication/` | Matches existing layout (`ids-000-aa` at `C:/idfs/ids-000-aa/`) |

### 1. Executive Summary

Phase 018 creates `ids-sync`, the IDS crate responsible for replica reconciliation and convergence: keeping every replica of a dataset convergent despite independent local writes, missed updates, out-of-order delivery, and long-lived partitions. It is a **separate crate** (CRATES.md entry 18) located at `C:/idfs/ids-sync/`, not a folder inside an existing crate.

The crate layers four mechanisms on top of each other, from low-latency common case to full-convergence backstop:

1. **Incremental change streams** — per-dataset append-only change feed keyed by version; peers exchange only entries newer than their last acknowledged checkpoint (push/pull via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` datagrams).
2. **Checkpoint management** — periodic signed state snapshots with version positions; a replica resumes sync from the latest common checkpoint instead of replaying the whole history.
3. **Missing update detection** — version-vector / dotted-version-vector comparison plus Merkle-tree digest exchange locates exactly which keys/ranges diverge in O(d · k) hash comparisons instead of O(n) full comparison.
4. **Anti-entropy repair + read repair** — scheduled Merkle-tree sweep reconciles cold/rarely-read data (the backstop that guarantees convergence regardless of access pattern); read repair heals divergent keys on the read path.

Convergence model: **strong eventual consistency (SEC)** — replicas that have received the same set of updates reach identical state regardless of delivery order, duplication, or delay (CALM theorem; Shapiro et al. 2011). Every update is inflationary in the join-semilattice sense; merge is commutative, associative, idempotent.

**Carrier-agnostic absolute rule:** no `std::net`, `SocketAddr`, `IpAddr`, `tokio::net`, libp2p, IP, TCP, UDP, QUIC, HTTP, DNS, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular, VPN, or conventional mesh anywhere. `ids-carrier::Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>`, opaque bytes capped per carrier) is the sole address and traffic type. All sync traffic rides `ids-carrier::Endpoint` datagrams: `send_datagram(endpoint, &[u8])` / `receive_datagram() -> (Endpoint, Vec<u8>)`.

**Allowed crypto only:** ed25519 (signed checkpoints, signed change entries, authenticated reconciliation messages), xchacha20poly1305 / chacha20poly1305 (optional payload encryption for sync entries in transit), sha256 / blake3 (Merkle tree digests, content addressing, version hashes). All crypto consumed from `ids-crypto`; `ids-sync` declares usage boundaries only, never implements primitives.

`ids-000-aa` is the master crate with all canonical types and sealed trait contracts: `NodeId`, `DatasetId`, `RecordId`, `PartitionId`, `Version`, `OrderingPos`, `Endpoint`, `CarrierType`, `OpState`, `CommitState`, `ConsistencyProfile`, sealed `trait Replication`, sealed `trait CRDT`, invariants (`version_vector`, `commit_prefix`, `replica_freshness`, `custody_graph`, `out_eq_in`), versioning (`ProtocolVersion`, `EdgeCaseBits` u128). `ids-sync` imports these verbatim and never redefines them.

**Research only** — no code, no source modifications, only this plan document.

### 2. Architecture Overview

`ids-sync` sits between `ids-replication` (ordered streams, checkpoints, retries — CRATES.md entry 17) and `ids-consistency` (consistency profiles, committed-prefix — CRATES.md entry 19), below the application/query layer and above `ids-carrier`.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   APPLICATION / QUERY LAYER (ids-*)                 │
│  reads, writes, consistency-profile requests, read-repair triggers   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                    Phase 018: ids-sync (THIS CRATE)                 │
│  ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────────┐   │
│  │ Change Stream   │ │ Checkpoint      │ │ Missing Update      │   │
│  │ (feed, versions)│ │ Management      │ │ Detection (VV/DVV)  │   │
│  └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────────┘   │
│  ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────────┐   │
│  │ Merkle Tree     │ │ Anti-Entropy    │ │ Read Repair +       │   │
│  │ Comparison      │ │ Repair          │ │ Reconciliation      │   │
│  └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────────┘   │
│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │ Integrity Verification · Retry Procedures · Version Tracking   │  │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│              CARRIER BOUNDARY (ids-carrier::Endpoint only)          │
│  send_datagram(Endpoint{CarrierType, Vec<u8>}, &[u8])               │
│  receive_datagram() -> (Endpoint, Vec<u8>)                          │
│  No std::net / tokio::net / libp2p / IP / TCP / UDP / QUIC / HTTP   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Data flow — incremental sync (common case):**
1. Local write lands via `ids-replication` stream; `ids-sync` appends a versioned change entry to the local change stream (append-only log keyed by `Version`/`OrderingPos`).
2. On a sync tick (or on demand), the local replica sends its current checkpoint position + version-vector summary to a peer over `ids-carrier::Endpoint`.
3. The peer compares version vectors (or Merkle roots) to compute the missing set: entries the peer lacks but the sender has, and vice versa.
4. Missing entries are shipped as compact change batches (only the delta, not full state); each entry is signed with ed25519 and integrity-verified with sha256/blake3 before apply.
5. Receiver applies entries idempotently (duplicate suppression by entry ID); advances its checkpoint position; sends an ack back over the carrier endpoint.

**Data flow — anti-entropy repair (backstop):**
1. Periodically (or on integrity-audit trigger), each replica builds a Merkle tree over its dataset partition keyed by `RecordId`; leaves hash `(key, version, value/tombstone)`, interior nodes hash `sha256(left || right)` or `blake3(left || right)`.
2. Replicas exchange root hashes (one hash summarizes the entire range). Equal roots ⇒ identical state, stop immediately.
3. On mismatch, descend only into divergent subtrees (prune matching branches). Locating k divergent keys costs O(d · k) hash exchanges instead of O(n).
4. At divergent leaves, exchange actual key-value entries; resolve by deterministic winner (LWW by version/timestamp, tombstone beats value, CRDT merge for concurrent writes) — symmetric so the outcome does not depend on which replica starts.
5. Re-hash repaired leaves up to the root; roots now equal ⇒ convergence verified.

**Data flow — read repair (opportunistic):**
1. A read contacts R replicas; coordinator compares versions/digests of the returned values.
2. On disagreement, the winner (by consistency profile: LWW, CRDT merge, or quorum overlap) is pushed back to stale replicas before returning to the client.
3. Heals hot keys on the access path; anti-entropy handles cold keys.

**No end-to-end path assumption:** sync messages are datagrams over `ids-carrier::Endpoint`; the carrier decides delivery. Retransmission is expressed as re-sending a datagram to the same endpoint — never a TCP retransmit, never RTT-bound timers. Timeouts are absolute deadlines keyed to entry creation/checkpoint time.

---

### 3. Detailed Research Dimensions

#### 3.1 Incremental change streams & checkpoint management

**Change stream model:** per-dataset append-only log of change entries `{ entry_id, version, op_type, record_id, value/tombstone, prev_version_hash, sig }`. Entry ID derived from BLAKE3(content-addressed) so identical changes have identical IDs and duplicates are trivially deduped. Each entry references its predecessor (hash chain / append-only log), giving a tamper-evident history without a central sequencer.

**Checkpoint management:** periodic signed snapshots `{ dataset_id, checkpoint_version, state_root (Merkle root), version_vector, sig }` persisted via `ids-replication` checkpoints. A sync session begins by exchanging checkpoint positions; replicas resume from the latest *common* checkpoint and only stream entries after it. Checkpoints are signed with ed25519 so an untrusted peer cannot serve a forged snapshot.

Research basis: write-ahead log + periodic checkpoint (append-only log before apply; recovery = load snapshot + replay tail — bounds replay work); CouchDB replication protocol changes feed (sequence ID, continuous replication); subduction batch/incremental sync (fingerprint-based reconciliation + per-peer monotonic counters); hypercore/hyperdb secure append-only logs (public-key identified feed, immutable entries, verify-on-download from untrusted peers).

#### 3.2 Missing update detection (version tracking)

**Version Vector (VV):** map `ReplicaId → counter`; detects causality (VV1 ≤ VV2 iff every entry ≤; concurrent when neither ≤ the other). Source: DOMAINS Layer 12 (`version_vector` invariant in ids-000-aa); Parker et al. 1983.

**Dotted Version Vector (DVV):** compact form — a version vector plus "dots" (replica, counter) for the most recent writes; reduces metadata size when few replicas write each key. Source: Preguiça et al. 2010/2012 "Dotted Version Vectors"; eribeiro VV-vs-DVV comparison.

**Missing set computation:** peer A sends its VV/DVV summary (O(replicas) size, not O(keys)); peer B computes which entries it lacks and which A lacks; only those are transferred. For very large datasets, Merkle-tree digest exchange (3.4) replaces VV when per-key metadata is too large.

Research basis: Dynamo/Dread versioning, Causal Bayes, did:crdt signed deltas (version-vector-based optimized OR-Set tombstone-free variant).

#### 3.3 Merkle tree comparison & anti-entropy repair

**Merkle tree over dataset partition:** leaves = hash buckets of `(key || version || value || tombstone)`; interior = `sha256(left || right)` or `blake3(left || right)`; fixed binary shape (bucketized key space) so two replicas' trees share shape and compare positionally. Leaf covers a fixed key-range (not one key), capping tree size: depth d covers 2^d buckets; O(d · k) diff cost for k divergent buckets.

**Diff algorithm:** send root hash. Equal → converged in O(1). Different → exchange child hashes, recurse only into mismatched subtrees, prune matching ones. At leaf level, exchange actual entries in divergent buckets, resolve deterministically, re-hash up.

**Repair semantics:** symmetric last-writer-wins by version/timestamp (tombstone beats value), or CRDT merge for concurrent writes — outcome independent of which replica initiates. Overstreaming trade-off: coarse buckets stream more keys than needed; fine buckets cost more tree metadata.

Research basis: Dynamo anti-entropy (Merkle trees, 2007), Cassandra `nodetool repair` (full/sub-range/incremental repair, depth-15 compact trees), Riak active anti-entropy, ScyllaDB, Git object model, IPFS Merkle-DAG, Certificate Transparency (RFC 6962 inclusion/consistency proofs), "Anti-Entropy, Digests, and Reconciliation" (digest exchange + Merkle localization), Merkle-CRDTs (arXiv 2004.00107 — Merkle-DAG as logical clock, sync without copying full DAG).

#### 3.4 Read repair & replica reconciliation

**Read repair:** coordinator reads from R replicas; digests compared; mismatches trigger write-back of winning version to stale replicas. Foreground (blocking, stronger) vs background (probabilistic, lower latency). Heals only keys that are read — complementary to anti-entropy backstop.

**Reconciliation / read repair vs anti-entropy division of labor:**
| Mechanism | When it runs | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| Read repair | On read path | Hot keys touched by clients |
| Hinted handoff (via ids-replication retries) | Transient peer unavailability | Writes missed during short outage |
| Anti-entropy Merkle sweep | Scheduled / on-demand | Cold data, long outages, bit rot |

Research basis: Cassandra read repair (blocking/none/probabilistic), Dynamo hinted handoff + Merkle anti-entropy, "Anti-Entropy & Read Repair" synthesis (semicolony.dev), CRDT-based reconciliation (merge eliminates winner-picking for CRDT-typed keys).

#### 3.5 Retry procedures & integrity verification

**Retry:** sync entries are idempotent (entry-ID dedup); failed delivery = re-send datagram to same `Endpoint`. Bounded retry with jittered backoff, retry-storm prevention (ids-fault circuit breakers), dead-letter queue for persistently-failing peers. No RTT-estimate timeouts — absolute deadlines keyed to entry creation time.

**Integrity verification:** every change entry carries ed25519 signature over (author, entry_id, prev_version_hash, payload); receiver verifies before apply (rejects forged/tampered entries). Merkle tree leaves include value hash so a peer serving corrupted data is detected at leaf comparison. Checkpoints signed with ed25519; chunk-level hash proofs (sha256/blake3) let untrusted peers ferry data without being trusted.

**Version tracking:** per-dataset `Version` + `OrderingPos` from ids-000-aa; `commit_prefix` invariant (committed-prefix tracking) ensures reads respect committed position prefix; `replica_freshness` invariant validates replica freshness for reads.

Research basis: RFC 8032 EdDSA deterministic signatures (no bad randomness), batch verification (ed25519-dalek `verify_batch`), hash-history mechanism (OceanStore — dependency graph of version hashes, false-coincidence reduction), "Ensuring Convergence and Invariants Without Coordination" (ECOOP 2025 — No-Op framework, causal stability, strong convergence without coordination).

#### 3.6 Gossip/epidemic dissemination & carrier-agnostic delivery

Sync may run over sparse/multi-hop carrier topology. Gossip fanout (periodic random peer exchange; O(log N) rounds to reach all w.h.p.) disseminates change announcements; actual entry transfer is pull-based on request. SRM-style reliable multicast (eventual delivery without enforced order) as the base; ordering machinery (ids-broadcast) layered on top when needed. All delivery re-expressed as `send_datagram(endpoint, &[u8])` retries — carrier-agnostic.

Research basis: Demers et al. gossip/epidemic protocols, HyParView fanout tuning, SRM reliable multicast, did:crdt causal delivery (weaker than total order, no consensus).

---

### 4. Threat Model & Mitigations

| Threat | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Forged / tampered change entries | ed25519 signature over (author, entry_id, prev_hash, payload); verify before any state effect |
| Replay of old signed entries | Per-peer monotonic sequence + nonce replay cache with TTL; tombstones carry deletion authority; causality check rejects stale dependency positions |
| Duplicate datagrams | Entry-ID dedup (idempotent apply); Uniform Integrity at-most-once |
| Lost datagrams / carrier loss | Idempotent re-send to same Endpoint; bounded retry with jittered backoff; retry-storm prevention |
| Byzantine sender conflicting values | Deterministic merge (LWW/CRDT) is order-independent; signed entries prevent forgery; equivocation detectable via signed prev_hash chain |
| Metadata bomb (huge change batch) | Per-peer batch size caps, max entry count, depth/size budgets before verification |
| State explosion / merge bomb | Expansion-ratio ceiling, delta-size caps, per-peer merge budget, cascade-breaker depth limit |
| Read repair clobbers fresher state | Deterministic symmetric winner (LWW by version, tombstone beats value, CRDT merge); never clobber newer |
| Checkpoint forgery | ed25519-signed checkpoints; verify before resume-from-checkpoint |
| Merkle tree stale after bulk inserts | Rebuild/incremental-update tree on every write; O(log N) rehash per leaf change |
| Clock-skew dependence | Never use wall-clock for validity; versions/positions are logical (OrderingPos, IdsTime) |
| Disallowed crypto | Only ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305; ids-crypto enforces |
| Carrier-agnostic rule violation | Endpoint sole address type; dependency audit bans networking crates; grep test for prohibited symbols |

Critical failure modes: forged updates (signatures), key compromise (bounded revocation + content trust — accepted updates stay valid), metadata bombs (budgets), replay (cache + nonces), amplification (merge guards), clock skew (never trust wall time for validity), state-drift silence (periodic state-root exchange + divergence audit triggers gap reconciliation from signed checkpoints).

### 7. Key Algorithms & Data Structures

**ChangeEntry** = `{ entry_id: BLAKE3(content), version: Version, op: OpType, record_id: RecordId, value: Option<Vec<u8>>, tombstone: bool, prev_version_hash: [u8;32], author: NodeId, sig: Ed25519Signature }`

**Checkpoint** = `{ dataset_id: DatasetId, checkpoint_version: Version, state_root: [u8;32], version_vector: VersionVector, sig: Ed25519Signature }`

**Merkle diff** (top-down):
```
merkle_diff(node_a, node_b):
  if node_a.hash == node_b.hash: return ∅        # identical subtree, prune
  if node_a.is_leaf: return {node_a.range}        # divergent bucket
  return merkle_diff(a.left, b.left) ∪ merkle_diff(a.right, b.right)
```
Cost: O(d · k) hash exchanges for k divergent buckets out of 2^d leaves; O(1) when roots match.

**Anti-entropy repair** (symmetric):
```
repair(bucket_a, bucket_b):
  winner = LWW_by_version(bucket_a, bucket_b)   # tombstone beats value; CRDT merge for concurrent
  apply winner to losing side; re-hash leaf → root
```
Outcome independent of which replica initiates.

**Missing set via DVV:**
```
missing(A_dvv, B_dvv):
  for each (replica, counter) in A_dvv not dominated by B_dvv:
     emit entries with version > B's counter for replica
  symmetric for B_dvv vs A_dvv
```

**Read repair:**
```
read_repair(key, values[(replica, version, digest)]):
  if all digests equal: return
  winner = select_winner(values, consistency_profile)  # LWW / CRDT merge / quorum
  write_back(winner, stale_replicas)
  return winner to client
```

**Retry with absolute deadline:**
```
retry_send(endpoint, datagram, deadline):
  while now() < deadline:
     if send_datagram(endpoint, datagram).ok(): return
     sleep(jittered_backoff(attempt))
  dead_letter_queue.push(endpoint, datagram)
```

### 9. Measurable Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ids-sync` compiles as a standalone crate with no `std::net`, `tokio::net`, libp2p, or any networking dependency
- [ ] All traffic via `ids_carrier::Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>`); source grep confirms zero prohibited symbols
- [ ] Crypto surface limited to ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305 (via `ids-crypto` only)
- [ ] Every canonical type imported from `ids_000_aa::X`, never redefined
- [ ] Implements `ids_000_aa::contracts::Replication` and `trait CRDT` (sealed traits from master)
- [ ] Change entries content-addressed by BLAKE3; duplicates deduped; idempotent apply
- [ ] Merkle diff locates k divergent buckets in O(d · k) hash exchanges (verified in tests)
- [ ] Equal Merkle roots ⇒ converged in O(1) (one hash exchange)
- [ ] Anti-entropy repair produces symmetric outcome independent of initiating replica
- [ ] Read repair never clobbers a fresher version (LWW/tombstone/CRDT winner rules)
- [ ] Checkpoints ed25519-signed; verified before resume-from-checkpoint
- [ ] Retry uses absolute deadlines keyed to entry creation time (no RTT-bound timers)
- [ ] Per-peer replay cache (nonce + monotonic sequence) with TTL-bounded eviction
- [ ] Batch size caps and expansion-ratio ceiling enforced (merge bomb protection)
- [ ] Divergence audit (state-root exchange) detects drift; triggers gap reconciliation from signed checkpoints
- [ ] File structure ≥90 files in subfolders under `ids-sync/src/` (per plan table)
- [ ] Research only: no `.rs` implementation files written, no repository modifications

### 10. Remaining Uncertainties

- Whether `ids-sync` should implement a sealed `trait Sync` in addition to `Replication`/`CRDT`, or whether `Replication` alone covers streams+checkpoints+retries (decided at implementation, contract surface in `ids-000-aa`).
- Exact Merkle tree depth / bucket size defaults (workload-dependent; configurable via `MerkleConfig`, depth 15–16 typical per Cassandra).
- Whether DVV or plain VV is the default summary; DVV needs contiguous-prefix property validation per replica.
- Whether read repair is foreground (blocking) or background (probabilistic) by default — consistency-profile-dependent.
- Checkpoint periodicity and retention bounds (tombstone GC only at causal stability).
- Interaction with `ids-consistency` profiles for read-repair winner selection under bounded staleness / read-your-writes.
- Whether anti-entropy throttle is credit-based or time-window-based (ids-fault integration).

---

### 11. Engineering Decisions Summary

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Separate crate `ids-sync`, not folders in existing crates | CRATES.md entry 18; "try to use separate crates instead of more folders" |
| Four-layer stack: change stream → checkpoint → VV/DVV missing detection → Merkle anti-entropy + read repair | Low-latency common case (incremental) + full-convergence backstop (anti-entropy); read repair heals hot keys opportunistically |
| SEC via join-semilattice merge (commutative, associative, idempotent) | CALM theorem; convergence without coordination; matches carrier-agnostic unknown-membership model |
| Content-addressed entry IDs (BLAKE3) + hash-chained append log | Trivial dedup, tamper-evident history, no central sequencer |
| Merkle trees bucketized by fixed key-range, sha256/blake3 interior | O(d · k) diff vs O(n) full compare; fixed shape lets two replicas compare positionally |
| Symmetric repair (LWW/tombstone/CRDT, outcome independent of initiator) | Never clobber fresher state; no two-way handshake needed |
| ed25519-signed entries + checkpoints; verify before apply | Untrusted peers/carriers can ferry data without being trusted; batch verification via `verify_batch` |
| Absolute deadlines keyed to entry creation time (no RTT) | Correct over arbitrary carrier delay; no TCP/RTT assumptions |
| All crypto via `ids-crypto` only; allowed set enforced | Carrier-agnostic + crypto policy compliance |

### 2. Architecture Overview

`ids-consistency` sits above `ids-000-aa` (types + sealed `trait Consistency` contract + invariants + versioning + errors) and `ids-carrier` (opaque `Endpoint` datagram send/receive). It is layered so each consistency dimension is an independent module:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   APPLICATION / READ-WRITE LAYER (ids-* crates)         │
│  dataset reads/writes · visibility checks · profile selection · ack     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│              Phase 019: ids-consistency (THIS CRATE)                    │
│  ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐   │
│  │ consistency  │ │ committed    │ │ MVCC /       │ │ op-state     │   │
│  │ profiles     │ │ prefix       │ │ versions     │ │ tracking     │   │
│  │ (5 profiles) │ │ tracking     │ │ (visibility) │ │ lifecycle    │   │
│  └──────────────┘ └──────────────┴────────────────┴──────────────┘   │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │ durability-aware ack · read visibility · profile table · prefix │   │
│  │ validator · committed-prefix GC · version store · read manager   │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│             CARRIER BOUNDARY (ids-carrier::Endpoint only)               │
│  send_datagram(Endpoint{CarrierType, Vec<u8>}, &[u8])                   │
│  receive_datagram → (Endpoint, Vec<u8>)                                 │
│  No std::net / tokio::net / libp2p / IP / TCP / UDP / QUIC / HTTP       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Design rules (non-negotiable):**
- One canonical definition per type; canonical types (`NodeId`, `OrderingPos`, `OpRef`, `DatasetId`, `PartitionId`, `RecordId`, `Endpoint`, `CarrierType`, `OpState`, `CommitState`, `ConsistencyProfile`, `FailureDomain`, `DurabilityCondition`) imported from `ids_000_aa::X`, never redefined.
- `ids-consistency` implements the sealed `trait Consistency` from `ids-000-aa/src/contracts/consistency.rs`; downstream crates use it as a trait bound, cannot implement it.
- All message transport is datagram-based via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` (`CarrierType` enum: Loopback, Serial, Optical, Radio, Custom(u16) + opaque `Vec<u8>`). No IP addresses, ports, sockets.
- Crypto surface: ed25519 signatures (authentication of profile changes / prefix updates), sha256/blake3 (version digests, prefix commitments), xchacha20poly1305/chacha20poly1305 (optional payload encryption for version values). All ops in `ids-crypto`; this crate declares only usage boundaries.
- Per-dataset consistency profiles stored in `ids-000-aa::ConsistencyProfileMgr`; this crate orchestrates and enforces them.
- Operation lifecycle reuses `ids-000-aa` `OpState` (`received → ordered → executing → committed → synchronized → verified → failed`) and `CommitState` (`accepted → prepared → committed → aborted`).
- Committed prefix is a monotonic `OrderingPos` watermark per dataset; regressions are rejected (`PositionOutOfOrder`).

---

### 3. Detailed Research Dimensions

#### 3.1 Consistency Profiles (per dataset)

**Strong consistency:** Linearizable reads — every read returns the most recent committed write; real-time ordering preserved between operations. Reads require quorum intersection (r + w > n). No fallback allowed — if the quorum cannot be reached, the read fails rather than serving stale data. Source: Azure Cosmos DB strong consistency (linearizability), Princeton COS 418 consistency models, Cambridge Distributed Systems notes.

**Causal consistency:** Causally-related operations observed by every replica in the same order; concurrent operations may be observed in different orders. Built on happens-before (Lamport): thread-of-execution, reads-from, transitivity. Strongest always-available convergent model; compatible with high availability under partitions. Source: Jepsen causal consistency, Springer Encyclopedia (Shapiro/Tomsic), ACM CSUR survey on causally consistent cloud systems.

**Bounded staleness:** Reads are guaranteed to be within a configured time or version bound of the latest committed write. Reads may be served from local replicas without blocking on the leaseholder, trading staleness for latency and partition availability. Source: Azure Cosmos DB bounded staleness, CockroachDB bounded staleness reads, Google Cloud Spanner TrueTime bounded-staleness reads.

**Eventual consistency:** In the absence of new updates, all replicas eventually converge to the same value. No ordering guarantees beyond convergence; weakest model, highest availability. Source: Dynamo (Cassandra), Jepsen eventual consistency, Shapiro et al. 2011 CRDTs.

**Read-your-writes:** Within a client session, a read always reflects all writes previously performed by that same session. Implemented via session tokens carrying the last-written version; reads are served only by replicas at or beyond that version. Source: Azure Cosmos DB session consistency, Jepsen read-your-writes, Scixa session guarantees, Terry et al. session guarantees.

**Consistency profiles table:** A per-dataset mapping `DatasetId → ConsistencyProfile`, with defaults (Strong), profile change tracking, per-profile capabilities (`requires_quorum`, `allows_fallback`), and version-gated enforcement. Source: IDS `ids-000-aa` `ConsistencyProfile` enum + `ConsistencyProfileMgr`; CRATES.md entry 60 (`ids-consistency-profile`).

#### 3.2 Committed-Prefix Tracking

A monotonic `OrderingPos` watermark per dataset representing the highest position known to be durably committed across the quorum. Every write records its position; the prefix advances only monotonically (regressions rejected with `PositionOutOfOrder`). Reads at positions ≤ committed prefix are visible; positions beyond are withheld until the prefix advances. This gives each dataset a consistent-prefix view: clients observe a valid ordered sequence of writes starting from the first committed update, possibly stale but never out of order. Source: Rialo consistent-prefix guide, Azure Cosmos DB consistent prefix, Jepsen consistent-prefix model, IDS `CommittedPrefixTracker` (update_prefix/get_prefix/advance_prefix).

#### 3.3 Operation-State Tracking

Each operation progresses through `OpState`: `received` (ingress accepted) → `ordered` (assigned an `OrderingPos`) → `executing` (being applied) → `committed` (quorum-acked, durable) → `synchronized` (replicated to required replicas) → `verified` (read-visible / checksum confirmed) → `failed` (terminal error). Parallel commit lifecycle `CommitState`: `accepted → prepared → committed → aborted`. Transitions are guarded by the dataset's consistency profile and durability condition; invalid transitions are rejected. Source: IDS `ids-000-aa` `OpState`/`CommitState` definitions; CRATES.md entry 19.

#### 3.4 Durability-Aware Acknowledgement

An acknowledgement is only meaningful when tied to a durability condition: e.g., `replicated` (quorum commit + local application, no stable-storage barrier) vs `persisted` (quorum commit backed by stable-storage copies + local application). The ack level is chosen per write operation and per dataset profile; strong profiles require `persisted` + quorum, weaker profiles may accept `replicated` or single-replica acks. Source: Apache Iggy cluster durability (VSR quorum commit / persisted prepare history), DynamoDB write completion semantics, Cassandra tunable consistency (R + W > N).

#### 3.5 MVCC Versions and Read Visibility

Multi-version concurrency control: each write creates a new version at an `OrderingPos`; reads specify an `at_position` and return the latest version ≤ that position. Visibility is determined by the consistency profile: Strong/BoundedStaleness/Session/Prefix require `version_position ≤ committed_prefix`; Eventual is always visible. Version conflicts (out-of-order position) are rejected. Source: IDS `ids-000-aa` `MVCCManager`/`VersionStore`/`ReadVisibilityManager` (check_visibility rules at consistency.rs lines 610-642), Dotted Version Vectors causality tracking.

#### 3.6 Causality and Ordering Metadata

Causal consistency requires tracking happens-before dependencies between operations. Vector clocks (one entry per replica) detect exact causality; dotted version vectors compact the representation; hybrid logical clocks (HLC) combine logical causality with physical-time proximity for timestamping. Timestamps from `ids-hlc` (crate 67) optional; `ids-time` (crate 5) `Idstime` tick basis for commit/ordering timestamps. Never raw wall-clock for validity decisions. Source: ACM Queue "Why Logical Clocks are Easy", Kulkarni HLC paper, YugabyteDB HLC, TiKV time blog, IDS `ids-vector-clock`/`ids-hlc`.

#### 3.7 Consistency Hierarchy and Trade-offs

Linearizability (Strong) > Sequential > Causal+ > Causal > Consistent Prefix > Eventual. Stronger models sacrifice availability and latency under partitions (CAP); weaker models improve availability at the cost of stale reads and conflict resolution. Per-dataset profiles let each dataset choose its point on the spectrum. Source: Princeton COS 418 consistency hierarchy, Jepsen consistency models, ACM CSUR CRDT survey, DynamoDB read consistency options.

#### 3.8 Quorum and Replication for Consistency

Read quorum `R`, write quorum `W`, replication factor `N`; consistent reads guaranteed when `R + W > N` (quorum intersection). Majority quorums, flexible quorum intersection (Flexible Paxos: only cross-phase intersection required). Quorum capacity and fault tolerance bounded per dataset. Source: Cassandra tunable consistency (R + W > N), Flexible Paxos (arXiv 1608.06696), quorum intersection theory.

#### 3.9 Fencing Tokens and Write Serialization

Monotonic fencing tokens issued per write epoch prevent stale writers from overwriting newer state after a lease/partition recovery. Each write carries a fencing token; storage rejects writes with tokens below the last seen. Prevents split-brain and stale-write resurrection. Source: Kleppmann DDIA fencing tokens, Hazelcast FencedLock, etcd/ZooKeeper zxid as fencing token, IDS `ids-lease` (crate 24) fencing epochs.

#### 3.10 Chain Replication and Total-Order Commit

Chain replication arranges replicas linearly: writes enter at the head and propagate to the tail; reads served by the tail; linearizable with committed-prefix semantics. Complements (does not replace) consensus-based total order; useful for single-leader datasets. Source: Unseel chain replication, Renesse & Schneider chain replication.

#### 3.11 Raft / Paxos Committed Prefix

Consensus logs advance a committed index / committed prefix; committing entry N implies all entries before N are committed (log matching property). Provides the committed-prefix foundation for strong consistency on top of `ids-broadcast`/`ids-total-order-broadcast`. Source: Ongaro Raft (ATC14), openraft commit-index, university.kurz.fyi Raft commitment, Paxos chosen-value semantics.

#### 3.12 Session Guarantees Formalism

The four client-facing session guarantees — read-your-writes, monotonic reads, monotonic writes, writes-follow-reads — are implemented via per-session version vectors (last-written version + last-read version). Read-your-writes and monotonic reads are incomparable; both are cheaper than full causal consistency. Source: Terry et al. session guarantees, Jepsen read-your-writes/monotonic-reads, Scixa session guarantees, MerceMay session guarantees.

### 4. Threat Model & Mitigations

|| Threat | Mitigation ||
||--------|-----------|-------------|
|| Stale reads under weak profiles | Document per-profile staleness bounds; Strong profile rejects fallback; session tokens enforce read-your-writes ||
|| Profile downgrade / silent weakening | Profile changes are versioned and audited; `EdgeCaseBits` gating; downgrade requires explicit admin action ||
|| Committed-prefix regression | `PositionOutOfOrder` error on non-monotonic prefix updates; prefix advances only forward ||
|| Read visibility violations | `is_read_visible` enforced at every read; version_position ≤ committed_prefix check for Strong/BoundedStaleness/Session/Prefix ||
|| Operation state corruption | Invalid `OpState` transitions rejected; terminal `failed` state requires explicit recovery ||
|| Unacknowledged writes read as committed | Durability-aware ack: read only from positions covered by the required ack level (replicated/persisted) ||
|| Vector clock / causality metadata growth | Pruning / HLC fallback; bounded retention per dataset ||
|| Fencing token reuse / stale writer | Monotonic fencing tokens; storage rejects token ≤ last_seen; tied to lease epochs (`ids-lease`) ||
|| Quorum not reachable (Strong profile) | Read fails rather than serving stale; configurable quorum sizes per dataset; failure-domain-aware quorum ||
|| Carrier-agnostic rule violation (`std::net`, `tokio::net`, IP/TCP/UDP/QUIC/HTTP/DNS/…) | `Endpoint` sole address type; dependency audit bans networking crates; CI greps source for prohibited symbols ||
|| Disallowed crypto algorithm | Only ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305; `ids-crypto` enforces at implementation layer ||
|| Version skew / wire incompatibility | `ProtocolVersion` + `EdgeCaseBits` from ids-000-aa; consistency messages version-tagged; mismatched peers reject before visibility check ||
|| MVCC version store unbounded growth | Bounded version store (default 100k versions); eviction policy; GC at causal stability ||
|| Durability-ack spoofing | Ack level verified against durable storage state; persisted ack requires stable-storage confirmation ||

### 7. Key Algorithms & Data Structures

1. **Per-dataset consistency profile table** — `HashMap<DatasetId, ConsistencyProfile>`; default `Strong`; `set_profile`/`get_profile`; change counting; profile capabilities (`requires_quorum`, `allows_fallback`).

2. **Committed-prefix tracking** — monotonic `OrderingPos` watermark per dataset; `update_prefix` rejects positions below current (`PositionOutOfOrder`); `advance_prefix` on quorum ack; prefix commitment via sha256/blake3 digest over `(dataset_id, position)`.

3. **Strong consistency visibility** — read visible iff `version_position.as_u64() <= committed_prefix.as_u64()`; requires quorum (`requires_quorum == true`); no fallback.

4. **Causal consistency visibility** — causally-related operations ordered via happens-before (vector clock / dotted version vector); concurrent operations unordered; read must observe all dependencies before returning.

5. **Bounded staleness visibility** — read served if within configured time/version bound of committed prefix; may be served from local replica; dynamic timestamp per read (CockroachDB `with_max_staleness` pattern).

6. **Eventual consistency visibility** — always visible (`true`); convergence only, no ordering guarantee; conflicts resolved later.

7. **Read-your-writes visibility** — session token carries last-written version per item; read served only by replica at or beyond that version; session affinity optional routing heuristic.

8. **Operation-state machine** — `received → ordered → executing → committed → synchronized → verified → failed`; transitions guarded by profile + durability; `CommitState`: `accepted → prepared → committed → aborted`.

9. **Durability-aware acknowledgement** — ack level `replicated` (quorum commit + local application) vs `persisted` (quorum commit + stable-storage copies + local application); read only from positions meeting the required ack level.

10. **MVCC version creation** — new version at `OrderingPos` per `(dataset, partition, record)`; reject positions ≤ existing last position (`VersionConflict`); bounded store with eviction.

11. **Read visibility check** — profile-gated: Strong/BoundedStaleness/Session/Prefix → `version_position ≤ committed_prefix`; Eventual → always visible.

12. **Fencing token** — monotonic token per write epoch; storage rejects writes with token ≤ last_seen; tied to `ids-lease` epochs.

13. **Version digest** — sha256/blake3 digest over `(dataset_id, partition_id, record_id, position, value)` for version integrity and committed-prefix commitments.

### 10. Remaining Uncertainties

|| Uncertainty | Impact | Resolution path ||
||-------------|--------|-----------------|
|| Consistency profile granularity | Per-dataset vs per-partition vs per-record profiles | Default per-dataset (per `ConsistencyProfile`); finer granularity deferred ||
|| Committed-prefix advancement trigger | When does prefix advance (quorum ack vs full replication)? | Durability-condition-driven; tuned per profile ||
|| Bounded staleness bound source | Config vs dynamic per-read timestamp | Both supported; dynamic default (CockroachDB pattern) ||
|| Session token transport | How are session tokens passed between client and replicas? | Opaque `Vec<u8>` via `Endpoint`; token format deferred ||
|| MVGC version store eviction policy | Size/age/conflict-based eviction | Bounded store (100k default); LRU + conflict eviction ||
|| Fencing token vs OpState interaction | How fencing tokens integrate with operation lifecycle | Fencing checked at `received → ordered` transition ||
|| Profile downgrade safety | Downgrading Strong → Eventual may expose stale reads | Versioned profile changes + audit; downgrade requires explicit action ||
|| Integration timing with ids-broadcast | Committed positions from broadcast must exist before consistency tracks them | Phases ordered: ordering domain + broadcast before consistency enforcement ||
|| Whether consistency owns quorum or delegates | Crate boundaries | Delegate to ids-quorum (21); this crate consumes quorum results ||
|| GC at causal stability with offline members | Causal-stability GC freezes if a member never acks | Quarantine/grace window; deliberate eviction (cf. plan-077 tombstone GC issue) ||

---

### 11. Engineering Decisions Summary

|| Decision | Rationale ||
||----------|-----------|
|| Separate `ids-consistency` crate (not folders inside existing crates) | Matches user directive "try to use separate crates instead of more folders in existing ones"; enforces single-responsibility boundary ||
|| Five consistency profiles (Strong, Causal, BoundedStaleness, Eventual, ReadYourWrites) | Matches prompts.txt entry 19 contents exactly; covers full consistency spectrum ||
|| Committed-prefix tracking per dataset | Matches prompts.txt entry 19; consistent-prefix reads (stale but ordered) ||
|| Operation-state tracking reusing ids-000-aa OpState | Single canonical definition; `received → ordered → executing → committed → synchronized → verified → failed` ||
|| Durability-aware acknowledgement (replicated vs persisted) | Ack semantics tied to durability condition; strong profiles require `persisted` ||
|| All traffic via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` only | Carrier-agnostic absolute rule (CRATES.md, prompts.txt entry 19) ||
|| Allowed crypto: ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305 | IDS policy; `ids-crypto` implements, this crate declares usage boundaries ||
|| Sealed `trait Consistency` from ids-000-aa | Downstream crates use as trait bound; cannot implement; single canonical contract ||
|| Per-dataset profiles (not per-record) | Matches `ConsistencyProfile` enum scope in `ids-000-aa/types.rs`; simpler enforcement ||
|| Quorum delegated to ids-quorum (21) | Quorum intersection is a separate concern (CRATES.md entry 21) ||
|| No code in this phase | Research only per prompts.txt entry 19 ||

### 12. Sources

1. Linearizability / strong consistency — Cambridge Distributed Systems notes (cl.cam.ac.uk/teaching/2526/ConcDisSys) — every operation takes effect atomically between invocation and response; "up-to-date" reads.
2. Princeton COS 418 Consistency Models (cs.princeton.edu) — linearizability vs sequential vs causal vs eventual hierarchy; RAFT provides linearizability.
3. Jepsen Causal Consistency (jepsen.io/consistency/models/causal) — causally-related operations in same order; concurrent operations unordered; sticky availability.
4. Jepsen Read Your Writes (jepsen.io/consistency/models/read-your-writes) — a process's subsequent read observes its own write; sticky available.
5. Jepsen Monotonic Reads (jepsen.io/consistency/models/monotonic-reads) — reads cannot go backwards within a process; totally available.

# PHASE 020:

## Phase 020 — Create the ids-broadcast crate (reliable/causal/total order/atomic broadcast): Research Findings & Implementation Blueprint

**Research complete (30 targeted searches executed). No code written, no files created, no repository changes made. This document is the blueprint for implementation.**

---

### 1. Executive Summary

Phase 020 creates `ids-broadcast`, the IDS crate for message ordering guarantees across replicas. It implements the broadcast hierarchy: **reliable broadcast → FIFO broadcast → causal broadcast → total order broadcast (atomic broadcast) → FIFO-total order broadcast**, plus state machine replication (SMR) on top, and the four atomic broadcast properties **uniform agreement, uniform integrity, validity, termination**.

Crate: `ids-broadcast` (CRATES.md entry 20). Purpose: message ordering guarantees across replicas. Contents per prompts.txt entry 20: reliable broadcast, FIFO broadcast, causal broadcast, total order broadcast (atomic broadcast), FIFO-total order broadcast, state machine replication, uniform agreement, uniform integrity, validity, termination.

Verbatim prompt (C:/idfs/prompts.txt lines 295-309): "Phase 020 — Create the ids-broadcast crate: Message ordering guarantees across replicas."

Research basis: 30 parallel searches returned Bracha's reliable broadcast (1987, validity/agreement/integrity), FIFO broadcast (per-sender sequence ordering), causal broadcast (happens-before, vector clocks), total order = atomic broadcast (Hadzilacos & Toueg 1994: validity, uniform agreement, uniform integrity, uniform total order), Paxos made simple (Lamport), Zab (ZooKeeper total order broadcast), Raft (replicated log SMR), Viewstamped Replication (Oki & Liskov), PBFT (Castro & Liskov, 3f+1, pre-prepare/prepare/commit), Dolev-Strong authenticated broadcast (signature chains, t+1 rounds, PKI), HotStuff (view-by-view recipe, optimistic responsiveness), Flexible Paxos (cross-phase quorum intersection only), Totem (fault-tolerant totally ordered multicast), Lamport logical clocks, vector clocks (causality detection), hybrid logical clock (HLC), gossip/epidemic broadcast (HyParView, eventual reliability), SRM reliable multicast, atomic multicast vs atomic broadcast taxonomy, Chandra-Toueg failure detectors (consensus reducible to atomic broadcast), Fast Paxos (2-message-delay learning), EPaxos (leaderless dependency graph), causal atomic broadcast, delta-CRDT anti-entropy.

A skeleton `ids-broadcast` crate does NOT yet exist at `C:/idfs/ids-broadcast/`. `ids-000-aa` already declares `trait Broadcast` (reliable/causal/total order/atomic) at `src/contracts/broadcast.rs`; `ids-broadcast` implements it. Carrier-agnostic absolute rule: no `std::net`, `tokio::net`, libp2p, IP, TCP, UDP, QUIC, HTTP, DNS, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular, VPN, or mesh. All traffic via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>`, max 1024 bytes). Allowed crypto only: ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305 (implemented in `ids-crypto`; `ids-broadcast` consumes type-level surface and primitive IDs only). `ids-000-aa` is the master crate with all canonical types and sealed trait contracts. Research only — no code, no source modifications, only this plan document.

### 2. Architecture Overview

`ids-broadcast` sits above `ids-000-aa` (types + sealed `trait Broadcast` contract + invariants + versioning + errors) and `ids-carrier` (opaque `Endpoint` datagram send/receive). It is layered so each ordering guarantee is an independent module that can be composed:
