Carrier-agnostic constraint enforced structurally: the `src/` tree has no transport modules and no `std::net`/`tokio::net` references; every outbound message is typed as `Vec<u8>` addressed to `ids-carrier::Endpoint`.

### 7. Key Algorithms & Data Structures

**`DurabilityPolicy[dataset_id]`** (per dataset): `{ local_tier: PersistenceTier, quorum: {n, w}, regional: {r, R}, cross_region: CrossRegionMode, ack_level: AckLevel, ack_basis: AckBasis, sync_required: bool, wtimeout: Duration }`. Evaluated per write.

**Persistence tier evaluation:** `durable(local_tier)` → `MemoryOnly` (no barrier) | `Journaled` (WAL appended) | `Synced` (fsync/fdatasync + parent-dir sync crossed) | `SyncedAndReplicated` (synced + quorum). Exposure window reported per tier.

**Quorum arithmetic:** write quorum `w` and read quorum `r` valid iff `w + r > n` and `2w > n`; tolerates `⌊(n−1)/2⌋` replica failures; quorum reports exclude non-electable/dead replicas.

**Regional check:** `regionally_durable` iff `synced_regions ≥ r` across `R` regions with failure-domain anti-affinity satisfied (no two required copies in the same AZ/failure domain).

**Commit vs sync separator:** `Commit` (write accepted + ordered) and `Sync` (stable-storage barrier reached) computed independently; `verdict = Satisfied` iff commit ∧ sync (per policy); `Unsatisfied` iff commit ∧ ¬sync and timeout elapsed; `Undetermined` otherwise.

**Content-addressed durability manifest:** blake3/sha256 hash over durable metadata + payload per shard/copy; corrupted or substituted copy detected at verification (spacedb-durability manifest pattern).

**Allowed crypto:** ed25519 (durable-record signatures), xchacha20poly1305/chacha20poly1305 (AEAD for durable payloads at rest), sha256/blake3 (content hashing, manifest integrity). No other primitives.

**Sealed traits:** any extension trait (e.g., `DurabilityEvaluator`) sealed via `private::Sealed` supertrait so only this crate implements it (Rust API Guidelines C-SEALED).

### 9. Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Criterion | Target | Measurement |
|-----------|--------|-------------|
| Local persistence tier | `Synced` survives single-node power loss; `MemoryOnly` does not | crash/power-loss fault-injection test per tier |
| fsync/fdatasync barrier | fsync + parent-directory sync before ack for new dataset files | unit test + fsync-failure injection (writer poisoned on fsync failure) |
| Quorum arithmetic | `w + r > n` and `2w > n` enforced; tolerates ⌊(n−1)/2⌋ failures | property test over n/w/r combinations |
| Quorum ack verdict | `Satisfied` only when `w` replicas durably persisted | replica-tracker unit test with dead/unelectable replica exclusion |
| Regional threshold | `r` of `R` regions synced, failure-domain anti-affinity satisfied | region-report unit test; reject same-AZ placement |
| Cross-region | async replication lag bound exposed per dataset | RPO benchmark (lag ≤ configured bound) |
| Commit vs sync | commit and sync boundaries independently configurable; verdict `Satisfied` iff both met | boundary-separator unit test; `Undetermined` when committed-not-synced |
| Acknowledgement levels | Unacknowledged / Leader / Quorum / All with `AckBasis::{Memory, Journal, StableStorage}` | unit test per level; `wtimeout` converts block to `Unsatisfied` |
| Content integrity | blake3/sha256 over durable metadata + payload; corruption detected | manifest verification unit test (tampered shard rejected) |
| Crypto constraint | only ed25519/xchacha20poly1305/sha256/blake3/chacha20poly1305 | dependency/cargo audit + primitive-ID allowlist test |
| Carrier-agnostic | compiles with zero `std::net`/`tokio::net`/libp2p references; all traffic via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` | build lint + dependency scan |
| Property tests | 100,000+ iterations | proptest/bolero |
| Chaos tests | partition, offline member, replica churn | pass/fail |

---

### 10. Remaining Uncertainties

1. **Quorum size vs. availability trade-off per dataset:** `w = quorum` maximizes durability but blocks on minority failure; `w = n` (all) maximizes durability but zero fault tolerance for availability. Per-dataset policy must be product-configured, not research-determined.
2. **Cross-region replication lag bound:** acceptable RPO per dataset is workload-dependent; unquantified until deployment targets exist.
3. **fsync failure handling:** a failed fsync poisons the writer (durability crate); recovery path (restart from WAL vs. fail the dataset) needs an operator decision.
4. **Wire format for durability signals:** CBOR vs bincode vs protobuf for the opaque `Vec<u8>` handed to `ids-carrier::Endpoint`; CBOR favored for compactness/schema evolution but crate TBD.
5. **Tombstone / WAL reclamation:** durable WAL growth unbounded without checkpoint-compaction; retention policy (size/age/ack-based) deferred.
6. **Formal verification scope:** TLA+/PlusCal spec proving quorum + commit/sync separation correctness is additional effort beyond this plan.

---

### 11. Engineering Decisions Summary

| Decision | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|
| New separate crate `ids-durability-policy` | Follows "separate crates instead of more folders in existing ones"; clean dependency boundary |
| Commit vs. sync as separate boundaries | Oracle Berkeley DB model: durability = acknowledgment guarantees + synchronization guarantees; prevents overclaiming |
| `Synced` tier default for durable datasets | fsync/fdatasync barrier before ack survives power loss (durability crate, quipu-log SyncPolicy `Always`/`EveryN`) |
| Parent-directory fsync after file creation | New-file durability trap (kernel internals; PostgreSQL/LevelDB practice) |
| blake3 preferred, sha256 allowed | content hashing/manifest integrity (spacedb-durability pattern); within allowed-crypto set |
| ed25519 signatures for durable records | non-repudiation of durability verdicts; within allowed-crypto set |
| Quorum `w + r > n`, `2w > n` | intersecting write quorums prevent divergent committed state (Apache Iggy quorum rules, Cassandra consistency) |
| Failure-domain anti-affinity for regional threshold | region copies in one AZ defeat regional redundancy (spacedb-durability placement; Cloud Storage/Azure AZ semantics) |
| Bounded `wtimeout`; `Undetermined` verdict | prevents indefinite quorum block (MongoDB wtimeout; Iggy immediate-failure when insufficient sites) |
| All traffic via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` | carrier-agnostic mandate; no `std::net`/`tokio::net`/libp2p |
| Research only — no code, no source modifications | per task constraint; this document is the implementation blueprint |

### 1. Executive Summary

Phase 059 creates `ids-redundancy-mode`, the IDS crate that owns per-dataset redundancy method selection: full replication vs erasure coding, hybrid coexistence of both modes, dataset-specific redundancy objectives, H-unit-aware redundancy, and replica/fragment placement across failure domains. `ids-redundancy-mode` is a pure decision-and-placement layer: it does not encode, decode, move, or store data itself — it selects the redundancy mode per dataset, determines how many replicas or (k, m) fragments to place, picks failure-domain-diverse placement targets, and exposes the redundancy plan to `ids-distribution`, `ids-replication`, `ids-recovery`, and `ids-placement` for execution. All traffic it influences rides as opaque `Vec<u8>` datagrams over `ids-carrier::Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>`); the crate itself never imports a network stack.

Redundancy mode is a per-dataset property, not a global constant. Hot/performance-sensitive datasets use full replication (3 copies typical) for fast local reads and trivial single-copy rebuild. Cold/capacity-sensitive datasets use systematic Reed-Solomon erasure coding (e.g., RS(10,4), RS(6,3)) for 1.33×–1.5× storage overhead vs 3× for triple replication, tolerating any m fragment losses per stripe, at the cost of k-fragment read amplification on rebuild and read-modify-write on small writes. Hybrid redundancy lets both modes coexist in one dataset (hot shards replicated, cold shards erasure-coded), and H-unit-aware redundancy constrains placement so no two copies share an H-unit, rack, power circuit, or network switch.

`ids-redundancy-mode` does NOT yet exist at `C:/idfs/ids-redundancy-mode/`. `ids-000-aa` already declares canonical types referenced by this crate but never redefined: `NodeId`, `RegionId`, `HUnitId`, `DatasetId`, `PartitionId`, `RecordId`, `CarrierType`, `RedundancyMode`, `Checksum`, plus sealed trait contracts (`Placement`, `Replication`, `Erasure`, `Durability`, `Topology`, `FaultTolerance`) and error types. `ids-000-aa` is the master crate holding every canonical type and sealed trait contract. Research only — no code, no source modifications, only this plan document.

Research basis: 30 parallel searches returned Reed-Solomon systematic (k+m) erasure coding over GF(2^8) with any-k-of-n reconstruction (MDS property); ISA-L Cauchy/Vandermonde generator matrices and `reed_solomon_erasure` Rust crate (GF(2^8)/0x11d); RAID 1 mirroring vs RAID 5/6 trade-offs (storage 2x vs 1.33×–1.5×, rebuild from one copy vs k fragments); HDFS rack-aware replica placement (local rack + remote rack, 2-rack spread); Ceph CRUSH failure domains (host/rack/row/room/datacenter, at most one slice per domain); Cassandra NetworkTopologyStrategy (per-DC replica counts, rack-aware placement); Dynamo N/R/W quorum replication with consistent hashing; Amazon S3 11-nines durability across 3+ AZs with erasure coding; Facebook f4 warm storage reducing effective replication factor from 3.6 to 2.8/2.1 via RS; Microsoft Azure WAS LRC (local reconstruction codes) reducing repair reads from k to r ≪ k; pyramid codes trading MDS distance for locality; regenerating codes minimizing repair bandwidth; locally repairable codes (LRC) minimizing helper-node count; EVENODD/RDP/Liberation XOR-based RAID-6 codes; comparison papers showing erasure coding wins for cold data, replication wins for hot data; hybrid replication→erasure-coding transitioning (ELECT/F4 pattern: replicate hot, EC cold, transition offline); bitrot detection via per-shard checksum sidecars; MTTDL data-loss probability for k-of-n codes under node failure/repair distributions.

### 2. Architecture Overview

`ids-redundancy-mode` sits above `ids-000-aa` (types + sealed contracts + invariants + errors), `ids-carrier` (opaque `Endpoint` datagram transport), and `ids-crypto` (allowed primitives for integrity). It is a decision-and-placement layer: it never touches payload bytes, never encodes/decodes, never opens a socket, and never imports `std::net`, `tokio::net`, libp2p, or any transport. It consumes dataset identity, topology state, policy version, resource measurements, and operation context; it emits a redundancy plan (mode, replica/fragment count, placement targets, reconstruction threshold, verification requirements) consumed by `ids-distribution`, `ids-replication`, `ids-recovery`, and `ids-placement`.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    APPLICATION / ids-* LAYER (redundancy consumers)          │
│  ids-distribution, ids-replication, ids-recovery, ids-placement — apply plan │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│              Phase 059: ids-redundancy-mode (THIS CRATE — decision/placement)│
│  ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌───────────┐ │ │
│  │ mode selection  │ │ dataset policy  │ │ placement engine│ │ H-unit    │ │ │
│  │ (full vs EC vs  │ │ (per-dataset    │ │ (failure-domain │ │ aware     │ │ │
│  │  hybrid)        │ │  objectives)    │ │  diversity)     │ │ redundancy│ │ │
│  └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └───────────┘ │ │
│  ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌───────────┐ │ │
│  │ replica/fragment│ │ EC (k,m) config │ │ integrity plan  │ │ contracts │ │ │
│  │  count planner  │ │ (parity shards, │ │ (checksums,     │ │ + invariants│ │ │
│  │                 │ │  stripe width)  │ │  sidecars)      │ │           │ │ │
│  └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └───────────┘ │ │
│  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │
│  │  audit/logging (every decision signed+chained, sha256/blake3 chain)   │ │ │
│  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                                         │ opaque Vec<u8> datagrams
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────▼────────────────────┐
│              CARRIER BOUNDARY: ids-carrier::Endpoint only                   │
│  send_datagram(Endpoint{CarrierType≤1024B addr, Vec<u8>}, payload: &[u8])  │
│  receive_datagram → (Endpoint, Vec<u8>)                                     │
│  No std::net / tokio::net / libp2p / IP / TCP / UDP / QUIC / HTTP / DNS    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Data flow of a redundancy decision:** `ids-distribution` (or `ids-placement`) submits a dataset identity + policy intent → `ids-redundancy-mode` evaluates dataset-specific redundancy objectives against topology state, capacity, failure-domain diversity, and H-unit membership → emits `RedundancyPlan{mode, replica_count|ec_k_m, placement_targets[], threshold, verification}` → consumer crate executes placement/copy/encode over `ids-carrier::Endpoint` datagrams → `ids-redundancy-mode` records the decision in the append-only, hash-chained audit log.

**Redundancy modes:**
- **Full replication mode:** N complete copies of the dataset (or partition), each on a distinct failure domain. Any single copy serves reads; loss of N−1 copies tolerable; rebuild = copy one surviving replica. Storage overhead N×. Best for hot, read-heavy, low-latency datasets.
- **Erasure coding mode:** systematic Reed-Solomon (k, m): data split into k equal fragments, m parity fragments computed over GF(2^8), n=k+m fragments stored across distinct failure domains; any k of n reconstruct. Storage overhead (k+m)/k. Best for cold, capacity-sensitive datasets; rebuild reads k fragments (k× bandwidth vs replication's 1×).
- **Hybrid redundancy:** full replication + erasure coding coexist per dataset (per-shard or per-partition mode selection). Hot shards replicated, cold shards erasure-coded; transitions between modes online (replication→EC encoding after data cools; EC→replication on hotness increase).
- **Dataset-specific redundancy:** each dataset declares its own objective (durability target, read latency, storage budget, failure tolerance); `ids-redundancy-mode` evaluates each policy independently, never forcing one global config.
- **H-unit-aware redundancy:** placement constrained so copies/fragments of one dataset never share an H-unit (and optionally rack, power, network, operator domain); H-unit failure compensated by another eligible H-unit when capacity and policy permit.

-----

### 3. Detailed Research Dimensions

#### 3.1 Full Replication Mode

Full replication stores N complete, independent copies of the data (or partition), each on a distinct node/H-unit/region. Reads can be served from any replica; writes fan out to all N copies (or a write quorum W of N with read quorum R, R+W>N for consistency per Dynamo quorum technique). Tolerates loss of any N−1 copies without data loss. Rebuild after a failure copies one surviving replica — minimal bandwidth (one object's worth) and no computation.

Research-verified characteristics:
- **Storage overhead:** N× (3× for triple replication, the HDFS/Cassandra default).
- **Read performance:** excellent — any replica can serve, read load balances across copies, locality-aware reads preferred (HDFS reads from same-rack replica first).
- **Write performance:** write must reach W replicas before acknowledgment; write amplification N× (or W× with quorum); small writes are cheap (no read-modify-write parity update).
- **Rebuild:** cheapest of all redundancy methods — copy c bytes from any one surviving replica to the replacement node.
- **Consistency:** replica divergence handled by read repair, anti-entropy, hinted handoff, version vectors (Dynamo pattern); last-write-wins or vector-clock conflict resolution.

Best fit: hot datasets, low-latency reads, small objects, workloads where storage is cheap relative to performance. IDS-A §37 (hybrid redundancy) and `hybrid_redundancy.rs` in `ids-000-aa/src/invariants/` reference full replication + erasure coding coexisting per dataset.

#### 3.2 Erasure Coding Mode

Systematic Reed-Solomon (k, m) erasure coding: data object partitioned into k equal data fragments; m parity fragments computed over GF(2^8) via a Cauchy or Vandermonde generator matrix; n=k+m fragments stored across distinct failure domains. Any k of n fragments reconstruct the original (MDS property). Storage overhead (k+m)/k — e.g., RS(10,4) = 1.4× overhead vs 3× for triple replication, tolerating any 4 fragment losses per stripe. RS(6,3) = 1.5×. RS(4,2) = 1.5×.

Research-verified characteristics:
- **Storage overhead:** (k+m)/k — 40–50% for typical configs vs 200% for triple replication.
- **Fault tolerance:** tolerates any m fragment losses per stripe (data or parity).
- **Read performance:** full reads need all k data fragments (or any k of n); degraded reads of a missing fragment require reconstruction from k others — k× bandwidth vs replication's 1×.
- **Write performance:** small writes incur read-modify-write or reconstruct-write penalty (read existing fragments, recompute parity, write back) — write amplification up to k+1×; stripe-sized writes avoid RMW.
- **Rebuild:** reconstructs lost fragment from k surviving fragments — k× bandwidth and GF(2^8) computation vs replication's 1× copy.
- **Integrity risk:** parity shards are cold (never read on normal serving) — silent bitrot in parity poisons reconstruction; requires per-fragment checksum sidecars + scrubbing (SeaweedFS EC bitrot detection pattern).

RS over GF(2^8): addition = XOR, multiplication via log/antilog tables; generator matrix rows 0..k identity (systematic), rows k..k+m from Cauchy/Vandermonde so any k×k submatrix is invertible. Rust crates: `reed_solomon_erasure` (GF(2^8)/0x11d, klauspost/Backblaze-compatible), `rusty_erasure` (ISA-L-compatible pure Rust), `sia_reed_solomon` (AVX2/GFNI/NEON). ISA-L `gf_gen_cauchy1_matrix` / `gf_gen_rs_matrix` produce invertible Cauchy matrices.

EVENODD/RDP/Liberation XOR-based RAID-6 codes (m=2) avoid GF arithmetic entirely (XOR + cyclic shifts) — optimal XOR count, prime-number disk constraints. Regenerating codes (MSR/MBR) minimize repair bandwidth; LRC/pyramid codes minimize helper nodes (locality r ≪ k) for single-fragment repair. Azure WAS uses LRC; Facebook f4 uses RS for warm blobs.

Best fit: cold/capacity-sensitive datasets, large objects, storage-constrained environments, workloads tolerant of higher rebuild/read amplification.

#### 3.3 Hybrid Redundancy

Hybrid redundancy lets full replication and erasure coding coexist within the same dataset — different shards, partitions, or temperature zones use different modes. Microsoft Azure pattern: objects enter replicated (hot), later erasure-coded and replicas deleted as they cool. Facebook f4: warm blobs use EC to cut effective replication factor from 3.6 to 2.8/2.1 while tolerating disk, host, rack, and datacenter failures. USENIX FAST'24 ELECT: LSM-tree KV store with hotness-aware redundancy transitioning — hot KV pairs replicated, cold SSTables erasure-coded, cold data offloaded to a cold tier; 56.1% less hot-tier storage than pure replication with similar normal read/write performance.

Research-verified considerations:
- **Transitioning:** replication→EC requires encoding all replicas then deleting extras (encoding-aware replication placement avoids cross-rack downloads during encoding — CMU HDFS paper); EC→replication requires decoding then copying.
- **Granularity:** per-object, per-shard, per-partition, or per-SSTable mode selection; metadata tracks each unit's mode and placement.
- **Temperature tracking:** access-frequency/recency scoring decides hot vs cold; hysteresis avoids mode-flapping.
- **Consistency during transition:** both copies must be valid and verifiable before the old mode's copies are retired; checksum sidecars validate before delete.

Best fit: datasets with mixed access patterns (hot head, long cold tail), tiered storage (hot/warm/cold), capacity-plus-performance requirements.

#### 3.4 Dataset-Specific Redundancy

Each dataset declares its own redundancy objective: durability target (nines), read-latency SLO, storage budget, maximum tolerated failures, failure-domain scope (node/H-unit/rack/region). `ids-redundancy-mode` evaluates each policy independently — no global forced configuration. IDS CAPABILITIES §41/§42/§43 define hybrid redundancy, dataset-specific redundancy, and H-unit-aware redundancy as explicit system responsibilities; CRATES.md entry 59 defines ids-redundancy-mode contents as "Full replication mode, erasure coding mode, hybrid redundancy, dataset-specific redundancy, H-unit-aware redundancy, replica/fragment placement across failure domains."

Per-dataset policy fields: `mode ∈ {FullReplication, ErasureCoding, Hybrid}`, `replica_count` or `(k, m)`, `required_failure_domains`, `min_redundancy_state`, `recovery_requirements`, `verification_requirements`, `temperature_threshold` (for hybrid), `allowed_regions`, `allowed_hunits`.

#### 3.5 H-Unit-Aware Redundancy

H-units are intermediate operational groups of storage nodes inside a regional database cluster (IDS CAPABILITIES §34, IDS-A §36). H-unit-aware redundancy constrains replica/fragment placement so copies of one dataset never share an H-unit — an H-unit failure loses at most one copy/fragment per dataset. Compensation: another eligible H-unit assumes serving/storage/reconstruction if capacity, redundancy, and policy permit (IDS-A §36, `hunit_compensation.rs` invariant).

Placement constraints extend recursively: H-unit → rack → power circuit → network switch → region (topological failure domains). `topology_diversity.rs` invariant: different locations, H-units, regions, failure domains per copy. CRUSH-style placement (Ceph): at most one slice per failure domain; failure domain = bucket type (host/rack/row/room/datacenter). HDFS rack-aware: with RF=3, one replica local rack, one remote rack, third different node in remote rack (2-rack spread); BlockPlacementPolicyRackFaultTolerant places on 3 different racks.

Best fit: any redundancy mode where correlated failure (whole H-unit lost) must not cause data loss or extended unavailability.

#### 3.6 Replica/Fragment Placement Across Failure Domains

Placement selects target nodes/H-units/regions for each replica or fragment. Key algorithms:
- **Consistent hashing (with virtual nodes):** maps partition/fragment ID to node ring position; only k/n keys remap on node add/remove (Cassandra vnodes, Dynamo, Karger et al.). Improves load distribution; vnodes handle heterogeneity (weighted by capacity).
- **Rack/failure-domain awareness:** place copies on distinct failure domains at the configured level (H-unit, rack, region). HDFS: local rack + remote rack; Ceph CRUSH: at most one slice per failure domain.
- **Capacity-aware:** track usable/reserved capacity per node/H-unit/region; avoid assignments exceeding declared capacity with safety margins (`ids-000-aa/src/placement/capacity_tracker.rs`).
- **Topology-aware:** prefer nearest replica for reads (near-to-far routing, region affinity); fallback to next-closest eligible replica on failure (`read_fallback.rs` invariant).

Placement outputs a `PlacementPlan{targets: Vec<(FragmentIndex, NodeId/HUnitId/RegionId)>, failure_domains: Vec<DomainId>}` consumed by `ids-placement` and `ids-distribution` for actual datagram shipping over `ids-carrier::Endpoint`.

### 4. Threat Model & Mitigations

|| Threat | Asset at risk | Mitigation (this crate) ||
|--------|-----------|----------------|--------------------------|
| Correlated failure wipes all copies (same H-unit/rack/power) | Durability | H-unit-aware placement: at most one copy/fragment per failure domain; topology diversity invariant |
| Silent bitrot in cold parity shards poisons reconstruction | Integrity | Per-fragment checksum sidecars (sha256/blake3), scrub before rebuild, RS arbitration of corrupt shards |
| Erasure-coded rebuild reads k fragments (k× bandwidth, latency) | Availability/performance | Prefer local fragments for degraded reads; LRC/pyramid locality for single-fragment repair; schedule rebuild off-peak |
| Small-write penalty on erasure-coded data (read-modify-write) | Performance | Stripe-sized writes avoid RMW; hybrid mode keeps hot data replicated |
| Replica divergence under concurrent writes | Consistency | Version vectors + quorum (R+W>N); conflict policy per dataset (last-writer-wins / MV-register) |
| Placement overcommits capacity (node/H-unit full) | Availability | Capacity-aware placement with reserved recovery headroom; rejection before commit |
| Mode transition leaves data under-protected mid-transition | Durability | Both modes valid + checksum-verified before retiring old copies; atomic plan commit |
| H-unit failure exceeds compensation capacity | Durability | H-unit compensation via eligible peer H-unit; degradation mode documented; regional fallback |
| Carrier duplicates/delays/reorders placement datagrams | Correctness | Idempotent placement application; sequence numbers; carrier-agnostic boundary (opaque Endpoint) |

The carrier is never trusted: placement decisions are signed over payload bytes, surviving re-framing by any carrier; no network stack is in the trust base.

### 7. Key Algorithms & Data Structures

#### 7.1 Redundancy Mode Selection

```
select_mode(dataset, policy, topology, capacity) -> RedundancyMode
  if policy.hot && capacity.permits(replica_count): FullReplication
  if policy.cold && capacity.permits(ec_overhead): ErasureCoding
  if policy.mixed: Hybrid (per-shard/partition mode by temperature)
  else: policy.default (FullReplication for latency-critical, ErasureCoding for capacity-critical)
```

#### 7.2 Full Replication Plan

```
ReplicaPlan { replica_count: u32, targets: Vec<NodeId>, failure_domains: Vec<DomainId>, quorum: (R, W) }
read: any replica; prefer local failure domain (near-to-far)
write: fan out to W of N; ack on W (R+W>N for consistency)
rebuild: copy c bytes from one surviving replica
storage overhead: N×
tolerates: any N−1 copy losses
```

#### 7.3 Erasure Coding Plan (systematic Reed-Solomon over GF(2^8))

```
EcPlan { k: u32, m: u32, n=k+m, stripe_size: u64, fragment_size: u64, targets: Vec<NodeId>, failure_domains: Vec<DomainId> }
encode: data[k fragments] × G[(k+m)×k] → n fragments (first k = data verbatim, last m = parity)
decode: any k of n fragments → solve linear system over GF(2^8) → reconstruct
GF(2^8): addition = XOR; multiplication via log/antilog tables (0x11d primitive polynomial)
generator: Cauchy or Vandermonde; any k×k submatrix invertible (MDS)
storage overhead: (k+m)/k
tolerates: any m fragment losses per stripe
rebuild: reconstruct lost fragment from k fragments (k× bandwidth, GF compute)
integrity: per-fragment sha256/blake3 checksum sidecar; scrub before rebuild
```

Typical configs: RS(10,4) = 1.4× overhead, any 4 losses; RS(6,3) = 1.5×; RS(4,2) = 1.5×; RS(3,2) = 1.67×. k+m ≤ 255 (GF(2^8) field size).

#### 7.4 Hybrid Redundancy Plan

```
HybridPlan { shards: Vec<(ShardId, Mode, Plan)>, temperature_threshold, transition_policy }
hot shards: FullReplication(N=3)
cold shards: ErasureCoding(RS(10,4))
transition: replicate→EC after cool period; EC→replicate on heat increase; both modes verified before switch
```

#### 7.5 Dataset-Specific Redundancy Policy

```
DatasetPolicy { dataset_id, mode, replica_count | (k,m), required_failure_domains, min_redundancy_state, recovery_requirements, verification_requirements, temperature_threshold, allowed_regions, allowed_hunits }
evaluated per-dataset; no global forced config
```

#### 7.6 H-Unit-Aware Placement

```
place(dataset_plan, topology) -> PlacementPlan
  group nodes by H-unit → rack → region → power/network domain
  select targets so each copy/fragment lands in a distinct failure domain at configured level
  if H-unit fails: compensation via eligible peer H-unit (capacity + redundancy + policy)
  topology diversity: no two copies share H-unit/rack/power/switch/region unless policy allows
```

Placement algorithms: consistent hashing with virtual nodes (baseline distribution), rack/fault-domain-aware selection (constrain to distinct domains), capacity-aware filtering (usable ≥ reserved + safety margin), near-to-far read preference.

### 9. Measurable Acceptance Criteria

|| Criterion | Target | Measurement ||
|-----------|----------|-------------|--------------|
| Per-dataset mode selection | full replication / erasure coding / hybrid chosen per dataset policy | unit test per dataset class |
| Full replication tolerance | tolerates any N−1 replica losses; rebuild = 1× object copy | unit test + fault-injection test |
| Erasure coding (k,m) | any k of n=k+m fragments reconstruct; tolerates any m losses | unit test (matrix invertibility), RS(10,4)/RS(6,3) configs |
| Storage overhead | replication N× vs EC (k+m)/k; EC ≤ 1.5× for typical cold configs | calculation/test |
| H-unit-aware placement | no two copies/fragments of one dataset share an H-unit | placement test with synthetic topology |
| Failure-domain diversity | copies spread across distinct H-unit/rack/region per policy | placement test |
| Dataset-specific policy | each dataset evaluated independently; no global forced config | unit test (multiple datasets, different modes) |
| Hybrid coexistence | hot shards replicated, cold shards EC within one dataset | unit test (shard-level mode map) |
| Mode transition atomicity | old and new copies both valid+checksummed before switch | transition test |
| Checksum sidecars | per-fragment sha256/blake3 checksum; scrub detects bitrot before rebuild | unit test |
| Carrier agnosticism | zero references to `std::net`/`tokio::net`/IP/TCP/UDP/QUIC/HTTP/DNS; all traffic via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` | grep/audit |
| Crypto allowlist | only ed25519, sha256, blake3 (xchacha20poly1305/chacha20poly1305 if encryption needed) | dependency audit |
| Signed decisions | every redundancy decision recorded in append-only, hash-chained, ed25519-signed audit log | audit-log test |
| Placement capacity | never assigns beyond node/H-unit declared capacity + safety margin | capacity test |
| Rebuild bandwidth | EC rebuild reads k fragments vs replication 1×; documented ratio | bench/calculation |

### 10. Remaining Uncertainties

1. **Erasure-code parametrization per dataset class:** which (k,m) defaults for hot/warm/cold datasets (RS(10,4) vs RS(6,3) vs RS(4,2)) — product decision, not research conclusion.
2. **Hybrid transition granularity:** per-object, per-shard, per-partition, or per-SSTable; affects metadata size and transition complexity.
3. **Temperature tracking:** access-frequency/recency scoring algorithm and hysteresis thresholds to prevent mode-flapping — workload-dependent.
4. **H-unit compensation eligibility:** what makes an H-unit "eligible" (capacity headroom, redundancy state, policy) — intersects with `ids-recovery` and `ids-placement` integration.
5. **Checksum sidecar storage:** where sidecars live (per-volume, per-fragment, separate crate) and scrub cadence — overlaps `ids-integrity` / `ids-security`.
6. **Quorum vs N for full replication:** whether writes require all N or W<N with read-quorum consistency (R+W>N) — consistency profile interacts with `ids-consistency-profile` (Phase 060).
7. **Erasure-code math crate selection:** `reed_solomon_erasure` vs `rusty_erasure` vs `sia_reed_solomon` lives in `ids-erasure`, but this crate's `(k,m)` advice must match the chosen crate's GF(2^8) matrix format — defer to `ids-erasure` phase.
8. **Failure-domain level granularity:** H-unit vs rack vs region vs power/switch — policy-driven, deployment-specific.

### 11. Engineering Decisions Summary

|| Decision | Rationale ||
|----------|-----------|-------------|
| Separate crate `ids-redundancy-mode` | "Separate crates instead of more folders" directive; clean decision/placement boundary |
| Decision/placement only — no encode/decode | Keeps crate small, carrier-agnostic, no GF(2^8) math dependency; `ids-erasure` handles codec |
| Per-dataset redundancy mode (not global) | Matches IDS CAPABILITIES §41/§42/§43 and CRATES.md entry 59 contents |
| Systematic Reed-Solomon over GF(2^8) for EC | MDS property (any k of n), widely implemented (ISA-L, klauspost, rust crates), Cauchy/Vandermonde invertible matrices |
| Full replication = N copies, EC = (k+m)/k overhead | Established RAID/storage fact: 3× vs 1.33×–1.5× |
| H-unit-aware placement with at most one copy per failure domain | IDS-A §36 hunit_compensation; `correlated_failure`, `topology_diversity`, `hunit_compensation` invariants |
| Hybrid hot-replicated / cold-EC | Azure f4 / ELECT FAST'24 pattern: replication for hot, EC for cold; 56.1% storage savings |
| Checksum sidecars + scrub before rebuild | SeaweedFS EC bitrot detection: cold parity shards rot silently and poison RS reconstruction |
| Carrier-agnostic via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` only | Absolute IDS rule; no network stack in trust base |
| Crypto limited to ed25519/sha256/blake3 | IDS allowed-crypto list; signed plans + checksum sidecars |

### 1. Executive Summary

Phase 060 creates `ids-consistency-profile`, the IDS crate that defines read/write behavior per consistency profile. It owns profile registration, read quorum (R), write quorum (W), durability profile assignment, consistency-model enforcement per profile, failure behavior per profile, read-only degraded operation, and causal consistency tracking — all carrier-agnostic. `ids-consistency-profile` does not open sockets or drive any transport directly; it evaluates whether a read or write satisfies a profile's quorum/durability requirements, issues acknowledgment decisions, tracks causal ordering via dotted version vectors, and ships every protection-relevant message as opaque `Vec<u8>` datagrams to `ids-carrier::Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>`).

Profiles defined:

| Profile | Read behavior | Write behavior | Guarantee |
|---------|---------------|----------------|-----------|
| Local acknowledged | Read from local replica only (R=1) | Write acknowledged on local replica only (W=1) | Weakest; lowest latency, highest staleness risk |
| Quorum durable | Read from quorum (R where R+W>N) | Write to quorum (W where R+W>N) | Strong: reads see latest write |
| Regionally durable | Read quorum within region | Write quorum within region; async replicate cross-region | Strong within region, eventual cross-region |
| Cross-region durable | Read quorum across regions | Write quorum across regions (EACH_QUORUM-style) | Strong across regions; highest latency |
| Eventually replicated | Read any single replica (R=1) | Write any single replica + hinted handoff (W=1) | Eventual; anti-entropy converges |
| Read-only degraded | Read from any available replica | Writes rejected (read-only) | Availability during partitions |
| Causally consistent | Read with causal context (DVV/dotted VV) | Write with causal dependency vector | Causal order preserved; no linearizability |

Carrier-agnostic absolute rule: no `std::net`, `tokio::net`, libp2p, IP, TCP, UDP, QUIC, HTTP, DNS, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular, VPN, or mesh. All traffic via `ids-carrier::Endpoint`. Allowed crypto only: ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305 (implemented in `ids-crypto`; `ids-consistency-profile` consumes type surface and primitive IDs from `ids-000-aa`/`ids-crypto` only).

A skeleton `ids-consistency-profile` crate does NOT yet exist at `C:/idfs/ids-consistency-profile/`. `ids-000-aa` already declares canonical types referenced by this crate but never redefined: `NodeId`, `RegionId`, `IdsTime`, `CarrierType`, `RecordId`, `Checksum`, plus sealed trait contracts and error types. `ids-000-aa` is the master crate holding every canonical type and sealed trait contract. Research only — no code, no source modifications, only this plan document.

Research basis: 30 parallel searches returned Dynamo quorum R+W>N mechanics (Cassandra docs, Stanford CS145, UMD, MIT 6.033, arXiv 2002.06098); causal consistency model (Wikipedia causal consistency); sequential vs linearizable consistency (Attiya SPAA'91, MIT 6.824, Princeton COS418/518); CAP theorem and PACELC (Abadi PACELC paper, Wikipedia PACELC); CRDT state-based/op-based and LWW/MV-register conflict resolution (arXiv 1805.06358, arXiv 2504.05398, arxiv.org/html/1603.01529 delta-CRDTs, Shapiro et al.); dotted version vectors / efficient causality tracking (ACM DL 10.1145/2332432.2332497); Dynamo-style sloppy quorum, hinted handoff, read repair, anti-entropy (Cassandra docs, Dynamo paper); anti-entropy digests and gossip reconciliation (systemoverflow anti-entropy digests); MongoDB read concern / write concern and causal consistency (MongoDB docs v5.0); CockroachDB follower reads, bounded/exact staleness (CockroachDB docs); Spanner TrueTime external consistency (Google Cloud docs); ed25519 Rust crate (ed25519-dalek docs.rs); xchacha20poly1305/chacha20poly1305 Rust crate (chacha20poly1305 docs.rs); sha256/blake3 Rust crates (sha2, blake3 docs.rs and BLAKE3-team README).

### 2. Architecture Overview

`ids-consistency-profile` sits above `ids-000-aa` (types + sealed contracts + invariants + errors), `ids-carrier` (opaque `Endpoint` datagram transport), and `ids-crypto` (allowed primitives). It is a policy/evaluation layer: given a read or write request tagged with a profile and a replica set, it decides (a) whether the operation may proceed, (b) how many replicas must acknowledge (W) / respond (R), (c) whether durability requirements are met, (d) what causal metadata to attach, and (e) what failure behavior applies. It never sends bytes itself; it returns an `AckDecision` / `ReadDecision` that the caller frames into opaque `Vec<u8>` datagrams to `ids-carrier::Endpoint`.

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    APPLICATION / ids-* LAYER (profile users)                 │
│  ids-store, ids-replication, ids-fragment — read/write with profile tag      │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│               Phase 060: ids-consistency-profile (THIS CRATE — policy)      │
│  ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────┐ │ │\n│  │ profile         │ │ quorum          │ │ durability      │ │ failure  │ │ │\n│  │ registry        │ │ evaluation (R+W│ │ evaluation      │ │ behavior │ │ │\n│  │ (7 profiles)    │ │  >N, locality)  │ │ (local/region/  │ │ (reject/ │ │ │\n│  └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ │  cross-region)  │ │ degrade) │ │ │\n│  ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ └─────────────────┘ └──────────┘ │ │\n│  │ causal          │ │ read-only       │ │                 │                │ │ │\n│  │ tracking (DVV)  │ │ degraded mode   │ │                 │                │ │ │\n│  └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ │                 │                │ │\n│  ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ │                 │                │ │ │\n│  │ ack/read        │ │ audit/logging   │ │                 │                │ │ │\n│  │ decision types  │ │ (signed+chained)│ │                 │                │ │ │\n│  └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ │                 │                │ │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────┴──────────────┘\n                                          │ opaque Vec<u8> datagrams\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────▼──────────────────┐\n│              CARRIER BOUNDARY: ids-carrier::Endpoint only  │\n│  send_datagram(Endpoint{CarrierType≤1024B addr, Vec<u8>},  │\n│  payload: &[u8])                                           │\n│  receive_datagram → (Endpoint, Vec<u8>)                    │\n│  No std::net / tokio::net / libp2p / IP / TCP / UDP /      │\n│  QUIC / HTTP / DNS / Wi-Fi / Bluetooth / cellular / VPN    │\n└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Data flow of a profile-tagged write:** client submits `Write{record_id, payload, profile, causal_ctx}` → `ids-consistency-profile` evaluates the profile: computes required W, durability scope (local/region/cross-region), checks replica availability, returns `WriteAck{required_w, acked_replicas, durability_met, causal_dot, ack_or_reject}` → caller sends the write as opaque datagram(s) to `ids-carrier::Endpoint` targets and collects acks → profile re-evaluates ack count against W → returns `WriteResult{committed, durable, causal_context}`.

**Data flow of a profile-tagged read:** client submits `Read{record_id, profile, causal_ctx}` → profile evaluates required R, read scope, staleness tolerance → returns `ReadDecision{required_r, read_replicas, max_staleness, causal_gate}` → caller fetches from replicas via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` → profile merges responses, applies causal gate (reject if causal dependencies unmet), returns `ReadResult{value, version, causal_context, staleness}`.

**Profile semantics (research-verified):**

- **Local acknowledged** (W=1, R=1): write acked on first local replica; read from local replica. No quorum overlap — stale reads possible. Lowest latency, lowest durability.
- **Quorum durable** (W + R > N): strict quorum. Write waits for W acks; read gathers R responses and returns newest by version. Quorum intersection guarantees reads see the latest write (Dynamo/Cassandra model).
- **Regionally durable**: write quorum within the region (W_local), async geo-replication to other regions. Read quorum within region. Strong within region; eventual cross-region.
- **Cross-region durable** (EACH_QUORUM-style): write quorum must be reached in every region; read quorum across regions. Strong cross-region; highest latency (WAN).
- **Eventually replicated** (W=1, R=1, W+R≤N): write to one replica + hinted handoff / anti-entropy gossip. Read any replica. Converges eventually; anti-entropy digests (Merkle-tree or version-vector based) heal divergence.
- **Read-only degraded**: writes rejected; reads served from any available replica. Used during partitions to preserve availability (CAP: choose A over C).
- **Causally consistent**: writes attach a dotted version vector (DVV) causal dependency; reads gate on causal context — a read returns only after its causal past is satisfied (read-your-writes, monotonic reads, writes-follow-reads). No linearizability; available under partition.

**Crypto used:** ed25519 for signing ack/read decisions and audit checkpoints; sha256/blake3 for profile IDs, version-vector hashing, audit-chain links; xchacha20poly1305/chacha20poly1305 to encrypt profile state at rest when confidentiality required.

### 3. Detailed Research Dimensions

Each dimension maps to one or more of the 30 targeted searches executed. Sources are cited inline with the source list in Section 13.

#### 3.1 Quorum replication: R + W > N (Dynamo/Cassandra model)

**Source:** Apache Cassandra Dynamo architecture docs (cassandra.apache.org); Stanford CS145 Consistency in Replicas; UMD Distributed Systems quorum notes; MIT 6.033 Quorum Consensus note; arXiv 2002.06098 Consistency Analysis of Replication-Based Probabilistic Key-Value Stores; thecodeforge.io Quorum R+W>N; medium.com/double-pointer Replication R+W>N.

Given N replicas, a write succeeds when W replicas ack; a read succeeds when R replicas respond. If R + W > N, every read quorum intersects every write quorum in at least one node (minimum overlap = W + R − N), so a read always contacts at least one replica that holds the latest write — strong consistency. If R + W ≤ N, quorums may be disjoint → stale reads possible → eventual consistency. Tuning extremes: W = N, R = 1 (fast reads, writes blocked by any single failure); W = 1, R = N (fast writes, reads need all nodes). Dynamo recommends N=3, W=2, R=2. `ids-consistency-profile` implements the `QuorumDurable` profile with strict quorum (R + W > N) and the `EventuallyReplicated` profile with partial quorum (R + W ≤ N) plus anti-entropy.

#### 3.2 Local acknowledged profile (W=1, R=1)

**Source:** Dynamo-style quorum analysis; thecodeforge.io write quorum spectrum (W=1 = single acknowledgment, fastest writes, data on one node only, suitable for logs/metrics/regenerable data).

`LocalAcknowledged`: write acked by the first local replica only; read served from the local replica only. No cross-replica coordination. Lowest latency, no quorum overlap guarantee — stale reads and lost writes possible on replica failure. Intended for ephemeral/cache-tier data where latency dominates durability.

#### 3.3 Regionally durable profile

**Source:** AWS DynamoDB Global Tables (multi-Region strong vs eventual modes); Cassandra LOCAL_QUORUM / EACH_QUORUM consistency levels; PACELC theorem (Abadi).

Write quorum reached within a single region (W_local replicas in-region); async replication to other regions. Read quorum within region. Strong consistency within region; eventual consistency cross-region (replication lag bounded by anti-entropy interval). Fits PACELC: elsewhere (no partition) choose latency (local reads/writes) with eventual cross-region; during partition choose availability within region.

#### 3.4 Cross-region durable profile (EACH_QUORUM-style)

**Source:** Cassandra EACH_QUORUM consistency level (majority of replicas in each datacenter); AWS DynamoDB Global Tables multi-Region strong consistency (RPO zero); Spanner TrueTime external consistency.

Write must reach a quorum in every region before ack; read gathers from quorums across regions and returns newest. Strong consistency across regions; highest latency (WAN round trips); tolerates single-region failure without losing consistency. Most expensive profile; used for control-plane / configuration data.

#### 3.5 Eventually replicated profile

**Source:** Dynamo sloppy quorum + hinted handoff (cs.cornell.edu Dynamo paper, cs.cornell.edu/cs5414); Cassandra ANY consistency level + hinted replay; anti-entropy digests and gossip reconciliation (systemoverflow anti-entropy digests); CRDT delta-state (arXiv 1603.01529); eventually consistent register (arXiv 1511.05010).

Write to one replica (W=1); coordinator stores a hint and replays later; anti-entropy gossip periodically reconciles divergent replicas via digest exchange (version vectors or Merkle hashes) and transfers only missing/conflicting entries. Read any replica (R=1); may return stale until convergence. CRDT merge (commutative, associative, idempotent) ensures all replicas converge to the same state given the same update set. `ids-consistency-profile` defines the merge/audit interface; `ids-replication` performs the actual gossip transport via `ids-carrier::Endpoint`.

#### 3.6 Read-only degraded profile

**Source:** CAP theorem (blogs.bmc.com CAP theorem: during partition choose C or A); CockroachDB follower reads / stale reads (docs.cockroachlabs.com); PACELC (during partition P choose A or C).

During a partition or when write quorum cannot be reached, the crate switches affected records to `ReadOnlyDegraded`: writes are rejected with `WriteRejected` error; reads served from any available replica (possibly stale). Preserves availability (CAP A) at the cost of consistency. Rejoining the partition triggers anti-entropy reconciliation to converge.

#### 3.7 Causally consistent profile

**Source:** Wikipedia Causal Consistency (available under partition; asynchronous; stronger than eventual, weaker than sequential/linearizable); MongoDB Causal Consistency and Read/Write Concerns (majority read + majority write = all four guarantees: read-own-writes, monotonic reads, monotonic writes, writes-follow-reads); dotted version vectors / efficient causality tracking (ACM DL 10.1145/2332432.2332497); version vectors / vector clocks.

Writes attach a causal dependency vector (dotted version vector): `(node_id, counter)` dot plus version-vector causal past. A read carries its observed causal context; the profile gates read delivery until the causal past is satisfied (replica has applied all dependencies). Guarantees read-your-writes, monotonic reads, monotonic writes, writes-follow-reads without linearizability; available under partition. DVV enables compact causality tracking (compare dots instead of full VVs).

#### 3.8 Sequential vs linearizable consistency

**Source:** Attiya SPAA'91 (sequential vs linearizable); MIT 6.824 linearizability notes; Princeton COS418/518 strong consistency lectures; geeksforgeeks strong vs eventual consistency.

Linearizability = strong consistency: once a write completes, all later reads (by real-time order) return that write or a later one; operations appear instantaneous at a single point between invocation and completion. Sequential consistency: all nodes agree on a single order of operations, but real-time order need not be preserved. `ids-consistency-profile` does NOT implement linearizability (requires consensus/leader + quorum read, e.g. Raft read_index); its strongest profile is `QuorumDurable` (strong read-your-writes via quorum intersection) plus `CrossRegionDurable` (strong across regions). Causal consistency is weaker than both.

#### 3.9 CAP theorem and PACELC

**Source:** CAP theorem (blogs.bmc.com); PACELC design principle (Wikipedia PACELC; Abadi PACELC paper cs.umd.edu).

CAP: under network partition P, choose between Consistency C and Availability A — not both. PACELC extends: elsewhere (E, no partition) choose between Latency L and Consistency C. `ids-consistency-profile` encodes this explicitly: `QuorumDurable`/`CrossRegionDurable` choose C (sacrifice A under partition); `EventuallyReplicated`/`ReadOnlyDegraded` choose A (sacrifice C); `RegionallyDurable` chooses C within region, A cross-region; `LocalAcknowledged` chooses A (lowest latency, weakest C). PACELC "elsewhere" latency vs consistency maps to profile selection: low-latency profiles (`LocalAcknowledged`, `EventuallyReplicated`) vs high-latency strong profiles (`CrossRegionDurable`).

#### 3.10 Failure behavior per profile

**Source:** Dynamo/Riak sloppy quorum and hinted handoff; Cassandra consistency levels (ONE/TWO/THREE/QUORUM/ALL/LOCAL_QUORUM/EACH_QUORUM/ANY/LOCAL_ONE); quorum availability analysis (W + R > N failure tolerance: writes tolerate N−W failures, reads tolerate N−R failures); deepengineering.net staleness SLOs for Dynamo-style stores.

Each profile defines failure behavior:
- `LocalAcknowledged`: write fails if local replica down; read fails if local replica down. No redundancy.
- `QuorumDurable`: write succeeds iff ≥ W replicas available; read succeeds iff ≥ R replicas available. Tolerates N−W write failures / N−R read failures. Below quorum → operation rejected (choose C over A).
- `RegionallyDurable`: write succeeds iff ≥ W_local replicas available in region; cross-region lag tolerated. Region failure → fall back to `EventuallyReplicated` or `ReadOnlyDegraded` for that region's data.
- `CrossRegionDurable`: write succeeds iff quorum reached in every region. Any single region down → writes blocked (strong C).
- `EventuallyReplicated`: write succeeds on any single replica; hint stored for later. Always available for writes (W=1). Reads always available (R=1) but possibly stale.
- `ReadOnlyDegraded`: writes always rejected; reads always available from any replica.
- `CausallyConsistent`: write succeeds if causal deps can be recorded; read blocks (bounded wait) until causal past satisfied or times out → `CausalTimeout` failure.

Failure behavior is recorded in the append-only audit log (sha256/blake3 chain + ed25519-signed checkpoints).

#### 3.11 Allowed crypto only (ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305)

**Source:** ed25519-dalek docs.rs (ed25519 key gen/sign/verify, RFC 8032 EdDSA over Curve25519); chacha20poly1305 docs.rs (ChaCha20Poly1305 RFC 8439 AEAD + XChaCha20Poly1305 extended 192-bit nonce); sha2 RustCrypto (SHA-256); blake3 BLAKE3-team README (256-bit output, SIMD, keyed hash, KDF, XOF).

`ids-consistency-profile` uses:
- ed25519: signing ack/read decisions and audit checkpoints (proof of profile evaluation).
- sha256: profile ID derivation, version-vector entry hashing, audit-chain links.
- blake3: fast content hashing for anti-entropy digests, causal-context hashing, checkpoint chaining (preferred for speed/parallelism).
- xchacha20poly1305: encrypt profile state at rest (bounded replay windows, causal histories) with 24-byte nonce safe for random generation.
- chacha20poly1305: encrypt session/state payloads with 12-byte nonce (counter-based, bounded use).

No other crypto. `ids-crypto` exposes primitive IDs; `ids-consistency-profile` references them via `ids-000-aa` only.

---

### Threat Model

|| Threat | Asset at risk | Mitigation (this crate) ||
|--------|-----------|-------------------------------|--------------------------|
| Stale read below quorum (R + W ≤ N) | Read correctness | `QuorumDurable`/`CrossRegionDurable` enforce R + W > N; `EventuallyReplicated` documents staleness bound via anti-entropy SLO |
| Lost write (W=1 replica fails) | Write durability | `LocalAcknowledged` documents risk; `QuorumDurable` requires W ≥ 2 for N ≥ 3; `CrossRegionDurable` requires quorum per region |
| Split-brain / divergent replicas | State convergence | Anti-entropy digest reconciliation (version vectors/Merkle) in `ids-replication`; CRDT merge is commutative/associative/idempotent |
| Causal dependency violation | Causal consistency | DVV gating: read blocks until causal past satisfied; `CausalTimeout` on violation |
| Partition-induced inconsistency | CAP tradeoff | `ReadOnlyDegraded` chooses availability; `QuorumDurable` chooses consistency (rejects writes below quorum) |
| Replay of ack/read decisions | Decision integrity | ed25519-signed audit checkpoints; nonce-bound decisions; bounded replay cache per profile |
| Clock manipulation for causal order | Causality correctness | Logical clocks (DVV dots/counters), never wall-clock; monotonic `IdsTime` only for timeouts |
| Carrier duplicating/delaying datagrams | Replay/ordering | Carrier-agnostic: replay protection at profile layer; idempotent merge tolerates duplicates |
| Profile downgrade attack | Consistency integrity | Profile is immutable per record/region; downgrade requires signed governance decision, audited |
| Key extraction (profile signing key) | Decision authenticity | Signing keys never leave node; encrypted at rest (xchacha20poly1305/chacha20poly1305); zeroized on shutdown |
| Audit log tampering | Accountability | sha256/blake3 hash chain + periodic ed25519-signed checkpoints; offline verifiable |

The carrier is never trusted: profile decisions and audit entries are signed over bytes, surviving any carrier re-framing; the carrier-agnostic boundary (opaque `Endpoint`, `CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>`) means no network stack is in the trust base.

| `ids-000-aa` | Master crate: canonical types + sealed trait contracts + invariants + errors | `NodeId`, `RegionId`, `IdsTime`, `CarrierType`, `RecordId`, `Checksum`, `Error` — consumed, never redefined; sealed trait contracts mirrored |

### Key Algorithms & Data Structures

- **ProfileId / Profile**: `ProfileId` = BLAKE3-256 of profile name + region set; `Profile` enum {LocalAcknowledged, QuorumDurable, RegionallyDurable, CrossRegionDurable, EventuallyReplicated, ReadOnlyDegraded, CausallyConsistent} with associated `QuorumConfig{R, W, N, scope}`.
- **Quorum evaluation**: `admit_write(N, W, available) -> bool` iff `available ≥ W`; `admit_read(N, R, available) -> bool` iff `available ≥ R`; `strong_consistent(R, W, N)` iff `R + W > N`; `min_overlap(R, W, N) = W + R − N`.
- **Durability evaluation**: `Local` → local replica only; `Region` → quorum within region; `CrossRegion` → quorum in every region (EACH_QUORUM).
- **Causal context (DVV)**: dotted version vector `((node_id, counter), version_vector)`; `a < b` iff `dot_a.counter ≤ vv_b[dot_a.node]`; concurrent iff neither precedes. Read gate: deliver read only when `causal_past ⊆ applied`.
- **Ack decision**: `WriteAck{required_w, acked: BitSet<NodeId>, durable: bool, causal_dot, decision: Ack|Reject|Degrade}`; `ReadDecision{required_r, responses: Vec<(Endpoint, Value, Version)>, causal_gate, decision: Deliver|Wait|Reject}`.
- **Failure behavior**: per-profile matrix — reject below quorum (QuorumDurable/CrossRegionDurable), degrade to read-only (ReadOnlyDegraded), always-available with hints (EventuallyReplicated), local-only (LocalAcknowledged), bounded causal wait (CausallyConsistent).
- **Anti-entropy digest**: compact state summary (version vector or Merkle tree hash) exchanged peer-to-peer; mismatched digests trigger reconciliation of missing/conflicting entries via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` datagrams.
- **Audit chain**: each profile decision (admit/reject/degrade/deliver/wait) = SHA-256/BLAKE3-chained entry + ed25519-signed checkpoint; offline verifiable.

- `ids-000-aa` — canonical types (`NodeId`, `RegionId`, `IdsTime`, `CarrierType`, `RecordId`, `Checksum`, `Error`) and sealed trait contracts.
- `ids-carrier` — `Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>`) and `Carrier` trait — decision transport only; crate never sends directly.
- `ids-crypto` — allowed primitives only: ed25519, xchacha20poly1305, sha256, blake3, chacha20poly1305.
- `serde` — serialization of profile envelopes, quorum decisions, audit entries.
No `std::net`, `tokio::net`, libp2p, or any networking stack. No crypto beyond the allowed list.

---

### Measurable Acceptance Criteria

1. Profile registration: all 7 profiles register uniquely; `ProfileId` collision-free (BLAKE3-256).
2. Quorum durable: `R + W > N` enforced; 100% of reads after a committed quorum write return the latest value (quorum overlap ≥ 1).
3. Local acknowledged: `W=1, R=1`; write acked on first local replica; read from local replica; stale reads possible (documented).
4. Regionally durable: write quorum within region; async cross-region replication; strong within region, eventual cross-region.
5. Cross-region durable: quorum reached in every region before write ack; single-region failure blocks writes (strong C).
6. Eventually replicated: `W=1, R=1`; anti-entropy converges all replicas to same state given same update set (CRDT merge properties: commutative, associative, idempotent).
7. Read-only degraded: writes rejected 100%; reads served from any available replica during partition.
8. Causally consistent: DVV gating; read-your-writes, monotonic reads, monotonic writes, writes-follow-reads all hold; no linearizability (documented).
9. Failure behavior: write succeeds iff ≥ W available; read succeeds iff ≥ R available; below quorum → rejected (QuorumDurable/CrossRegionDurable) or degraded (ReadOnlyDegraded).
10. All traffic via `ids-carrier::Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>`); zero references to `std::net`/`tokio::net`/IP/TCP/UDP/QUIC/HTTP/DNS/Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/cellular/VPN/mesh in the crate.
11. Only ed25519/xchacha20poly1305/sha256/blake3/chacha20poly1305 in the crate's crypto surface.
12. Every profile decision recorded in append-only, hash-chained, ed25519-signed audit log with `NodeId` + `IdsTime`.

---

### Remaining Uncertainties

- **Quorum defaults per profile:** concrete `(N, R, W)` defaults for each profile (e.g. N=3, W=2, R=2 for QuorumDurable) are deployment-tuned; to be validated at integration with `ids-store`/`ids-replication`.
- **Anti-entropy interval and digest size:** gossip period and Merkle/vector digest tuning affect convergence speed vs bandwidth; workload-dependent.
- **Causal wait timeout:** bounded wait for causal past satisfaction; timeout value trades consistency vs availability under partition.
- **Cross-region latency budget:** `CrossRegionDurable` WAN round trips may exceed acceptable latency for some workloads; SLO definition pending.
- **Interaction with `ids-immutable` (Phase 040):** profile write admission must respect holds/retention; exact guard handshake defined here, validated at integration.
- **Interaction with `ids-session` (Phase 050):** session-bound profile tags and audit cross-referencing to be validated at integration.
- **Read repair vs anti-entropy:** whether read path performs read-repair (fetch newest, push to stale replicas) in addition to background anti-entropy; design decision pending.

---

### Engineering Decisions Summary

| Decision | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|
| Separate crate `ids-consistency-profile` (not a folder inside an existing crate) | Follows "separate crates instead of more folders" directive; clear policy boundary |
| Profile enum with associated `QuorumConfig{R, W, N, scope}` | Single data structure captures all seven profiles; R/W/N tuning explicit |
| Strongest profile = QuorumDurable (R + W > N), not linearizability | Linearizability needs consensus/leader (Raft read_index) — out of scope; quorum intersection gives read-your-writes without consensus |
| CausallyConsistent via dotted version vectors (DVV) | Compact causality tracking; available under partition; read-your-writes + monotonic guarantees |
| EventuallyReplicated = partial quorum (W=1, R=1) + anti-entropy gossip + CRDT merge | Dynamo sloppy quorum/hinted handoff pattern; convergence without coordination |
| ReadOnlyDegraded rejects writes, serves reads | CAP: choose availability during partition |
| Audit: sha256/blake3 hash chain + ed25519-signed checkpoints | Offline-verifiable decision log; tamper evidence |
| Logical clocks only (DVV dots/counters + monotonic IdsTime); no wall-clock for causality | Clock manipulation cannot break causal order |
| Carrier-agnostic boundary via `ids-carrier::Endpoint`; crate returns decisions, never sends bytes | Preserves IDS architecture; no network stack in trust base |
| Only allowed crypto; `ids-crypto` exposes primitive IDs via `ids-000-aa` | Complies with allowed-crypto rule |

### 1. Executive Summary

Phase 061 creates `ids-routing-table`, the IDS crate responsible for routing table construction and maintenance. It is a **separate crate** (not a folder inside an existing crate, per the project rule of separate crates for new capabilities), organized into subfolders by routing concern: route entries, next-hop resolution, path selection, locality metrics, replica freshness tracking, loop prevention, route expiration/revalidation, and routing convergence. `ids-routing-table` does not open sockets or drive any transport directly; it constructs, indexes, and maintains routing tables as pure data structures and policy functions, and returns every forwarding decision as opaque `Vec<u8>` datagrams addressed to `ids-carrier::Endpoint` (`CarrierType` + `Vec<u8>` ≤ 1024 bytes). The crate never touches `std::net`, `tokio::net`, libp2p, IP, TCP, UDP, QUIC, HTTP, DNS, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular, VPN, or mesh.

Routing table contents (per prompts.txt entry 61):

| Concern | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Routing table entries | Destination → next-hop/Endpoint entries with cost, metric, source, age, and state |
| Next-hop resolution | Given a destination, resolve the next-hop Endpoint and outgoing path |
| Path selection | Choose among candidate next-hops using cost, locality, freshness, ECMP groups |
| Locality metrics | Prefer local/region/rack replicas over remote (proximity-aware selection) |
| Replica freshness tracking | Track last-known-good/version per replica; prefer fresher replicas |
| Loop prevention | Split horizon / poison reverse / path-vector loop detection on table construction |
| Route expiration/revalidation | TTL per entry; stale entries revalidated or garbage-collected |
| Routing convergence | Detect topology change, recompute affected paths, converge to loop-free state |

A skeleton `ids-routing-table` crate does NOT yet exist at `C:/idfs/ids-routing-table/`. `ids-000-aa` already declares canonical types referenced by this crate but never redefined: `NodeId`, `RegionId`, `Endpoint`, `CarrierType`, `RecordId`, `Checksum`, `IdsTime`, `OpState`, plus sealed trait contracts and error types. `ids-000-aa` is the master crate holding every canonical type and sealed trait contract. Research only — no code, no source modifications, only this plan document.

Research basis: 30 parallel searches returned distributed construction of near-optimal routing schemes (Elkin & Neiman 2016, CONGEST-model routing tables with stretch guarantees), Kademlia DHT routing tables with XOR metric and k-buckets (libp2p docs), Chord DHT finger tables and successor lists (MIT TON Chord paper), distance-vector distributed Bellman-Ford (Stanford CS168 textbook) with route advertisement, next-hop + cost forwarding entries, split horizon and poison reverse loop prevention (CS168, INET RIP tutorial, RFC 2453 RIPv2), route expiration timers and garbage collection (INET RIP timeout/garbage-collection), routing convergence vs count-to-infinity (link state converges fast; distance vector suffers bad-news-travels-slowly), locality-aware routing for large-scale networks (Berkeley OceanStore locality paper), replica freshness / view divergence of freshness in replicated databases (SSRN freshness survey; Skybridge bounded staleness USENIX OSDI'25), BGP best-path selection algorithm (Cisco: weight, local preference, local origin, AS path, origin, MED, eBGP over iBGP, IGP metric, router ID), path-vector protocol loop detection via AS path (Wikipedia path vector; APNIC BGP basics; UCSD interdomain routing lecture), longest prefix match (DPDK LPM6 library; multi-bit trie), ECMP equal-cost multi-path load sharing (Palo Alto, Cumulus, Cisco, Huawei), BGP route flap damping (Juniper), loop-free alternate fast reroute (Cisco ASR 9000 LFA FRR), consistent hashing and rendezvous/highest random weight hashing (Ably blog; Wikipedia rendezvous hashing), on-demand MANET routing AODV/DSR route discovery and maintenance (INET MANET showcase), anycast closest-replica selection (OASIS anycast paper), reverse path forwarding loop prevention (Cisco community), gossip/sloppy management of structured P2P routing tables (HOTAC'08 sloppy management paper), distance vector vs link state vs path vector comparison (Princeton COS461; Auckland CS314), link-state SPF/Dijkstra routing table generation (Springer OSPF chapter; Pearson Routing Protocols Companion Guide; Nokia OSPF guide), RFC 9815 BGP-LS SPF routing (RIB/LSDB/SPF calculation), BGP route summarization and hierarchical aggregation (flylib summarizing outbound routing), routing table partitioning/sharding for scalable lookups (IEEE routing table partitioning SPAL; Tarantool vshard routing table bucket→replica set mapping), dead route detection and unreachable route garbage collection, carrier-agnostic opaque datagram addressing (IDS carrier-agnostic socket abstraction research), Rust Kademlia routing table implementation (mainline routing_table.rs k-buckets, MAX_BUCKET_SIZE_K=20), segment routing / source routing (RFC 8402 segment routing architecture;
